children.text: Chapter 1
asty uttarasyāṃ diśi devatātmā himālayo nāma nagādhirājaḥ
children.translated_text: In the northern quarter there is a divine-souled lord of mountains named <s>Himālaya</s>,

children.text: pūrvāparau toyanidhī vigāhya sthitaḥ pṛthivyā iva mānadaṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: standing as if the measuring rod of the earth, plunging into the eastern and western oceans.

children.text: yaṃ sarvaśailāḥ parikalpya vatsaṃ merau sthite dogdhari dohadakṣe
children.translated_text: All the mountains, having made him the calf while <s>Meru</s> stood as the skilled milker for what was desired,

children.text: bhāsvanti ratnāni mahauṣadhīś ca pṛthūpadiṣṭāṃ duduhur dharitrīm ||
children.translated_text: milked from the earth, as instructed by <s>Pṛthu</s>, shining jewels and great medicinal herbs.

children.text: anantaratnaprabhavasya yasya himaṃ na saubhāgyavilopi jātam
children.translated_text: Of him, the source of endless jewels, snow did not become a destroyer of beauty;

children.text: eko hi doṣo guṇasaṃnipāte nimajjatīndoḥ kiraṇeṣv ivāṅkaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for a single fault sinks amid a mass of virtues, like the spot on the moon amid its rays.

children.text: yaś cāpsarovibhramamaṇḍanānāṃ sampādayitrīṃ śikharair bibharti
children.translated_text: And with his peaks he bears mineral-rich slopes, which prepare the adornments for the playful movements of apsarases,

children.text: balāhakacchedavibhaktarāgām akālasaṃdhyām iva dhātumattām ||
children.translated_text: like an untimely twilight whose redness is divided by breaks in the clouds.

children.text: āmekhalaṃ saṃcaratāṃ ghanānāṃ chāyām adhaḥsānugatāṃ niṣevya
children.translated_text: After enjoying below the shadow, following along the lower slopes, of clouds moving up to the girdle-region of the mountain,

children.text: udvejitā vṛṣṭibhir āśrayante śṛṅgāṇi yasyātapavanti siddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the siddhas, distressed by rains, take shelter on his sun-warmed summits.

children.text: padaṃ tuṣārasrutidhautaraktaṃ yasminn adṛṣṭvāpi hatadvipānām
children.translated_text: On him, even without seeing the tracks of elephants slain, red and washed by streams of snow,

children.text: vidanti mārgaṃ nakharandhramuktair muktāphalaiḥ kesariṇāṃ kirātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Kirātas</s> know the path of the lions by pearls released from the hollows of their claws.

children.text: nyastākṣarā dhāturasena yatra bhūrjatvacaḥ kuñjarabinduśoṇāḥ
children.translated_text: There, birch-barks marked with letters in mineral pigment and reddened by drops from elephants,

children.text: vrajanti vidyādharasundarīṇām anaṅgalekhakriyayopayogam ||
children.translated_text: come into use among the lovely women of the <s>Vidyādharas</s> for the writing of love-letters.

children.text: yaḥ pūrayan kīcakarandhrabhāgān darīmukhotthena samīraṇena
children.translated_text: Filling the hollow parts of the reed-bamboos with wind rising from the mouths of caves,

children.text: udgāsyatām icchati kiṃnarāṇāṃ tānapradāyitvam ivopagantum ||
children.translated_text: he seems to wish to become the giver of pitch to the <s>Kiṃnaras</s> who are about to sing.

children.text: kapolakaṇḍūḥ karibhir vinetuṃ vighaṭṭitānāṃ saraladrumāṇām
children.translated_text: There, from pine trees rubbed and broken by elephants to remove itching on their cheeks,

children.text: yatra srutakṣīratayā prasūtaḥ sānūni gandhaḥ surabhīkaroti ||
children.translated_text: a fragrance, produced as though from flowing milk, perfumes the mountain slopes.

children.text: vanecarāṇāṃ vanitāsakhānāṃ darīgṛhotsaṅganiṣaktabhāsaḥ
children.translated_text: There, for forest-dwelling men accompanied by their women, with their light settled in the lap of cave-houses,

children.text: bhavanti yatrauṣadhayo rajanyām atailapūrāḥ suratapradīpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the herbs become, at night, lamps for lovemaking, needing no filling of oil.

children.text: udvejayaty aṅgulipārṣṇibhāgān mārge śilībhūtahime 'pi yatra
children.translated_text: There, even when stony ice on the road troubles the parts of their toes and heels,

children.text: na durvahaśroṇipayodharārtā bhindanti mandāṃ gatim aśvamukhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the horse-faced women, pained by the heavy burden of hips and breasts, do not break their slow gait.

children.text: divākarād rakṣati yo guhāsu līnaṃ divā bhītam ivāndhakāram
children.translated_text: He protects in his caves the darkness that has hidden by day from the sun, as if afraid;

children.text: kṣudre 'pi nūnaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapanne mamatvam uccaiḥśirasāṃ satīva ||
children.translated_text: surely, in the noble, there is affection even for a small being that has sought refuge.

children.text: lāṅgūlavikṣepavisarpiśobhair itas tataś candramarīcigauraiḥ
children.translated_text: With the spreading beauty of their tossed tails, white as moonbeams here and there,

children.text: yasyārthayuktaṃ girirājaśabdaṃ kurvanti vālavyajanaiś camaryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the yak-cows make the title 'king of mountains' meaningful for him by their chowries.

children.text: yatrāṃśukākṣepavilajjitānāṃ yadṛcchayā kiṃpuruṣāṅganānām
children.translated_text: There, when the women of the <s>Kiṃpuruṣas</s>, embarrassed by the accidental slipping aside of their garments,

children.text: darīgṛhadvāravilambibimbās tiraskariṇyo jaladā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: have their reflected forms hanging at the entrances of cave-houses, clouds become curtains for them.

children.text: bhāgīrathīnirjharasīkarāṇāṃ voḍhā muhuḥ kampitadevadāruḥ
children.translated_text: The wind there, bearing the spray of the cascades of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> and repeatedly shaking the deodars,

children.text: yad vāyur anviṣṭamṛgaiḥ kirātair āsevyate bhinnaśikhaṇḍibarhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is enjoyed by <s>Kirātas</s> searching for game, with the tail-feathers of peacocks split apart by it.

children.text: saptarṣihastāvacitāvaśeṣāṇy adho vivasvān parivartamānaḥ
children.translated_text: The sun, moving below the remnants of lotuses plucked by the hands of the Seven Seers,

children.text: padmāni yasyāgrasaroruhāṇi prabodhayaty ūrdhvamukhair mayūkhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: awakens the foremost lotuses of his high lakes with upward-facing rays.

children.text: yajñāṅgayonitvam avekṣya yasya sāraṃ dharitrīdharaṇakṣamaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Seeing his substance fit to be the source of sacrificial implements and capable of supporting the earth,

children.text: prajāpatiḥ kalpitayajñabhāgaṃ śailādhipatyaṃ svayam anvatiṣṭhat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> himself established him in lordship over mountains, with a share in sacrifice assigned to him.

children.text: sa mānasīṃ merusakhaḥ pitṝṇāṃ kanyāṃ kulasya sthitaye sthitijñaḥ
children.translated_text: He, the friend of <s>Meru</s> and knower of stability, for the continuance of his lineage,

children.text: menāṃ munīnām api mānanīyām ātmānurūpāṃ vidhinopayeme ||
children.translated_text: duly married <s>Menā</s>, the mind-born daughter of the Fathers, worthy of honor even among sages and suited to himself.

children.text: kālakrameṇātha tayoḥ pravṛtte svarūpayogye surataprasaṅge
children.translated_text: Then, in due course, when the occasion of love appropriate to their forms had begun for the two of them,

children.text: manoramaṃ yauvanam udvahantyā garbho 'bhavad bhūdhararājapatnyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: a pregnancy arose in the wife of the mountain-king, who was bearing charming youth.

children.text: asūta sā nāgavadhūpabhogyaṃ mainākam ambhonidhibaddhasakhyam
children.translated_text: She bore <s>Maināka</s>, fit for the enjoyment of serpent-maidens and bound in friendship with the ocean,

children.text: kruddhe 'pi pakṣacchidi vṛtraśatrāv avedanājñaṃ kuliśakṣatānām ||
children.translated_text: one who, even when <s>Indra</s>, the foe of <s>Vṛtra</s>, was angry and cut off wings, did not know the pain of thunderbolt wounds.

children.text: athāvamānena pituḥ prayuktā dakṣasya kanyā bhavapūrvapatnī
children.translated_text: Then the daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>, formerly the wife of <s>Bhava</s>, driven by her father's insult,

children.text: satī satī yogavisṛṣṭadehā tāṃ janmane śailavadhūṃ prapede ||
children.translated_text: the virtuous <s>Satī</s>, who had abandoned her body through yoga, came to that mountain-bride for rebirth.

children.text: sā bhūdharāṇām adhipena tasyāṃ samādhimatyām udapādi bhavyā
children.translated_text: She, auspicious, was born from the lord of mountains in that meditative woman,

children.text: samyakprayogād aparikṣatāyāṃ nītāv ivotsāhaguṇena saṃpat ||
children.translated_text: like prosperity born through the quality of energy in a policy unharmed by proper application.

children.text: prasannadik pāṃsuviviktavātaṃ śaṅkhasvanānantarapuṣpavṛṣṭi
children.translated_text: With the quarters clear, the wind free of dust, and a shower of flowers following the sound of conches,

children.text: śarīriṇāṃ sthāvarajaṅgamānāṃ sukhāya tajjanmadinaṃ babhūva ||
children.translated_text: that day of her birth became a source of happiness for embodied beings, both stationary and moving.

children.text: tayā duhitrā sutarāṃ savitrī sphuratprabhāmaṇḍalayā cakāse
children.translated_text: With that daughter, encircled by a flashing halo of radiance, the mother shone all the more,

children.text: vidūrabhūmir navameghaśabdād udbhinnayā ratnaśalākayeva ||
children.translated_text: like the distant earth at the sound of new clouds, with a sprout of jewel-light bursting forth.

children.text: dine dine sā parivardhamānā labdhodayā cāndramasīva lekhā
children.translated_text: Growing day by day, like a digit of the moon that has gained its rising,

children.text: pupoṣa lāvaṇyamayān viśeṣāñ jyotsnāntarāṇīva kalāntarāṇi ||
children.translated_text: she nourished successive distinctions made of beauty, as lunar phases nourish new increments of moonlight.

children.text: tāṃ pārvatīty ābhijanena nāmnā bandhupriyāṃ bandhujano juhāva
children.translated_text: Her relatives, fond of their kin, called her by the family name <s>Pārvatī</s>;

children.text: u meti mātrā tapaso niṣiddhā paścād umākhyāṃ sumukhī jagāma ||
children.translated_text: afterwards, since her mother had forbidden her austerity with the words 'u, mā' -- 'oh, do not' -- the beautiful-faced girl came to have the name <s>Umā</s>.

children.text: mahībhṛtaḥ putravato 'pi dṛṣṭis tasminn apatye na jagāma tṛptim
children.translated_text: Though the mountain had a son, his gaze did not reach satisfaction with that child;

children.text: anantapuṣpasya madhor hi cūte dvirephamālā saviśeṣasaṅgā ||
children.translated_text: for in spring, though it has endless flowers, a line of bees is especially attached to the mango tree.

children.text: prabhāmahatyā śikhayeva dīpas trimārgayeva tridivasya mārgaḥ
children.translated_text: Like a lamp by the greatness of its flame, like the path to heaven by the triple-flowing river,

children.text: saṃskāravatyeva girā manīṣī tayā sa pūtaś ca vibhūṣitaś ca ||
children.translated_text: like a wise man by cultivated speech, he was both purified and adorned by her.

children.text: mandākinīsaikatavedikābhiḥ sā kandukaiḥ kṛtrimaputrakaiś ca
children.translated_text: With little altars of sand from the <s>Mandākinī</s>, with balls, and with artificial dolls,

children.text: reme muhur madhyagatā sakhīnāṃ krīḍārasaṃ nirviśatīva bālye ||
children.translated_text: Again and again she delighted, standing among her friends, as though still tasting the flavor of play in childhood.

children.text: tāṃ haṃsamālāḥ śaradīva gaṅgāṃ mahauṣadhiṃ naktam ivātmabhāsaḥ
children.translated_text: As rows of swans approach the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in autumn, as great herbs at night approach their own radiance,

children.text: sthiropadeśām upadeśakāle prapedire prāktanajanmavidyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so the arts learned in former births came to her at the time of instruction, though she needed firm teaching.

children.text: asaṃbhṛtaṃ maṇḍanam aṅgayaṣṭer anāsavākhyaṃ karaṇaṃ madasya
children.translated_text: Then, beyond childhood, she attained an age that was an unassembled ornament for the slender stem of her body, a cause of intoxication not called wine,

children.text: kāmasya puṣpavyatiriktam astraṃ bālyāt paraṃ sātha vayaḥ prapede ||
children.translated_text: and a weapon of <s>Kāma</s> other than flowers.

children.text: unmīlitaṃ tūlikayeva citraṃ sūryāṃśubhir bhinnam ivāravindam
children.translated_text: Like a painting opened out by a brush, like a lotus split open by the sun's rays,

children.text: babhūva tasyāś caturasraśobhi vapur vibhaktaṃ navayauvanena ||
children.translated_text: her body became brilliant in all its parts, divided and displayed by fresh youth.

children.text: abhyunnatāṅguṣṭhanakhaprabhābhir nikṣepaṇād rāgam ivodgirantau
children.translated_text: Her two feet, with the radiance of their raised big-toe nails, as they were placed down, seemed to pour out red color,

children.text: ājahratus taccaraṇau pṛthivyāṃ sthalāravindaśriyam avyavasthām ||
children.translated_text: and brought to the earth the unstable beauty of land-lotuses.

children.text: sā rājahaṃsair iva saṃnatāṅgī gateṣu līlāñcitavikrameṣu
children.translated_text: When she, with her body slightly bent, moved in steps whose graceful advance was arched like royal swans,

children.text: vyanīyata pratyupadeśalubdhair āditsubhir nūpurasiñjitāni ||
children.translated_text: she was taught by them, greedy for instruction in return and wishing to take up the jingling of her anklets.

children.text: vṛttānupūrve ca na cātidīrghe jaṅghe śubhe sṛṣṭavatas tadīye
children.translated_text: When the creator had fashioned her auspicious shanks, rounded in due succession and not too long,

children.text: śeṣāṅganirmāṇavidhau vidhātur lāvaṇya utpādya ivāsa yatnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it was as though there remained effort for him to produce loveliness in the making of the rest of her limbs.

children.text: nāgendrahastās tvaci karkaśatvād ekāntaśaityāt kadalīviśeṣāḥ
children.translated_text: Elephant trunks, because of the roughness of their skin, and choice plantain stems, because of their absolute coldness,

children.text: labdhvāpi loke pariṇāhi rūpaṃ jātās tadūrvor upamānabāhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: though they had gained in the world a full and rounded form, became excluded from comparison with her thighs.

children.text: etāvatā nanv anumeyaśobhaṃ kāñcīguṇasthānam aninditāyāḥ
children.translated_text: Surely from so much one may infer the beauty of the faultless one's waist, the place of the girdle-string,

children.text: āropitaṃ yad giriśena paścād ananyanārīkamanīyam aṅkam ||
children.translated_text: since later <s>Giriśa</s> placed upon it the embrace lovely to no other woman.

children.text: tasyāḥ praviṣṭā natanābhirandhraṃ rarāja tanvī navalomarājiḥ
children.translated_text: Her delicate new line of hair, entering the hollow of her bent navel, shone

children.text: nīvīm atikramya sitetarasya tanmekhalāmadhyamaṇer ivārciḥ ||
children.translated_text: as though it were the ray of the dark central jewel of her girdle, passing beyond the skirt-knot.

children.text: madhyena sā vedivilagnamadhyā valitrayaṃ cāru babhāra bālā
children.translated_text: That girl, her middle clinging like an altar's waist, bore three lovely folds across her middle,

children.text: ārohaṇārthaṃ navayauvanena kāmasya sopānam iva prayuktam ||
children.translated_text: as though fresh youth had set them there as a stairway for <s>Kāma</s> to climb.

children.text: anyonyam utpīḍayad utpalākṣyāḥ stanadvayaṃ pāṇḍu tathā pravṛddham
children.translated_text: The lotus-eyed one's pair of breasts, pressing against each other, had grown so pale and full

children.text: madhye yathā śyāmamukhasya tasya mṛṇālasūtrāntaram apy alabhyam ||
children.translated_text: that between them, in the middle, there was not even space for a lotus-fiber thread, like the dark face of a lotus-stalk.

children.text: śirīṣapuṣpādhikasaukumāryau bāhū tadīyāv iti me vitarkaḥ
children.translated_text: Her two arms, I suppose, were softer than <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers,

children.text: parājitenāpi kṛtau harasya yau kaṇṭhapāśau makaradhvajena ||
children.translated_text: for though defeated by <s>Hara</s>, <s>Makaradhvaja</s> had made them into two nooses for his neck.

children.text: kaṇṭhasya tasyāḥ stanabandhurasya muktākalāpasya ca nistalasya
children.translated_text: Between her neck, curved by the breasts, and the smooth string of pearls,

children.text: anyonyaśobhājananād babhūva sādhāraṇo bhūṣaṇabhūṣyabhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because each produced the other's beauty, the relation of ornament and thing ornamented became mutual.

children.text: candraṃ gatā padmaguṇān na bhuṅkte padmāśritā cāndramasīm abhikhyām
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, having gone to the moon, does not enjoy the qualities of the lotus; dwelling in the lotus, she lacks the moon's radiance.

children.text: umāmukhaṃ tu pratipadya lolā dvisaṃśrayāṃ prītim avāpa lakṣmīḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when she reached <s>Umā</s>'s face, restless <s>Lakṣmī</s> obtained delight with both supports.

children.text: puṣpaṃ pravālopahitaṃ yadi syān muktāphalaṃ vā sphuṭavidrumastham
children.translated_text: If there were a flower set upon a coral shoot, or a pearl placed upon bright coral,

children.text: tato 'nukuryād viśadasya tasyās tāmrauṣṭhaparyastarucaḥ smitasya ||
children.translated_text: then it might imitate her clear smile, whose brightness was spread over coppery lips.

children.text: svareṇa tasyām amṛtasruteva prajalpitāyām abhijātavāci
children.translated_text: When she spoke with a voice like a stream of nectar and with noble speech,

children.text: apy anyapuṣṭā pratikūlaśabdā śrotur vitantrīr iva tāḍyamānā ||
children.translated_text: even cuckoos, their sound opposed to it, were like unstrung lutes being struck for the listener.

children.text: pravātanīlotpalanirviśeṣam adhīraviprekṣitam āyatākṣyā
children.translated_text: Her long-eyed, unsteady glance was indistinguishable from blue lotuses stirred by the wind.

children.text: tayā gṛhītaṃ nu mṛgāṅganābhyas tato gṛhītaṃ nu mṛgāṅganābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Was it taken by her from the does, or was it then taken by the does from her?

children.text: tasyāḥ śalākāñjananirmiteva kāntir bhruvor ānatalekhayor yā
children.translated_text: The beauty of her two bending eyebrows seemed made with collyrium on a stylus.

children.text: tāṃ vīkṣya līlācaturām anaṅgaḥ svacāpasaundaryamadaṃ mumoca ||
children.translated_text: Seeing it, playful and artful, bodiless <s>Anaṅga</s> gave up his pride in the beauty of his own bow.

children.text: lajjā tiraścāṃ yadi cetasi syād asaṃśayaṃ parvatarājaputryāḥ
children.translated_text: If modesty existed in the minds of animals, then, without doubt, on beholding the mountain-king's daughter's mass of hair,

children.text: taṃ keśapāśaṃ prasamīkṣya kuryur vālapriyatvaṃ śithilaṃ camaryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the yak-cows would make their affection for their tails slack.

children.text: sarvopamādravyasamuccayena yathāpradeśaṃ viniveśitena
children.translated_text: She had been fashioned by the creator of the universe with the whole collection of materials for comparison placed in their proper parts,

children.text: sā nirmitā viśvasṛjā prayatnād ekasthasaundaryadidṛkṣayeva ||
children.translated_text: as though through effort and from a desire to see beauty gathered in one place.

children.text: tāṃ nāradaḥ kāmacaraḥ kadācit kanyāṃ kila prekṣya pituḥ samīpe
children.translated_text: Once, it is said, <s>Nārada</s>, moving at will, saw that maiden near her father

children.text: samādideśaikavadhūṃ bhavitrīṃ premṇā śarīrārdhaharāṃ harasya ||
children.translated_text: and declared that she would become <s>Hara</s>'s sole bride, one who through love would take half his body.

children.text: guruḥ pragalbhe 'pi vayasy ato 'syās tasthau nivṛttānyavarābhilāṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore her father, though she had reached mature age, stood with his desire for other suitors withdrawn,

children.text: ṛte kṛśānor na hi mantrapūtam arhanti tejāṃsy aparāṇi havyam ||
children.translated_text: for no other fires, except fire itself, are fit to receive an oblation purified by mantras.

children.text: ayācitāraṃ na hi devadevam adriḥ sutāṃ grāhayituṃ śaśāka
children.translated_text: The mountain could not hand over his daughter to the god of gods while he had not asked for her;

children.text: abhyarthanābhaṅgabhayena sādhur mādhyasthyam iṣṭe 'py avalambate 'rthe ||
children.translated_text: a good man, from fear of a request being rejected, adopts neutrality even in a desired matter.

children.text: yadaiva pūrve janane śarīraṃ sā dakṣaroṣāt sudatī sasarja
children.translated_text: From the very time when, in her former birth, that fair-toothed one cast off her body through <s>Dakṣa</s>'s anger,

children.text: tadāprabhṛty eva vimuktasaṅgaḥ patiḥ paśūnām aparigraho 'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: the lord of beasts, freed from attachment, became one who took no wife.

children.text: sa kṛttivāsās tapase yatātmā gaṅgāpravāhokṣitadevadāru
children.translated_text: He, wearing a hide, self-controlled for austerity, dwelt on a plateau of <s>Himādri</s>,

children.text: prasthaṃ himādrer mṛganābhigandhi kiṃcit kvaṇatkiṃnaram adhyuvāsa ||
children.translated_text: sprinkled by the stream of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, fragrant with musk, and with deodars where <s>kiṃnaras</s> faintly sounded.

children.text: gaṇā nameruprasavāvataṃsā bhūrjatvacaḥ sparśavatīr dadhānāḥ
children.translated_text: His attendants, wearing ornaments of nameru blossoms and bearing birch-bark garments pleasant to the touch,

children.text: manaḥśilāvicchuritā niṣeduḥ śaileyanaddheṣu śilātaleṣu ||
children.translated_text: sat down on rock-slabs bound with mountain lichen and streaked with red arsenic.

children.text: tuṣārasaṃghātaśilāḥ khurāgraiḥ samullikhan darpakalaḥ kakudmān
children.translated_text: A humped bull, proud and sportful, scraping with the tips of his hoofs at masses of snow like stones,

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ kathaṃcid gavayair vivignair asoḍhasiṃhadhvanir unnanāda ||
children.translated_text: was seen by frightened wild oxen and, somehow unable to bear the sound of lions, bellowed upward.

children.text: tatrāgnim ādhāya samitsamiddhaṃ svam eva mūrtyantaram aṣṭamūrtiḥ
children.translated_text: There the eight-formed one, having laid a fire kindled with fuel,

children.text: svayaṃ vidhātā tapasaḥ phalānām kenāpi kāmena tapaś cacāra ||
children.translated_text: himself the ordainer of the fruits of austerity, performed austerity with some desire of his own.

children.text: anarghyam arghyeṇa tam adrināthaḥ svargaukasām arcitam arcayitvā
children.translated_text: The lord of the mountain, after honoring him, who was worshiped by the dwellers in heaven, with a priceless offering,

children.text: ārādhanāyāsya sakhīsametāṃ samādideśa prayatāṃ tanūjām ||
children.translated_text: appointed his self-restrained daughter, accompanied by her companions, to serve him.

children.text: pratyarthibhūtām api tāṃ samādheḥ śuśrūṣamāṇāṃ giriśo 'numene
children.translated_text: Although she was an obstacle to his meditation, <s>Giriśa</s> consented to her as she wished to serve him;

children.text: vikārahetau sati vikriyante yeṣāṃ na cetāṃsi ta eva dhīrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for those whose minds are not altered even when a cause for alteration is present, they alone are steadfast.

children.text: avacitabalipuṣpā vedisammārgadakṣā niyamavidhijalānāṃ barhiṣāṃ copanetrī
children.translated_text: Having gathered flowers for the offerings, skilled in sweeping the altar, bringing the prescribed waters and sacrificial grasses,

children.text: giriśam upacacāra pratyahaṃ sā sukeśī niyamitaparikhedā tacchiraścandrapādaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that fair-haired girl attended <s>Giriśa</s> every day, her fatigue regulated by the moonbeams on his head.

children.text: Chapter 2
tasmin viprakṛtāḥ kāle tārakeṇa divaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: At that time, the dwellers in heaven, injured by <s>Tāraka</s>,

children.text: turāsāhaṃ purodhāya dhāma svāyaṃbhuvaṃ yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: placing <s>Turāsāh</s> before them, went to the abode of the Self-born one.

children.text: teṣām āvirabhūd brahmā parimlānamukhaśriyām
children.translated_text: To them, whose facial beauty had faded, <s>Brahmā</s> appeared,

children.text: sarasāṃ suptapadmānāṃ prātar dīdhitimān iva ||
children.translated_text: like the sun at dawn appearing to lakes whose lotuses are asleep.

children.text: atha sarvasya dhātāraṃ te sarve sarvatomukham
children.translated_text: Then all of them, bowing down to the maker of all, the all-faced one,

children.text: vāgīśaṃ vāgbhir arthyābhiḥ praṇipatyopatasthire ||
children.translated_text: the lord of speech, approached him with meaningful words of petition.

children.text: namas trimūrtaye tubhyaṃ prāk sṛṣṭeḥ kevalātmane
children.translated_text: Homage to you, whose form is the triad, who before creation are the sole self,

children.text: guṇatrayavibhāgāya paścād bhedam upeyuṣe ||
children.translated_text: and who afterward, for the division of the three guṇas, have come into differentiation.

children.text: yad amogham apām antar uptaṃ bījam aja tvayā
children.translated_text: The unfailing seed, O Unborn one, which was sown by you within the waters,

children.text: ataś carācaraṃ viśvaṃ prabhavas tasya gīyase ||
children.translated_text: from that this whole moving and unmoving universe arose; you are sung as its source.

children.text: tisṛbhis tvam avasthābhir mahimānam udīrayan
children.translated_text: You, making manifest your greatness through the three states,

children.text: pralayasthitisargāṇām ekaḥ kāraṇatāṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: have become the single cause of dissolution, continuance, and creation.

children.text: strīpuṃsāv ātmabhāgau te bhinnamūrteḥ sisṛkṣayā
children.translated_text: The female and the male are two parts of your own self, of you whose form was divided by the wish to create;

children.text: prasūtibhājaḥ sargasya tāv eva pitarau smṛtau ||
children.translated_text: those two are remembered as the parents of creation, which partakes of birth.

children.text: svakālaparimāṇena vyastarātriṃdivasya te
children.translated_text: For you, whose night and day are separately measured by their own spans of time,

children.text: yau tu svapnāvabodhau tau bhūtānāṃ pralayodayau ||
children.translated_text: what are sleep and awakening for you are the dissolution and arising of beings.

children.text: jagadyonir ayonis tvaṃ jagadanto nirantakaḥ
children.translated_text: You are the womb of the world, yet without a womb; the end of the world, yet without an ender;

children.text: jagadādir anādis tvaṃ jagadīśo nirīśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: you are the beginning of the world, yet without beginning; the lord of the world, yet with no lord over you.

children.text: ātmānam ātmanā vetsi sṛjasy ātmānam ātmanā
children.translated_text: You know yourself by yourself; you create yourself by yourself;

children.text: ātmanā kṛtinā ca tvam ātmany eva pralīyase ||
children.translated_text: and by your own active self you dissolve into yourself alone.

children.text: dravaḥ saṃghātakaṭhinaḥ sthūlaḥ sūkṣmo laghur guruḥ
children.translated_text: You are fluid, compact and hard, gross, subtle, light, and heavy;

children.text: vyakto vyaktetaraś cāsi prākāmyaṃ te vibhūtiṣu ||
children.translated_text: you are manifest and other than manifest; unimpeded power is yours among your manifestations.

children.text: udghātaḥ praṇavo yāsāṃ nyāyais tribhir udīraṇam
children.translated_text: The opening of which is the praṇava, whose utterance proceeds by the three accents,

children.text: karma yajñaḥ phalaṃ svargas tāsāṃ tvaṃ prabhavo girām ||
children.translated_text: whose action is sacrifice and whose fruit is heaven: of those sacred utterances you are the source.

children.text: tvām āmananti prakṛtiṃ puruṣārthapravartinīm
children.translated_text: They declare you to be <s>prakṛti</s>, setting in motion the aims of the <s>puruṣa</s>;

children.text: taddarśinam udāsīnaṃ tvām eva puruṣaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: and they know you alone as the <s>puruṣa</s>, the witness of that, indifferent and apart.

children.text: tvaṃ pitṝṇām api pitā devānām api devatā
children.translated_text: You are the father even of the Fathers, the deity even of the gods;

children.text: parato 'pi paraś cāsi vidhātā vedhasām api ||
children.translated_text: you are beyond even what is beyond, the ordainer even of the creators.

children.text: tvam eva havyaṃ hotā ca bhojyaṃ bhoktā ca śāśvataḥ
children.translated_text: You alone are the oblation and the offering priest, the food and the eternal enjoyer;

children.text: vedyaṃ ca veditā cāsi dhyātā dhyeyaṃ ca yat param ||
children.translated_text: you are what is to be known and the knower, the meditator and that highest object of meditation.

children.text: iti tebhyaḥ stutīḥ śrutvā yathārthā hṛdayaṃgamāḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard from them these praises, accurate and entering the heart,

children.text: prasādābhimukho vedhāḥ pratyuvāca divaukasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the creator, turning toward favor, replied to the dwellers in heaven.

children.text: purāṇasya kaves tasya caturmukhasamīritā
children.translated_text: Set in motion by the four-faced one, the speech of that ancient poet

children.text: pravṛttir āsīc chabdānāṃ caritārthā catuṣṭayī ||
children.translated_text: proceeded in fourfold form, accomplishing its purpose in all four ways.

children.text: svāgataṃ svān adhīkārān prabhāvair avalambya vaḥ
children.translated_text: Welcome to you, mighty in valor, who have come all at once from the arms of the ages,

children.text: yugapad yugabāhubhyaḥ prāptebhyaḥ prājyavikramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: each relying through your powers upon your own offices.

children.text: kim idaṃ dyutim ātmīyāṃ na bibhrati yathā purā
children.translated_text: Why do your faces no longer bear their own brilliance as before,

children.text: himakliṣṭaprakāśāni jyotīṃṣīva mukhāni vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like lights whose radiance has been distressed by frost?

children.text: praśamād arciṣām etad anudgīrṇasurāyudham
children.translated_text: Because its flames are quieted, this thunderbolt of the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, not emitting the weapon of the gods,

children.text: vṛtrasya hantuḥ kuliśaṃ kuṇṭhitāśrīva lakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: appears as if its sharp splendor has been blunted.

children.text: kiṃ cāyam aridurvāraḥ pāṇau pāśaḥ pracetasaḥ
children.translated_text: And why has this noose, hard for enemies to withstand, in the hand of <s>Pracetas</s>,

children.text: mantreṇa hatavīryasya phaṇino dainyam āśritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: fallen into the wretchedness of a serpent whose power has been destroyed by a spell?

children.text: kuberasya manaḥśalyaṃ śaṃsatīva parābhavam
children.translated_text: The arm of <s>Kubera</s>, its mace cast aside, seems to proclaim defeat, a thorn in his heart,

children.text: apaviddhagado bāhur bhagnaśākha iva drumaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like a tree with a broken branch.

children.text: yamo 'pi vilikhan bhūmiṃ daṇḍenāstamitatviṣā
children.translated_text: Even <s>Yama</s>, scratching the ground with a staff whose brilliance has set,

children.text: kurute 'sminn amoghe 'pi nirvāṇālātalāghavam ||
children.translated_text: makes that unfailing rod seem as light as a coal gone out.

children.text: amī ca katham ādityāḥ pratāpakṣatiśītalāḥ
children.translated_text: And how have these <s>Ādityas</s>, cooled by the loss of their heat,

children.text: citranyastā iva gatāḥ prakāmālokanīyatām ||
children.translated_text: become fit to be gazed at at will, as if painted in a picture?

children.text: paryākulatvān marutāṃ vegabhaṅgo 'numīyate
children.translated_text: From the agitation of the <s>Maruts</s>, the breaking of their speed is inferred,

children.text: ambhasām oghasaṃrodhaḥ pratīpagamanād iva ||
children.translated_text: as the obstruction of a flood of waters is inferred from its flowing backward.

children.text: āvarjitajaṭāmaulivilambiśaśikoṭayaḥ
children.translated_text: The heads even of the <s>Rudras</s>, with the crescent moons hanging from their bent masses of matted hair,

children.text: rudrāṇām api mūrdhānaḥ kṣatahuṃkāraśaṃsinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: show that their roar has been wounded.

children.text: labdhapratiṣṭhāḥ prathamaṃ yūyaṃ kiṃ balavattaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Having first obtained established authority, have you now, by stronger beings,

children.text: apavādair ivotsargāḥ kṛtavyāvṛttayaḥ paraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: been made exceptions, like general rules by later exclusions?

children.text: tad brūta vatsāḥ kim itaḥ prārthayadhve samāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore speak, my children: what do you desire from me, having come here?

children.text: mayi sṛṣṭir hi lokānāṃ rakṣā yuṣmāsv avasthitā ||
children.translated_text: For the creation of the worlds rests in me, but their protection rests in you.

children.text: tato mandāniloddhūtakamalākaraśobhinā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vāsava</s>, with his thousand eyes beautified like a lotus-bed stirred by a gentle wind,

children.text: guruṃ netrasahasreṇa codayāmāsa vāsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: urged his preceptor on.

children.text: sa dvinetro hareś cakṣuḥ sahasranayanādhikam
children.translated_text: He of two eyes, <s>Vācaspati</s>, whose sight was greater than <s>Hari</s>'s thousand eyes,

children.text: vācaspatir uvācedaṃ prāñjalir jalajāsanam ||
children.translated_text: with joined palms spoke this to the lotus-seated one.

children.text: evaṃ yad āttha bhagavann āmṛṣṭaṃ naḥ paraiḥ padam
children.translated_text: What you have said, blessed lord, is so: our station has been assailed by enemies.

children.text: pratyekaṃ viniyuktātmā kathaṃ na jñāsyasi prabho ||
children.translated_text: Since each one's self has been appointed by you, how could you not know it, O lord?

children.text: bhavallabdhavarodīrṇas tārakākhyo mahāsuraḥ
children.translated_text: The great Asura named <s>Tāraka</s>, swollen with the boon obtained from you,

children.text: upaplavāya lokānāṃ dhūmaketur ivotthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has risen up like a comet for the affliction of the worlds.

children.text: pure tāvantam evāsya tanoti ravir ātapam
children.translated_text: In his city the sun extends just so much heat

children.text: dīrghikākamalonmeṣo yāvanmātreṇa sādhyate ||
children.translated_text: as is needed for the opening of the lotuses in the ponds.

children.text: sarvābhiḥ sarvadā candras taṃ kalābhir niṣevate
children.translated_text: The moon always serves him with all his digits,

children.text: nādatte kevalāṃ lekhāṃ haracūḍāmaṇīkṛtām ||
children.translated_text: and does not assume only that single crescent which has been made the crest-jewel of <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: vyāvṛttagatir udyāne kusumasteyasādhvasāt
children.translated_text: Because of fear of stealing flowers, the wind, its motion turned back in the garden,

children.text: na vāti vāyus tatpārśve tālavṛntānilādhikam ||
children.translated_text: does not blow near him with a breeze stronger than that of a palm-leaf fan.

children.text: paryāyasevām utsṛjya puṣpasaṃbhāratatparāḥ
children.translated_text: Abandoning their regular attendance, intent on heaps of flowers,

children.text: udyānapālasāmānyam ṛtavas tam upāsate ||
children.translated_text: the seasons serve him like ordinary gardeners.

children.text: tasyopāyanayogyāni ratnāni saritāṃ patiḥ
children.translated_text: The lord of rivers somehow waits, among the waters,

children.text: katham apy ambhasām antar ā niṣpatteḥ pratīkṣate ||
children.translated_text: for precious stones fit to be presented to him, until they emerge.

children.text: jvalanmaṇiśikhāś cainaṃ vāsukipramukhā niśi
children.translated_text: At night, serpents headed by <s>Vāsuki</s>, with blazing jewel-crests,

children.text: sthirapradīpatām etya bhujaṃgāḥ paryupāsate ||
children.translated_text: attend upon him, having become steady lamps.

children.text: tatkṛtānugrahāpekṣī taṃ muhur dūtahāritaiḥ
children.translated_text: Even <s>Indra</s>, hoping for favor from him, repeatedly seeks to please him

children.text: anukūlayatīndro 'pi kalpadrumavibhūṣaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with ornaments from the wish-fulfilling tree carried by messengers.

children.text: ittham ārādhyamāno 'pi kliśnāti bhuvanatrayam
children.translated_text: Although he is worshiped in this way, he afflicts the three worlds:

children.text: śāmyet pratyapakāreṇa nopakāreṇa durjanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a wicked man is pacified by retaliation, not by benefaction.

children.text: tenāmaravadhūhastaiḥ sadayālūnapallavāḥ
children.translated_text: Because of him, the trees of <s>Nandana</s>, whose tender shoots are compassionately cut by the hands of immortal women,

children.text: abhijñāś chedapātānāṃ kriyante nandanadrumāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are made familiar with the fall caused by cutting.

children.text: vījyate sa hi saṃsuptaḥ śvāsasādhāraṇānilaiḥ
children.translated_text: For when he sleeps he is fanned by the captive women of the gods

children.text: cāmaraiḥ surabandīnāṃ bāṣpaśīkaravarṣibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with chowries whose breezes are mingled with his breaths and which shower droplets of tears.

children.text: utpāṭya meruśṛṅgāṇi kṣuṇṇāni haritāṃ khuraiḥ
children.translated_text: Having torn up peaks of <s>Meru</s>, crushed by the hooves of his horses,

children.text: ākrīḍaparvatās tena kalpitāḥ sveṣu veśmasu ||
children.translated_text: he has made them pleasure mountains in his own mansions.

children.text: mandākinyāḥ payaḥśeṣaṃ digvāraṇamadāvilam
children.translated_text: The remaining water of the <s>Mandākinī</s>, muddied by the rut of the elephants of the quarters,

children.text: hemāmbhoruhasasyānāṃ tadvāpyo dhāma sāṃpratam ||
children.translated_text: is now the home of golden lotus crops in his tanks.

children.text: bhuvanālokanaprītiḥ svargibhir nānubhūyate
children.translated_text: The joy of looking upon the worlds is no longer experienced by the dwellers in heaven,

children.text: khilībhūte vimānānāṃ tadāpātabhayāt pathi ||
children.translated_text: because the path of their aerial cars has become obstructed through fear of his attack.

children.text: yajvabhiḥ saṃbhṛtaṃ havyaṃ vitateṣv adhvareṣu saḥ
children.translated_text: The oblation gathered by sacrificers in extended sacrifices

children.text: jātavedomukhān māyī miṣatām ācchinatti naḥ ||
children.translated_text: that trickster snatches from the mouth of <s>Jātavedas</s> while we look on.

children.text: uccair uccaiḥśravās tena hayaratnam ahāri ca
children.translated_text: And by him the jewel of horses, lofty <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>, has been carried off,

children.text: dehabaddham ivendrasya cirakālārjitaṃ yaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Indra</s>'s fame, won over a long time and embodied in a form.

children.text: tasminn upāyāḥ sarve naḥ krūre pratihatakriyāḥ
children.translated_text: Against that cruel one all our stratagems have their action blocked,

children.text: vīryavaty auṣadhānīva vikāre sāṃnipātike ||
children.translated_text: like potent medicines in a disorder caused by all the humors together.

children.text: jayāśā yatra cāsmākaṃ pratighātotthitārciṣā
children.translated_text: Where our hope of victory lay, there by him, with its flames risen from resistance,

children.text: haricakreṇa tenāsya kaṇṭhe niṣka ivārpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the discus of <s>Hari</s> was placed upon his neck like a necklace.

children.text: tadīyās toyadeṣv adya puṣkarāvartakādiṣu
children.translated_text: Now his elephants, having conquered <s>Airāvata</s>, practice blows against banks

children.text: abhyasyanti taṭāghātaṃ nirjitairāvatā gajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: upon his clouds, <s>Puṣkara</s>, <s>Āvartaka</s>, and the rest.

children.text: tad icchāmo vibho sṛṣṭaṃ senānyaṃ tasya śāntaye
children.translated_text: Therefore, lord, we desire that a commander be created for the pacification of him,

children.text: karmabandhacchidaṃ dharmaṃ bhavasyeva mumukṣavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as those seeking liberation desire <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), which cuts the bond of action.

children.text: goptāraṃ surasainyānāṃ yaṃ puraskṛtya gotrabhit
children.translated_text: Putting him in front as protector of the armies of the gods, <s>Gotrabhit</s>

children.text: pratyāneṣyati śatrubhyo bandīm iva jayaśriyam ||
children.translated_text: will bring back from the enemies the fortune of victory, as though she were a captive woman.

children.text: vacasy avasite tasmin sasarja giram ātmabhūḥ
children.translated_text: When that speech had ended, the Self-born One uttered a voice,

children.text: garjitānantarāṃ vṛṣṭiṃ saubhāgyena jigāya yā ||
children.translated_text: which by its beauty surpassed rain that follows immediately after thunder.

children.text: sampatsyate vaḥ kāmo yaṃ kālaḥ kaścit pratīkṣyatām
children.translated_text: Your desire will be fulfilled; let a certain time be awaited.

children.text: na tv asya siddhau yāsyāmi sargavyāpāram ātmanā ||
children.translated_text: But in accomplishing it I shall not myself enter upon the business of creation.

children.text: itaḥ sa daityaḥ prāptaśrīr neta evārhati kṣayam
children.translated_text: That demon, having gained prosperity from here, deserves destruction from here alone;

children.text: viṣavṛkṣo 'pi saṃvardhya svayaṃ chettum asāṃpratam ||
children.translated_text: even a poisonous tree, once fostered, is not fitting to be cut down by oneself.

children.text: vṛtaṃ tenedam eva prāṅ mayā cāsmai pratiśrutam
children.translated_text: This very thing was formerly chosen by him, and by me it was promised to him as a boon;

children.text: vareṇa śamitaṃ lokān alaṃ dagdhuṃ hi tattapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for his austerity, appeased by a boon, was able enough to burn the worlds.

children.text: saṃyuge sāṃyugīnaṃ tam udyataṃ prasaheta kaḥ
children.translated_text: When he is raised up for battle and fit for battle, who could withstand him in combat,

children.text: aṃśād ṛte niṣiktasya nīlalohitaretasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: except the portion of the seed of the Blue-and-Red One once deposited?

children.text: sa hi devaḥ paraṃ jyotis tamaḥpāre vyavasthitam
children.translated_text: For that god is the supreme light established beyond darkness,

children.text: paricchinnaprabhāvarddhir na mayā na ca viṣṇunā ||
children.translated_text: whose increase of radiance is bounded neither by me nor by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: umārūpeṇa te yūyaṃ saṃyamastimitaṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: Through <s>Umā</s>'s form, you should strive to draw the self-restrained, motionless mind

children.text: śaṃbhor yatadhvam ākraṣṭum ayaskāntena lohavat ||
children.translated_text: of <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, like iron by a lodestone.

children.text: ubhe eva kṣame voḍhum ubhayor vīryam āhitam
children.translated_text: Both alone are capable of bearing the power deposited by both:

children.text: sā vā śaṃbhos tadīyā vā mūrtir jalamayī mama ||
children.translated_text: she, or that form of <s>Śaṃbhu</s> belonging to him, my water-formed shape.

children.text: tasyātmā śitikaṇṭhasya saināpatyam upetya vaḥ
children.translated_text: The son of that dark-throated one, after taking up command of your army,

children.text: mokṣyate surabandīnāṃ veṇīr vīryavibhūtibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: will release the braids of the captive women of the gods by the splendors of his valor.

children.text: iti vyāhṛtya vibudhān viśvayonis tirodadhe
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the gods, the source of the universe disappeared,

children.text: manasy āhitakartavyās te 'pi pratiyayur divam ||
children.translated_text: and they too, placing in their minds what had to be done, returned to heaven.

children.text: tatra niścitya kandarpam agamat pākaśāsanaḥ
children.translated_text: There, having fixed upon <s>Kandarpa</s>, the chastiser of <s>Pāka</s> went to him,

children.text: manasā kāryasaṃsiddhitvarādviguṇaraṃhasā ||
children.translated_text: with a speed doubled by his mind through haste for the accomplishment of the task.

children.text: atha sa lalitayoṣidbhrūlatācāruśṛṅgaṃ rativalayapadāṅke cāpam āsajya kaṇṭhe
children.translated_text: Then the flower-bowed god, having hung upon his neck the bow whose graceful tip was charming like a lovely woman's creeper-like eyebrow and which bore the marks of <s>Rati</s>'s bracelets,

children.text: sahacaramadhuhastanyastacūtāṅkurāstraḥ śatamakham upatasthe prāñjaliḥ puṣpadhanvā ||
children.translated_text: with mango-shoot arrows placed in the hand of his companion Spring, stood before the hundred-sacrificed one with joined palms.

children.text: Chapter 3
tasmin maghonas tridaśān vihāya sahasram akṣṇāṃ yugapat papāta
children.translated_text: Upon him <s>Maghavan</s>'s thousand eyes fell all at once, leaving the gods,

children.text: prayojanāpekṣitayā prabhūṇāṃ prāyaś calaṃ gauravam āśriteṣu ||
children.translated_text: for the respect of the powerful toward dependents is generally unstable when a purpose is expected.

children.text: sa vāsavenāsanasaṃnikṛṣṭam ito niṣīdeti visṛṣṭabhūmiḥ
children.translated_text: Given a place by <s>Vāsava</s> near his seat, with the words, 'Sit here,'

children.text: bhartuḥ prasādaṃ pratinandya mūrdhnā vaktuṃ mithaḥ prākramataivam enam ||
children.translated_text: he acknowledged his lord's favor with his head and began to speak to him privately as follows.

children.text: ājñāpaya jñātaviśeṣa puṃsāṃ lokeṣu yat te karaṇīyam asti
children.translated_text: Command me, you who know the distinctions among men, in whatever task of yours there is to be done in the worlds.

children.text: anugrahaṃ saṃsmaraṇapravṛttam icchāmi saṃvardhitam ājñayā te ||
children.translated_text: I wish the favor that has arisen from your remembering me to be increased by your command.

children.text: kenābhyasūyā padakāṅkṣiṇā te nitāntadīrghair janitā tapobhiḥ
children.translated_text: By what man, envying you and desiring your station, has jealousy been produced through exceedingly long austerities,

children.text: yāvad bhavaty āhitasāyakasya matkārmukasyāsya nideśavartī ||
children.translated_text: so that he may become subject to this bow of mine when its arrow has been set upon it?

children.text: asaṃmataḥ kas tava muktimārgaṃ punarbhavakleśabhayāt prapannaḥ
children.translated_text: Who is displeasing to you, having entered the path of liberation through fear of the pain of rebirth?

children.text: baddhaś ciraṃ tiṣṭhatu sundarīṇām ārecitabhrūcaturaiḥ kaṭākṣaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let him remain bound for a long time by the sidelong glances of lovely women, clever with arched brows.

children.text: adhyāpitasyośanasāpi nītiṃ prayuktarāgapraṇidhir dviṣas te
children.translated_text: Even if instructed in policy by <s>Uśanas</s>, your enemy, when a fixed application of passion has been employed...

children.text: kasyārthadharmau vada pīḍayāmi sindhos taṭāv ogha iva pravṛddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell me, whose prosperity and <s>dharma</s> do I afflict, grown like a flood on the two banks of a river?

children.text: kām ekapatnīvrataduḥkhaśīlāṃ lolaṃ manaś cārutayā praviṣṭām
children.translated_text: What woman do you desire: one committed to the hardship of a single-husband vow, into whose beauty a restless mind has entered,

children.text: nitambinīm icchasi muktalajjāṃ kaṇṭhe svayaṃgrāhaniṣaktabāhum ||
children.translated_text: a full-hipped woman who has cast off shame, with her arms fastened of themselves in a clasp around your neck?

children.text: kayāsi kāmin suratāparādhāt pādānataḥ kopanayāvadhūtaḥ
children.translated_text: By what angry beloved, because of an offense in love-play, have you, a lover bowed at her feet, been spurned,

children.text: yasyāḥ kariṣyāmi dṛḍhānutāpaṃ pravālaśayyāśaraṇaṃ śarīram ||
children.translated_text: so that I shall make her body, taking refuge on a bed of tender shoots, feel firm remorse?

children.text: prasīda viśrāmyatu vīra vajraṃ śarair madīyaiḥ katamaḥ surāriḥ
children.translated_text: Be gracious, hero; let the thunderbolt rest. Which enemy of the gods could fear my arrows,

children.text: bibhetu moghīkṛtabāhuvīryaḥ strībhyo 'pi kopasphuritādharābhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his arm-strength made futile, even more than women whose lips tremble with anger?

children.text: tava prasādāt kusumāyudho 'pi sahāyam ekaṃ madhum eva labdhvā
children.translated_text: By your favor even I, the flower-armed one, having obtained Spring alone as my helper,

children.text: kuryāṃ harasyāpi pinākapāṇer dhairyacyutiṃ ke mama dhanvino 'nye ||
children.translated_text: would cause even <s>Hara</s>, the bow-bearing wielder of <s>Pināka</s>, to lose firmness; what other archers are anything to me?

children.text: athorudeśād avatārya pādam ākrāntisaṃbhāvitapādapīṭham
children.translated_text: Then, lowering from his broad thigh the foot that had made a footstool seem honored by its tread,

children.text: saṃkalpitārthe vivṛtātmaśaktim ākhaṇḍalaḥ kāmam idaṃ babhāṣe ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>, seeing <s>Kāma</s> reveal his power for the intended task, spoke these words.

children.text: sarvaṃ sakhe tvayy upapannam etad ubhe mamāstre kuliśaṃ bhavāṃś ca
children.translated_text: All this is fitting in you, my friend. My two weapons are the thunderbolt and you.

children.text: vajraṃ tapovīryamahatsu kuṇṭhaṃ tvaṃ sarvatogāmi ca sādhakaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The thunderbolt is blunted against those great in the power of austerity, but you move everywhere and accomplish the end.

children.text: avaimi te sāram ataḥ khalu tvāṃ kārye guruṇy ātmasamaṃ niyokṣye
children.translated_text: I know your essence; therefore, indeed, I shall appoint you, as my own equal, to a weighty task.

children.text: vyādiśyate bhūdharatām avekṣya kṛṣṇena dehodvahanāya śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing his mountain-like strength, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> commanded <s>Śeṣa</s> to bear his body.

children.text: āśaṃsatā bāṇagatiṃ vṛṣāṅke kāryaṃ tvayā naḥ pratipannakalpam
children.translated_text: We look for the flight of an arrow against the bull-marked one; the task has been virtually undertaken by you.

children.text: nibodha yajñāṃśabhujām idānīm uccairdviṣām īpsitam etad eva ||
children.translated_text: Now hear this very desire of the high enemies of those who eat the shares of sacrifice.

children.text: amī hi vīryaprabhavaṃ bhavasya jayāya senānyam uśanti devāḥ
children.translated_text: These gods desire, for victory, a commander of the army born from <s>Bhava</s>'s virility.

children.text: sa ca tvadekeṣunipātasādhyo brahmāṅgabhūr brahmaṇi yojitātmā ||
children.translated_text: And he, born from <s>Brahmā</s>'s limb and with his mind fixed on <s>brahman</s>, can be mastered only by the fall of your single arrow.

children.text: tasmai himādreḥ prayatāṃ tanūjāṃ yatātmane rocayituṃ yatasva
children.translated_text: Strive to make acceptable to that self-restrained one the pure daughter of <s>Himādri</s>.

children.text: yoṣitsu tadvīryaniṣekabhūmiḥ saiva kṣamety ātmabhuvopadiṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: The Self-born has instructed us that she alone is a suitable ground among women for the deposit of his seed.

children.text: guror niyogāc ca nagendrakanyā sthāṇuṃ tapasyantam adhityakāyām
children.translated_text: And at her father's command the mountain-king's daughter attends upon <s>Sthāṇu</s>, who is performing austerity on a plateau.

children.text: anvāsta ity apsarasāṃ mukhebhyaḥ śrutaṃ mayā matpraṇidhiḥ sa vargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I have heard this from the mouths of the apsarases; that group is my informant.

children.text: tad gaccha siddhyai kuru devakāryam artho 'yam arthāntarabhāvya eva
children.translated_text: So go, and for success perform the gods' business. This aim is one to be brought about through another aim.

children.text: apekṣate pratyayam uttamaṃ tvāṃ bījāṅkuraḥ prāg udayād ivāmbhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It awaits you, the highest cause of confidence, just as a seed-sprout before rising awaits water.

children.text: tasmin surāṇāṃ vijayābhyupāye tavaiva nāmāstragatiḥ kṛtī tvam
children.translated_text: In that means for the gods' victory, the movement of the weapon is yours alone; you are the effective man.

children.text: apy aprasiddhaṃ yaśase hi puṃsām ananyasādhāraṇam eva karma ||
children.translated_text: For even an unknown deed, if uncommon to others, brings men fame.

children.text: surāḥ samabhyarthayitāra ete kāryaṃ trayāṇām api viṣṭapānām
children.translated_text: These gods are your petitioners; the matter concerns all three worlds.

children.text: cāpena te karma na cātihiṃsram aho batāsi spṛhaṇīyavīryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Your work is done with a bow, and is not excessively violent. Ah, how enviable is your valor!

children.text: madhuś ca te manmatha sāhacaryād asāvanukto 'pi sahāya eva
children.translated_text: And Spring, <s>Manmatha</s>, by reason of companionship with you, is your helper even though not named.

children.text: samīraṇo nodayitā bhaveti vyādiśyate kena hutāśanasya ||
children.translated_text: Who commands the wind to be the kindler of fire?

children.text: tatheti śeṣām iva bhartur ājñām ādāya mūrdhnā madanaḥ pratasthe
children.translated_text: Saying 'So be it,' <s>Madana</s> received on his head his lord's command, as though it were the remainder of it, and set out.

children.text: airāvatāsphālanakarkaśena hastena pasparśa tadaṅgam indraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> touched his body with a hand rough from striking <s>Airāvata</s>.

children.text: sa mādhavenābhimatena sakhyā ratyā ca sāśaṅkam anuprayātaḥ
children.translated_text: He, followed by <s>Mādhava</s>, his chosen friend, and by <s>Rati</s>, who was anxious,

children.text: aṅgavyayaprārthitakāryasiddhiḥ sthāṇvāśramaṃ haimavataṃ jagāma ||
children.translated_text: went to <s>Sthāṇu</s>'s Himalayan hermitage, seeking the success of a task that required the loss of his body.

children.text: tasmin vane saṃyamināṃ munīnāṃ tapaḥsamādheḥ pratikūlavartī
children.translated_text: In that forest of self-restrained sages, hostile to the absorption of austerity,

children.text: saṃkalpayoner abhimānabhūtam ātmānam ādhāya madhur jajṛmbhe ||
children.translated_text: <s>Madhu</s>, putting on himself as the pride of the mind-born god, burst forth.

children.text: kuberaguptāṃ diśam uṣṇaraśmau gantuṃ pravṛtte samayaṃ vilaṅghya
children.translated_text: When the hot-rayed sun began to go toward the quarter guarded by <s>Kubera</s>, transgressing the proper season,

children.text: dig dakṣiṇā gandhavahaṃ mukhena vyalīkaniḥśvāsam ivotsasarja ||
children.translated_text: the southern quarter let out the fragrance-bearing wind from its mouth, as though a sigh of resentment.

children.text: asūta sadyaḥ kusumāny aśokaḥ skandhāt prabhṛty eva sapallavāni
children.translated_text: The aśoka at once produced flowers, together with leaves, beginning from the trunk itself,

children.text: pādena nāpaikṣata sundarīṇāṃ saṃparkam āsiñjitanūpureṇa ||
children.translated_text: and did not wait for contact with the foot of beautiful women, ringing with anklets.

children.text: sadyaḥ pravālodgamacārupatre nīte samāptiṃ navacūtabāṇe
children.translated_text: When the new mango-arrow, lovely with leaves from which shoots had just emerged, was brought to completion,

children.text: niveśayāmāsa madhur dvirephān nāmākṣarāṇīva manobhavasya ||
children.translated_text: <s>Madhu</s> placed bees upon it like the letters of <s>Manobhava</s>'s name.

children.text: varṇaprakarṣe sati karṇikāraṃ dunoti nirgandhatayā sma cetaḥ
children.translated_text: Though the karṇikāra had excellence of color, it pained the mind through being scentless.

children.text: prāyeṇa sāmagryavidhau guṇānāṃ parāṅmukhī viśvasṛjaḥ pravṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Generally, when the full complement of qualities is being arranged, the creator of the universe turns away from some of them.

children.text: bālenduvakrāṇy avikāsabhāvād babhuḥ palāśāny atilohitāni
children.translated_text: Because they had not yet opened, the palāśa blossoms, very red, were like crescent moons,

children.text: sadyo vasantena samāgatānāṃ nakhakṣatānīva vanasthalīnām ||
children.translated_text: like nail-marks on the forest-grounds that had just been joined by Spring.

children.text: lagnadvirephāñjanabhakticitram mukhe madhuśrīs tilakaṃ prakāśya
children.translated_text: Spring's beauty, displaying on her face a tilaka mark variegated with the collyrium-lines of clinging bees,

children.text: rāgeṇa bālāruṇakomalena cūtapravāloṣṭham alaṃcakāra ||
children.translated_text: adorned the mango-shoot as her lip, tender and reddish like the young sun, with passion's color.

children.text: mṛgāḥ priyāladrumamañjarīṇāṃ rajaḥkaṇair vighnitadṛṣṭipātāḥ
children.translated_text: Deer, their sight hindered by particles of pollen from the clusters of priyāla trees,

children.text: madoddhatāḥ pratyanilaṃ vicerur vanasthalīr marmarapatramokṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: moved proudly with rut against the wind through forest-grounds dropping rustling leaves.

children.text: cūtāṅkurāsvādakaṣāyakaṇṭhaḥ puṃskokilo yan madhuraṃ cukūja
children.translated_text: The sweet note that the male cuckoo, his throat astringent from tasting mango sprouts, sang out

children.text: manasvinīmānavighātadakṣaṃ tad eva jātaṃ vacanaṃ smarasya ||
children.translated_text: became the very speech of <s>Smara</s>, skillful at breaking the offended pride of high-spirited women.

children.text: himavyapāyād viśadādharāṇām āpāṇḍurībhūtamukhacchavīnām
children.translated_text: Because the snow had departed, for the kiṃpuruṣa women, whose lips were clear and whose facial luster had grown pale,

children.text: svedodgamaḥ kiṃpuruṣāṅganānāṃ cakre padaṃ patraviśeṣakeṣu ||
children.translated_text: the arising of sweat took the place of decorative leaf-patterns.

children.text: tapasvinaḥ sthāṇuvanaukasas tām ākālikīṃ vīkṣya madhupravṛttim
children.translated_text: Seeing that untimely activity of Spring in <s>Sthāṇu</s>'s grove, the ascetics

children.text: prayatnasaṃstambhitavikriyāṇāṃ kathaṃcid īśā manasāṃ babhūvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose reactions were checked with effort somehow remained masters of their minds.

children.text: taṃ deśam āropitapuṣpacāpe ratidvitīye madane prapanne
children.translated_text: When <s>Madana</s>, with <s>Rati</s> as his second, entered that region with his flower-bow strung,

children.text: kāṣṭhāgatasneharasānuviddhaṃ dvandvāni bhāvaṃ kriyayā vivavruḥ ||
children.translated_text: the pairs there revealed their feeling through action, as if saturated with the sap of affection that had reached its full maturity.

children.text: madhu dvirephaḥ kusumaikapātre papau priyāṃ svām anuvartamānaḥ
children.translated_text: The bee drank honey from the same flower-cup, following his own beloved,

children.text: śṛṅgeṇa ca sparśanimīlitākṣīṃ mṛgīm akaṇḍūyata kṛṣṇasāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the black antelope scratched the doe with his horn, while her eyes closed at his touch.

children.text: dadau rasāt paṅkajareṇugandhi gajāya gaṇḍūṣajalaṃ kareṇuḥ
children.translated_text: Out of affection the female elephant gave her mate a mouthful of water fragrant with lotus pollen,

children.text: ardhopabhuktena bisena jāyāṃ saṃbhāvayāmāsa rathāṅganāmā ||
children.translated_text: and the cakravāka bird honored his wife with a lotus-fiber half enjoyed by himself.

children.text: gītāntareṣu śramavārileśaiḥ kiṃcitsamucchvāsitapatralekham
children.translated_text: During the pauses in song, while the painted leaf-pattern on her face was slightly raised by drops of sweat,

children.text: puṣpāsavāghūrṇitanetraśobhi priyāmukhaṃ kiṃpuruṣaś cucumbe ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s> kissed his beloved's face, beautiful with eyes rolling from flower-wine.

children.text: paryāptapuṣpastabakastanābhyaḥ sphuratpravālauṣṭhamanoharābhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Even the trees, from their creeper-brides whose breasts were full clusters of flowers and whose quivering coral lips were lovely,

children.text: latāvadhūbhyas taravo 'py avāpur vinamraśākhābhujabandhanāni ||
children.translated_text: received embraces from branch-arms bent low around them.

children.text: śrutāpsarogītir api kṣaṇe 'smin haraḥ prasaṃkhyānaparo babhūva
children.translated_text: Although he heard the song of the apsarases, at that moment <s>Hara</s> remained intent upon meditation;

children.text: ātmeśvarāṇāṃ na hi jātu vighnāḥ samādhibhedaprabhavo bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: for obstacles arising from the breaking of concentration never occur in those who are masters of themselves.

children.text: latāgṛhadvāragato 'tha nandī vāmaprakoṣṭhārpitahemavetraḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nandī</s>, standing at the doorway of the creeper-bower, with a golden staff resting on his left forearm,

children.text: mukhārpitaikāṅgulisaṃjñayaiva mā cāpalāyeti gaṇān vyanaiṣīt ||
children.translated_text: restrained the gaṇas merely by a sign of one finger placed upon his mouth, as if saying, 'No restlessness.'

children.text: niṣkampavṛkṣaṃ nibhṛtadvirephaṃ mūkāṇḍajaṃ śāntamṛgapracāram
children.translated_text: With its trees motionless, its bees quiet, its birds mute, and the movements of its deer stilled,

children.text: tacchāsanāt kānanam eva sarvaṃ citrārpitārambham ivāvatasthe ||
children.translated_text: at his command the whole forest stood as if its activity had been set into a painting.

children.text: dṛṣṭiprapātaṃ parihṛtya tasya kāmaḥ puraḥśukram iva prayāṇe
children.translated_text: Avoiding his line of sight, as one avoids Venus in front at the setting out on a journey, <s>Kāma</s>

children.text: prānteṣu saṃsaktanameruśākhaṃ dhyānāspadaṃ bhūtapater viveśa ||
children.translated_text: entered the meditation-place of the Lord of beings, where the nīpa branches clung along the edges.

children.text: sa devadārudrumavedikāyāṃ śārdūlacarmavyavadhānavatyām
children.translated_text: On a platform around a devadāru tree, covered with a tiger-skin spread,

children.text: āsīnam āsannaśarīrapātas tryambakaṃ saṃyaminaṃ dadarśa ||
children.translated_text: he saw <s>Tryambaka</s>, the self-restrained one, seated with his body close to being laid aside.

children.text: paryaṅkabandhasthirapūrvakāyam ṛjvāyataṃ saṃnamitobhayāṃsam
children.translated_text: His lower body was firm in the lotus posture, his trunk straight and extended, both shoulders drawn in,

children.text: uttānapāṇidvayasaṃniveśāt praphullarājīvam ivāṅkamadhye ||
children.translated_text: and because his two upturned hands were placed there, his lap seemed to hold a fully blossomed lotus.

children.text: bhujaṃgamonnaddhajaṭākalāpaṃ karṇāvasaktadviguṇākṣasūtram
children.translated_text: He wore his mass of matted hair bound up by serpents, and a double rosary hanging at his ear,

children.text: kaṇṭhaprabhāsaṅgaviśeṣanīlāṃ kṛṣṇatvacaṃ granthimatīṃ dadhānam ||
children.translated_text: and a knotted black hide made especially dark by the contact of the radiance of his throat.

children.text: kiṃcitprakāśastimitogratārair bhrūvikriyāyāṃ virataprasaṅgaiḥ
children.translated_text: With eyes whose fierce pupils were slightly visible and motionless, no longer engaged in the movement of the brows,

children.text: netrair avispanditapakṣmamālair lakṣyīkṛtaghrāṇam adhomayūkhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with rows of lashes unstirring and downward rays fixed upon the tip of his nose,

children.text: avṛṣṭisaṃrambham ivāmbuvāham apām ivādhāram anuttaraṅgam
children.translated_text: like a rain-cloud with no impulse to pour, like a reservoir of water without waves,

children.text: antaścarāṇāṃ marutāṃ nirodhān nivātaniṣkampam iva pradīpam ||
children.translated_text: like a lamp unstirred in a windless place because the inner breaths had been checked,

children.text: kapālanetrāntaralabdhamārgair jyotiḥprarohair uditaiḥ śirastaḥ
children.translated_text: with sprouts of light rising from his head, finding passage through the spaces of the skulls and eyes,

children.text: mṛṇālasūtrādhikasaukumāryāṃ bālasya lakṣmīṃ glapayantam indoḥ ||
children.translated_text: and dimming the beauty of the young moon, though it was more delicate than lotus fiber,

children.text: mano navadvāraniṣiddhavṛtti hṛdi vyavasthāpya samādhivaśyam
children.translated_text: having placed his mind in the heart, its activity barred from the nine gates and made subject to <s>samādhi</s> (absorbed concentration),

children.text: yam akṣaraṃ kṣetravido vidus tam ātmānam ātmany avalokayantam ||
children.translated_text: he was beholding within himself that self which knowers of the field know as the imperishable.

children.text: smaras tathābhūtam ayugmanetraṃ paśyann adūrān manasāpy adhṛṣyam
children.translated_text: Seeing the odd-eyed one in such a state, unassailable even by thought from nearby, <s>Smara</s>

children.text: nālakṣayat sādhvasasannahastaḥ srastaṃ śaraṃ cāpam api svahastāt ||
children.translated_text: did not notice, his hand slack with fear, that the arrow and even the bow had slipped from his own hand.

children.text: nirvāṇabhūyiṣṭham athāsya vīryaṃ saṃdhukṣayantīva vapurguṇena
children.translated_text: Then, as if kindling his power that was almost extinguished by the quality of her form,

children.text: anuprayātā vanadevatābhyām adṛśyata sthāvararājakanyā ||
children.translated_text: the daughter of the mountain-king was seen, followed by two forest goddesses.

children.text: aśokanirbhartsitapadmarāgam ākṛṣṭahemadyutikarṇikāram
children.translated_text: She wore spring-flower ornaments: aśoka that rebuked ruby, karṇikāra that drew away the luster of gold,

children.text: muktākalāpīkṛtasinduvāraṃ vasantapuṣpābharaṇaṃ vahantī ||
children.translated_text: and sinduvāra made into strings of pearls.

children.text: āvarjitā kiṃcid iva stanābhyāṃ vāso vasānā taruṇārkarāgam
children.translated_text: Wearing a garment somewhat drawn aside by her breasts and colored like the young sun,

children.text: paryāptapuṣpastabakāvanamrā saṃcāriṇī pallavinī lateva ||
children.translated_text: she was like a moving, leafing creeper bent low under abundant clusters of flowers.

children.text: srastāṃ nitambād avalambamānā punaḥ punaḥ kesaradāmakāñcīm
children.translated_text: Again and again she held up the girdle of kesara garlands slipping from her hips,

children.text: nyāsīkṛtāṃ sthānavidā smareṇa maurvīṃ dvitīyām iva kārmukasya ||
children.translated_text: as though it were a second bowstring of <s>Kāma</s>'s bow, deposited there by him who knew the proper place.

children.text: sugandhiniḥśvāsavivṛddhatṛṣṇaṃ bimbādharāsannacaraṃ dvirepham
children.translated_text: With her playful lotus she continually warded off a bee whose thirst had been increased by her fragrant breath

children.text: pratikṣaṇaṃ saṃbhramaloladṛṣṭir līlāravindena nivārayantī ||
children.translated_text: and which moved close to her bimba-red lower lip, while her glance trembled anxiously at every moment.

children.text: tāṃ vīkṣya sarvāvayavānavadyāṃ rater api hrīpadam ādadhānām
children.translated_text: Seeing her, flawless in every limb and able to bring shame even to <s>Rati</s>,

children.text: jitendriye śūlini puṣpacāpaḥ svakāryasiddhiṃ punar āśaśaṃse ||
children.translated_text: the flower-bowed god again hoped for the success of his task against the trident-bearing conqueror of the senses.

children.text: bhaviṣyataḥ patyur umā ca śaṃbhoḥ samāsasāda pratihārabhūmim
children.translated_text: And <s>Umā</s> approached the gate-place of her future husband <s>Śaṃbhu</s>;

children.text: yogāt sa cāntaḥ paramātmasaṃjñaṃ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ jyotir upārarāma ||
children.translated_text: he, after seeing through yoga the supreme light within, called the supreme self, ceased from meditation.

children.text: tato bhujaṃgādhipateḥ phaṇāgrair adhaḥ kathaṃcid dhṛtabhūmibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Īśa</s>, the portion of earth beneath him somehow held up by the hood-tips of the lord of serpents,

children.text: śanaiḥ kṛtaprāṇavimuktir īśaḥ paryaṅkabandhaṃ nibiḍaṃ bibheda ||
children.translated_text: slowly released his breath and broke the tight lotus posture.

children.text: tasmai śaśaṃsa praṇipatya nandī śuśrūṣayā śailasutām upetām
children.translated_text: Bowing down, <s>Nandī</s> reported to him that the daughter of the mountain had come for service,

children.text: praveśayāmāsa ca bhartur enāṃ bhrūkṣepamātrānumatapraveśām ||
children.translated_text: and he admitted her to her lord, her entrance permitted by the mere movement of his brow.

children.text: tasyāḥ sakhībhyāṃ praṇipātapūrvaṃ svahastalūnaḥ śiśirātyayasya
children.translated_text: After her two companions had bowed first, the handful of spring flowers plucked by her own hand,

children.text: vyakīryata tryambakapādamūle puṣpoccayaḥ pallavabhaṅgabhinnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: mixed with broken young leaves, was scattered at the feet of <s>Tryambaka</s>.

children.text: umāpi nīlālakamadhyaśobhi visraṃsayantī navakarṇikāram
children.translated_text: <s>Umā</s> too, letting slip the fresh karṇikāra that shone among her dark curls,

children.text: cakāra karṇacyutapallavena mūrdhnā praṇāmaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajāya ||
children.translated_text: made obeisance to the bull-bannered god with her head, from whose ear a young leaf had fallen.

children.text: ananyabhājaṃ patim āpnuhīti sā tathyam evābhihitā bhavena
children.translated_text: 'May you obtain a husband devoted to no one else,' she was addressed by <s>Bhava</s>, and it was the very truth.

children.text: na hīśvaravyāhṛtayaḥ kadācit puṣyanti loke viparītam artham ||
children.translated_text: For the utterances of the Lord never prosper in the world with an opposite meaning.

children.text: kāmas tu bāṇāvasaraṃ pratīkṣya pataṅgavad vahnimukhaṃ vivikṣuḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Kāma</s>, waiting for an opening for his arrow and wishing to enter the fire-mouth like a moth,

children.text: umāsamakṣaṃ harabaddhalakṣyaḥ śarāsanajyāṃ muhur āmamarśa ||
children.translated_text: with <s>Hara</s> as his fixed target before <s>Umā</s>'s eyes, repeatedly touched the string of his bow.

children.text: athopaninye giriśāya gaurī tapasvine tāmrarucā kareṇa
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gaurī</s>, with her copper-red hand, brought near to <s>Giriśa</s>, the ascetic,

children.text: viśoṣitāṃ bhānumato mayūkhair mandākinīpuṣkarabījamālām ||
children.translated_text: a rosary of seeds of the <s>Mandākinī</s> lotus, dried by the rays of the sun.

children.text: pratigrahītuṃ praṇayipriyatvāt trilocanas tām upacakrame ca
children.translated_text: And the three-eyed god began to receive it because what is offered by one who loves is dear;

children.text: saṃmohanaṃ nāma ca puṣpadhanvā dhanuṣy amoghaṃ samadhatta bāṇam ||
children.translated_text: and the flower-bowed one fitted to his bow the unfailing arrow called Bewilderment.

children.text: haras tu kiṃcit pariluptadhairyaś candrodayārambha ivāmburāśiḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Hara</s>, with his firmness somewhat impaired, like the ocean at the beginning of moonrise,

children.text: umāmukhe bimbaphalādharoṣṭhe vyāpārayāmāsa vilocanāni ||
children.translated_text: set his eyes upon <s>Umā</s>'s face, whose lower lip was like a bimba fruit.

children.text: vivṛṇvatī śailasutāpi bhāvam aṅgaiḥ sphuradbālakadambakalpaiḥ
children.translated_text: The daughter of the mountain too, revealing her feeling by limbs resembling trembling young kadamba shoots,

children.text: sācīkṛtā cārutareṇa tasthau mukhena paryastavilocanena ||
children.translated_text: stood with her lovely face turned aside and her eyes cast downward.

children.text: athendriyakṣobham ayugmanetraḥ punar vaśitvād balavan nigṛhya
children.translated_text: Then the uneven-eyed one, through self-mastery, again forcibly restrained the agitation of his senses,

children.text: hetuṃ svacetovikṛter didṛkṣur diśām upānteṣu sasarja dṛṣṭim ||
children.translated_text: and, wishing to see the cause of the disturbance in his own mind, sent his gaze toward the edges of the quarters.

children.text: sa dakṣiṇāpāṅganiviṣṭamuṣṭiṃ natāṃsam ākuñcitasavyapādam
children.translated_text: He saw the self-born one, whose fist was placed at the right corner of his eye, whose shoulder was bent, and whose left foot was drawn in,

children.text: dadarśa cakrīkṛtacārucāpaṃ prahartum abhyudyatam ātmayonim ||
children.translated_text: with his beautiful bow bent into a circle, raised up to strike.

children.text: tapaḥparāmarśavivṛddhamanyor bhrūbhaṅgaduṣprekṣyamukhasya tasya
children.translated_text: From him, whose anger had been increased by the assault on his austerity and whose face, made hard to look at by his frown,

children.text: sphurann udarciḥ sahasā tṛtīyād akṣṇaḥ kṛśānuḥ kila niṣpapāta ||
children.translated_text: a fire, flashing upward with flame, suddenly burst forth, it is said, from his third eye.

children.text: krodhaṃ prabho saṃhara saṃhareti yāvad giraḥ khe marutāṃ caranti
children.translated_text: While the voices of the wind-gods moved in the sky, crying, "Restrain your anger, lord, restrain it!"

children.text: tāvat sa vahnir bhavanetrajanmā bhasmāvaśeṣaṃ madanaṃ cakāra ||
children.translated_text: that fire, born from <s>Bhava</s>'s eye, reduced <s>Madana</s> to a remainder of ashes.

children.text: tīvrābhiṣaṅgaprabhaveṇa vṛttim mohena saṃstambhayatendriyāṇām
children.translated_text: With delusion produced by intense attachment checking the activity of her senses,

children.text: ajñātabhartṛvyasanā muhūrtaṃ kṛtopakāreva ratir babhūva ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rati</s>, not yet knowing her husband's calamity, for a moment seemed as if benefited.

children.text: tam āśu vighnaṃ tapasas tapasvī vanaspatiṃ vajra ivāvabhajya
children.translated_text: Having quickly broken down that obstacle to his austerity, as a thunderbolt breaks a tree,

children.text: strīsaṃnikarṣaṃ parihartum icchann antardadhe bhūtapatiḥ sabhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the ascetic lord of beings, wishing to avoid the company of women, disappeared together with his attendants.

children.text: śailātmajāpi pitur ucchiraso 'bhilāṣaṃ vyarthaṃ samarthya lalitaṃ vapur ātmanaś ca
children.translated_text: The mountain-born girl too, judging her high-headed father's desire and her own graceful body to be fruitless,

children.text: sakhyoḥ samakṣam iti cādhikajātalajjā śūnyā jagāma bhavanābhimukhī kathaṃcit ||
children.translated_text: and made still more ashamed before her two friends, somehow went back toward the house, empty at heart.

children.text: sapadi mukulitākṣīṃ rudrasaṃrambhabhītyā duhitaram anukampyām adrir ādāya dorbhyām
children.translated_text: At once the mountain, pitying his daughter, whose eyes were closed from fear of <s>Rudra</s>'s fury, took her in his arms,

children.text: suragaja iva bibhrat padminīṃ dantalagnāṃ pratipathagatir āsīd vegadīrghīkṛtāṅgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, bearing her like a divine elephant bearing a lotus caught on its tusk, went back along the path with his body lengthened by haste.

children.text: Chapter 4
atha mohaparāyaṇā satī vivaśā kāmavadhūr vibodhitā
children.translated_text: Then the virtuous wife, the bride of <s>Kāma</s>, wholly given over to bewilderment and helpless, was awakened

children.text: vidhinā pratipādayiṣyatā navavaidhavyam asahyavedanam ||
children.translated_text: by fate, which was about to assign to her the unbearable pain of fresh widowhood.

children.text: avadhānapare cakāra sā pralayāntonmiṣite vilocane
children.translated_text: Intent on attention, she opened her eyes, as if opening at the end of a cosmic dissolution;

children.text: na viveda tayor atṛptayoḥ priyam atyantaviluptadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: but with those two unsatisfied eyes she did not recognize her beloved, whose sight had been utterly lost.

children.text: ayi jīvitanātha jīvasīty abhidhāyotthitayā tayā puraḥ
children.translated_text: After rising and saying, "Ah, lord of my life, are you alive?"

children.text: dadṛśe puruṣākṛti kṣitau harakopānalabhasma kevalam ||
children.translated_text: she saw before her on the ground only ashes from the fire of <s>Hara</s>'s anger, in the shape of a man.

children.text: atha sā punar eva vihvalā vasudhāliṅganadhūsarastanī
children.translated_text: Then, bewildered once again, with her breasts greyed by embracing the earth,

children.text: vilalāpa vikīrṇamūrdhajā samaduḥkhām iva kurvatī sthalīm ||
children.translated_text: she lamented, her hair disheveled, as if making the ground share her sorrow.

children.text: upamānam abhūd vilāsināṃ karaṇaṃ yat tava kāntimattayā
children.translated_text: That body of yours, which by its beauty served as the standard of comparison for graceful lovers,

children.text: tad idaṃ gatam īdṛśīṃ daśāṃ na vidīrye kaṭhināḥ khalu striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has come to such a state as this; that I do not split apart shows that women are indeed hard-hearted.

children.text: kva nu māṃ tvadadhīnajīvitāṃ vinikīrya kṣaṇabhinnasauhṛdaḥ
children.translated_text: Where have you run off to, scattering me, whose life depends on you, with your affection broken in a moment,

children.text: nalinīṃ kṣatasetubandhano jalasaṃghāta ivāsi vidrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like a mass of water whose bank has been breached, leaving a lotus-bed behind?

children.text: kṛtavān asi vipriyaṃ na me pratikūlaṃ na ca te mayā kṛtam
children.translated_text: You have done me no wrong, nor has anything hostile been done to you by me;

children.text: kim akāraṇam eva darśanaṃ vilapantyai rataye na dīyate ||
children.translated_text: why, for no reason at all, is your sight not granted to <s>Rati</s> as she laments?

children.text: smarasi smara mekhalāguṇair uta gotraskhaliteṣu bandhanam
children.translated_text: Do you remember, <s>Smara</s>, the binding with girdle-strings when names were misspoken,

children.text: cyutakeśaradūṣitekṣaṇāny avataṃsotpalatāḍanāni vā ||
children.translated_text: or the blows from ear-lotuses whose filaments had fallen and soiled the eyes?

children.text: hṛdaye vasasīti matpriyaṃ yad avocas tad avaimi kaitavam
children.translated_text: When you said what was dear to me, "You dwell in my heart," I now know that to be deceit;

children.text: upacārapadaṃ na ced idaṃ tvam anaṅgaḥ katham akṣatā ratiḥ ||
children.translated_text: unless this was only a conventional phrase, how are you bodiless while <s>Rati</s> remains unwounded?

children.text: paralokanavapravāsinaḥ pratipatsye padavīm ahaṃ tava
children.translated_text: I shall follow your path, you who are newly gone abroad to the other world;

children.text: vidhinā jana eṣa vañcitas tvadadhīnaṃ khalu dehināṃ sukham ||
children.translated_text: this person has been deceived by fate, for the happiness of embodied beings truly depends on you.

children.text: rajanītimirāvaguṇṭhite puramārge ghanaśabdaviklavāḥ
children.translated_text: On city roads veiled in the darkness of night, when women are frightened by the sound of clouds,

children.text: vasatiṃ priya kāmināṃ priyās tvad ṛte prāpayituṃ ka īśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: who, beloved, except you has the power to bring lovers' beloved women to their dwellings?
