children.text: nayanāny aruṇāni ghūrṇayan vacanāni skhalayan pade pade
children.translated_text: Rolling their reddened eyes and stumbling over their words at every step,

children.text: asati tvayi vāruṇīmadaḥ pramadānām adhunā viḍambanā ||
children.translated_text: the wine-intoxication of women, with you absent, is now only a mockery.

children.text: avagamya kathīkṛtaṃ vapuḥ priyabandhos tava niṣphalodayaḥ
children.translated_text: When it understands that your body, dear friend, has become a mere tale, its rise becomes fruitless;

children.text: bahule 'pi gate niśākaras tanutāṃ duḥkham anaṅga mokṣyati ||
children.translated_text: even when the bright fortnight has passed, the moon, O bodiless one, will release sorrow into thinness.

children.text: haritāruṇacārubandhanaḥ kalapuṃskokilaśabdasūcitaḥ
children.translated_text: With charming green and red stalk, announced by the sweet sound of male cuckoos,

children.text: vada saṃprati kasya bāṇatāṃ navacūtaprasavo gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: tell me, into whose arrowhood will the fresh mango blossom now pass?

children.text: alipaṅktir anekaśas tvayā guṇakṛtye dhanuṣo niyojitā
children.translated_text: This row of bees, many times appointed by you to serve as the string of your bow,

children.text: virutaiḥ karuṇasvanair iyaṃ guruśokām anuroditīva mām ||
children.translated_text: with its cries of pitiful sound seems to be weeping along with me in my heavy grief.

children.text: pratipadya manoharaṃ vapuḥ punar apy ādiśa tāvad utthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Take on your lovely body and rise again; then command me once more.

children.text: ratidūtipadeṣu kokilāṃ madhurālāpanisargapaṇḍitām ||
children.translated_text: remember the cuckoo, naturally skilled in sweet speech, in the role of <s>Rati</s>'s messenger;

children.text: śirasā praṇipatya yācitāny upagūḍhāni savepathūni ca
children.translated_text: remember the embraces begged for with bowed head, and trembling,

children.text: suratāni ca tāni te rahaḥ smara saṃsmṛtya na śāntir asti me ||
children.translated_text: and those secret acts of love of yours; remembering them, I have no peace.

children.text: racitaṃ ratipaṇḍita tvayā svayam aṅgeṣu mamedam ārtavam
children.translated_text: O expert in love, this seasonal flower-adornment has been arranged by you yourself upon my limbs,

children.text: dhriyate kusumaprasādhanaṃ tava tac cāru vapur na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: and it remains there, but that lovely body of yours is not seen.

children.text: vibudhair asi yasya dāruṇair asamāpte parikarmaṇi smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Since you, though your decoration was not complete, were remembered by the cruel gods,

children.text: tam imaṃ kuru dakṣiṇetaraṃ caraṇaṃ nirmitarāgam ehi me ||
children.translated_text: come to me and make this left foot of mine red with lac.

children.text: aham etya pataṅgavartmanā punar aṅkāśrayiṇī bhavāmi te
children.translated_text: I shall come by the path of the sun and again become one who rests in your lap,

children.text: caturaiḥ surakāminījanaiḥ priya yāvan na vilobhyase divi ||
children.translated_text: before, my beloved, you are enticed in heaven by clever women of the gods.

children.text: madanena vinākṛtā ratiḥ kṣaṇamātraṃ kila jīviteti me
children.translated_text: It is settled as a saying of mine that <s>Rati</s>, deprived of <s>Madana</s>, lives only for a single moment,

children.text: vacanīyam idaṃ vyavasthitaṃ ramaṇa tvām anuyāmi yady api ||
children.translated_text: although, my lover, I am indeed following you.

children.text: kriyatāṃ katham antyamaṇḍanaṃ paralokāntaritasya te mayā
children.translated_text: How can the final adornment of you, hidden away in another world, be done by me?

children.text: samam eva gato 'sy atarkitāṃ gatim aṅgena ca jīvitena ca ||
children.translated_text: For you have gone at once to an unimagined state, both with your body and with your life.

children.text: ṛjutāṃ nayataḥ smarāmi te śaram utsaṅganiṣaṇṇadhanvanaḥ
children.translated_text: I remember your arrow being made straight, while the bow lay in your lap,

children.text: madhunā saha sasmitaṃ kathāṃ nayanopāntavilokitaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: and, together with <s>Madhu</s>, your smiling conversation and that glance from the corner of your eye.

children.text: kva nu te hṛdayaṃgamaḥ sakhā kusumāyojitakārmuko madhuḥ
children.translated_text: Where now is your heart-delighting friend <s>Madhu</s>, whose bow was fitted with flowers?

children.text: na khalūgraruṣā pinākinā gamitaḥ so 'pi suhṛdgatāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: Surely he too has not been brought by fierce wrathful <s>Pinākin</s> to the same state as his friend.

children.text: atha taiḥ paridevitākṣarair hṛdaye digdhaśarair ivārditaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, pained in heart by those syllables of lamentation as if by poisoned arrows,

children.text: ratim abhyupapattum āturāṃ madhur ātmānam adarśayat puraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Madhu</s> showed himself before <s>Rati</s>, who was desperate for help.

children.text: tam avekṣya ruroda sā bhṛśaṃ stanasaṃbādham uro jaghāna ca
children.translated_text: Seeing him, she wept intensely and struck her breast, crowded by her breasts;

children.text: svajanasya hi duḥkham agrato vivṛtadvāram ivopajāyate ||
children.translated_text: for before a kinsman grief arises as if through an opened door.

children.text: iti cainam uvāca duḥkhitā suhṛdaḥ paśya vasanta kiṃ sthitam
children.translated_text: And thus, sorrowing, she said to him: Look, <s>Vasanta</s>, at the condition of your friend,

children.text: yad idaṃ kaṇaśaḥ prakīryate pavanair bhasma kapotakarburam ||
children.translated_text: that this dove-colored ash is being scattered particle by particle by the winds.

children.text: ayi saṃprati dehi darśanaṃ smara paryutsuka eṣa mādhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, show yourself now, <s>Smara</s>; this <s>Mādhava</s> is full of longing.

children.text: dayitāsv anavasthitaṃ nṛṇāṃ na khalu prema calaṃ suhṛjjane ||
children.translated_text: Among men love is not steadfast toward beloved women, but it is certainly not fickle toward friends.

children.text: amunā nanu pārśvavartinā jagad ājñāṃ sasurāsuraṃ tava
children.translated_text: By this very one who stood at your side, the world with its gods and antigods

children.text: bisatantuguṇasya kāritaṃ dhanuṣaḥ pelavapuṣpapatriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was made obedient to your bow, whose string was a lotus-fiber and whose arrows were delicate flowers.

children.text: gata eva na te nivartate sa sakhā dīpa ivānilāhataḥ
children.translated_text: That friend of yours has gone and does not return, like a lamp struck by wind.

children.text: aham asya daśeva paśya mām aviṣahyavyasanapradūṣitām ||
children.translated_text: Look at me, like his condition itself, ruined by unbearable calamity.

children.text: vidhinā kṛtam ardhavaiśasaṃ nanu mām kāmavadhe vimuñcatā
children.translated_text: Fate did only half a slaughter, surely, in sparing me when <s>Kāma</s> was slain;

children.text: anaghāpi hi saṃśrayadrume gajabhagne patanāya vallarī ||
children.translated_text: for even a faultless creeper must fall when the supporting tree is broken by an elephant.

children.text: tad idaṃ kriyatām anantaraṃ bhavatā bandhujanaprayojanam
children.translated_text: Therefore let this service for a kinsman be performed next by you:

children.text: vidhurāṃ jvalanātisarjanān nanu māṃ prāpaya patyur antikam ||
children.translated_text: since I am widowed, send me by release into fire to my husband's side.

children.text: śaśinā saha yāti kaumudī saha meghena taḍit pralīyate
children.translated_text: Moonlight goes with the moon; lightning vanishes together with the cloud.

children.text: pramadāḥ pativartmagā iti pratipannaṃ hi vicetanair api ||
children.translated_text: That wives follow their husbands' path is accepted even by the insentient.

children.text: amunaiva kaṣāyitastanī subhagena priyagātrabhasmanā
children.translated_text: With my breasts reddened by this dear ash from my beloved's body,

children.text: navapallavasaṃstare yathā racayiṣyāmi tanuṃ vibhāvasau ||
children.translated_text: I shall lay my body in the fire as if on a bed of fresh shoots.

children.text: kusumāstaraṇe sahāyatāṃ bahuśaḥ saumya gatas tvam āvayoḥ
children.translated_text: Gentle one, you often assisted us with a bed of flowers.

children.text: kuru saṃprati tāvad āśu me praṇipātāñjaliyācitaś citām ||
children.translated_text: Now, then, quickly make for me the pyre that I request with anjali and bowing.

children.text: tadanu jvalanaṃ madarpitaṃ tvarayer dakṣiṇavātavījanaiḥ
children.translated_text: After that, speed the fire, given over by me, with fans of the southern wind;

children.text: viditaṃ khalu te yathā smaraḥ kṣaṇam apy utsahate na māṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: for you know well that <s>Smara</s> cannot bear to be without me even for a moment.

children.text: iti cāpi vidhāya dīyatāṃ salilasyāñjalir eka eva nau
children.translated_text: And when this has been done, let one single handful of water be offered for us both.

children.text: avibhajya paratra taṃ mayā sahitaḥ pāsyati te sa bāndhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That kinsman of yours, united with me, will drink it in the next world without division.

children.text: paralokavidhau ca mādhava smaram uddiśya vilolapallavāḥ
children.translated_text: And in the rite for the next world, O <s>Mādhava</s>, for <s>Smara</s>'s sake

children.text: nivapeḥ sahakāramañjarīḥ priyacūtaprasavo hi te sakhā ||
children.translated_text: cast down mango-blossom clusters with quivering shoots, for the dear mango-flower is your friend's own.

children.text: iti devavimuktaye sthitāṃ ratim ākāśabhavā sarasvatī
children.translated_text: As <s>Rati</s> stood ready for release from the gods, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, born in the sky,

children.text: śapharīṃ hradaśoṣaviklavāṃ prathamā vṛṣṭir ivānvakampata ||
children.translated_text: took pity on her, like the first rain on a fish distressed by the drying up of a lake.

children.text: kusumāyudhapatni durlabhas tava bhartā na cirād bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Wife of the flower-armed god, your husband, hard to obtain, will soon be yours again.

children.text: śṛṇu yena sa karmaṇā gataḥ śalabhatvaṃ haralocanārciṣi ||
children.translated_text: Hear by what deed he entered the state of a moth in the flame from <s>Hara</s>'s eye.

children.text: abhilāṣam udīritendriyaḥ svasutāyām akarot prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s>, with his senses aroused, formed desire for his own daughter.

children.text: atha tena nigṛhya vikriyām abhiśaptaḥ phalam etad anvabhūt ||
children.translated_text: Then, after suppressing that alteration, he was cursed by him and experienced this result.

children.text: pariṇeṣyati pārvatīṃ yadā tapasā tatpravaṇīkṛto haraḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Hara</s>, turned toward her by austerity, shall marry <s>Pārvatī</s>,

children.text: upalabdhasukhas tadā smaraṃ vapuṣā svena niyojayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: then, having attained happiness, he will appoint <s>Smara</s> to his own body again.

children.text: iti cāha sa dharmayācitaḥ smaraśāpāvadhidāṃ sarasvatīm
children.translated_text: And, being petitioned for righteousness, he spoke to <s>Sarasvatī</s>, who gives the limit of <s>Smara</s>'s curse;

children.text: aśaner amṛtasya cobhayor vaśinaś cāmbudharāś ca yonayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: both thunderbolt and nectar have their sources in the self-controlled and in clouds.

children.text: tad idaṃ parirakṣa śobhane bhavitavyapriyasaṃgamaṃ vapuḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore preserve this body, beautiful one, destined for future union with your beloved.

children.text: ravipītajalā tapātyaye punar oghena hi yujyate nadī ||
children.translated_text: For a river whose water has been drunk by the sun is joined again by a flood at the end of the hot season.

children.text: itthaṃ rateḥ kimapi bhūtam adṛśyarūpaṃ mandīcakāra maraṇavyavasāyabuddhim
children.translated_text: In this way some invisible being calmed <s>Rati</s>'s resolve set on death,

children.text: tatpratyayāc ca kusumāyudhabandhur enām āśvāsayat sucaritārthapadair vacobhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, because of that assurance, the flower-armed god's friend comforted her with words whose meanings were good and fitting.

children.text: atha madanavadhūr upaplavāntaṃ vyasanakṛśā paripālayāṃbabhūva
children.translated_text: Then <s>Madana</s>'s wife, thin from grief, waited for the end of her calamity,

children.text: śaśina iva divātanasya lekhā kiraṇaparikṣayadhūsarā pradoṣam ||
children.translated_text: like the line of the daytime moon, grey from the wasting of its rays, waiting for evening.

children.text: Chapter 5
tathā samakṣaṃ dahatā manobhavaṃ pinākinā bhagnamanorathā satī
children.translated_text: Thus, when <s>Pinākin</s> had burned <s>Manobhava</s> before her eyes, the chaste <s>Pārvatī</s>, her hopes broken,

children.text: nininda rūpaṃ hṛdayena pārvatī priyeṣu saubhāgyaphalā hi cārutā ||
children.translated_text: condemned her beauty in her heart; for loveliness bears its fruit as good fortune only among beloveds.

children.text: iyeṣa sā kartum avandhyarūpatāṃ samādhim āsthāya tapobhir ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: She wished to make her beauty not fruitless by resorting to concentration through her own austerities;

children.text: avāpyate vā katham anyathā dvayaṃ tathāvidhaṃ prema patiś ca tādṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for how else could two such things be obtained: love of that kind and a husband such as he?

children.text: niśamya caināṃ tapase kṛtodyamāṃ sutāṃ girīśapratisaktamānasām
children.translated_text: And when <s>Menā</s> heard that her daughter, her mind attached to the lord of the mountain, had set herself to austerity,

children.text: uvāca menā parirabhya vakṣasā nivārayantī mahato munivratāt ||
children.translated_text: she embraced her to her breast and spoke, trying to restrain her from the great vow of sages:

children.text: manīṣitāḥ santi gṛhe 'pi devatās tapaḥ kva vatse kva ca tāvakaṃ vapuḥ
children.translated_text: "The gods you desire are present even in the house; what place has austerity, child, and what place has your body?

children.text: padaṃ saheta bhramarasya pelavaṃ śirīṣapuṣpaṃ na punaḥ patatriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A delicate śirīṣa blossom may bear the foot of a bee, but not that of a bird."

children.text: iti dhruvecchām anuśāsatī sutāṃ śaśāka menā na niyantum udyamāt
children.translated_text: Though <s>Menā</s> instructed her daughter in this way, whose resolve was firm, she could not restrain her from her undertaking.

children.text: ka īpsitārthasthiraniścayaṃ manaḥ payaś ca nimnābhimukhaṃ pratīpayet ||
children.translated_text: Who can turn back a mind fixed firmly on its desired object, or water that is flowing down a slope?

children.text: kadācid āsannasakhīmukhena sā manorathajñaṃ pitaraṃ manasvinī
children.translated_text: Once, through the mouth of a close friend, that proud girl asked her father, who understood her wish,

children.text: ayācatāraṇyanivāsam ātmanaḥ phalodayāntāya tapaḥsamādhaye ||
children.translated_text: for permission to live in the forest, for a concentration of austerity ending only when its fruit arose.

children.text: athānurūpābhiniveśatoṣiṇā kṛtābhyanujñā guruṇā garīyasā
children.translated_text: Then, pleased by an attachment suited to her aim, and granted permission by her venerable father,

children.text: prajāsu paścāt prathitaṃ tadākhyayā jagāma gaurī śikharaṃ śikhaṇḍimat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaurī</s> went to a peacock-crested peak, afterwards famed among people by her name.

children.text: vimucya sā hāram ahāryaniścayā vilolayaṣṭipraviluptacandanam
children.translated_text: Putting off her necklace, firm in a resolve that could not be put off, whose sandal paste had been rubbed away by its swaying string,

children.text: babandha bālāruṇababhru valkalaṃ payodharotsedhaviśīrṇasaṃhati ||
children.translated_text: she tied on reddish-brown bark, like the young sun, its seams split apart by the swelling of her breasts.

children.text: yathā prasiddhair madhuraṃ śiroruhair jaṭābhir apy evam abhūt tadānanam
children.translated_text: As her face was charming with her celebrated hair, so too it became with matted locks;

children.text: na ṣaṭpadaśreṇibhir eva paṅkajaṃ saśaivalāsaṅgam api prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: a lotus shines not only with rows of bees, but even when clinging with moss.

children.text: pratikṣaṇaṃ sā kṛtaromavikriyāṃ vratāya mauñjīṃ triguṇāṃ babhāra yām
children.translated_text: For her vow she wore the triple-stranded muñja girdle, which at every moment made her hairs stand on end.

children.text: akāri tatpūrvanibaddhayā tayā sarāgam asyā rasanāguṇāspadam ||
children.translated_text: By that girdle, tied earlier, her waist became the seat of a cord endowed with passion's color.

children.text: visṛṣṭarāgād adharān nivartitaḥ stanāṅgarāgāruṇitāc ca kandukāt
children.translated_text: From lips where red dye had been abandoned and from a ball reddened by cosmetic from her breasts,

children.text: kuśāṅkurādānaparikṣatāṅguliḥ kṛto 'kṣasūtrapraṇayī tayā karaḥ ||
children.translated_text: her hand, its fingers wounded by taking up shoots of kuśa grass, was made fond of a rosary.

children.text: mahārhaśayyāparivartanacyutaiḥ svakeśapuṣpair api yā sma dūyate
children.translated_text: She who once was distressed even by her own hair-flowers fallen as she turned on a costly couch

children.text: aśeta sā bāhulatopadhāyinī niṣeduṣī sthaṇḍila eva kevale ||
children.translated_text: slept, using her creeper-like arm as a pillow, after sitting down on the bare ground alone.

children.text: punar grahītuṃ niyamasthayā tayā dvaye 'pi nikṣepa ivārpitam dvayam
children.translated_text: By her, steadfast in observance, two things seemed deposited in trust to be taken back later:

children.text: latāsu tanvīṣu vilāsaceṣṭitaṃ viloladṛṣṭaṃ hariṇāṅganāsu ca ||
children.translated_text: playful gestures among the slender creepers, and restless glances among the doe-eyed females.

children.text: atandritā sā svayam eva vṛkṣakān ghaṭastanaprasravaṇair vyavardhayat
children.translated_text: Untiring, she herself nourished the little trees with streams from pitchers shaped like breasts,

children.text: guho 'pi yeṣāṃ prathamāptajanmanāṃ na putravātsalyam apākariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: trees whose first birth, even for <s>Guha</s>, would not remove his filial tenderness.

children.text: araṇyabījāñjalidānalālitās tathā ca tasyāṃ hariṇā viśaśvasuḥ
children.translated_text: And the deer, caressed by handfuls of forest grain given by her, trusted her so much

children.text: yathā tadīyair nayanaiḥ kutūhalāt puraḥ sakhīnām amimīta locane ||
children.translated_text: that, before her friends, she measured their eyes with her own out of curiosity.

children.text: kṛtābhiṣekāṃ hutajātavedasaṃ tvaguttarāsaṅgavatīm adhītinīm
children.translated_text: The seers came to see her, bathed, with the sacred fire kindled, wearing an upper garment of bark and engaged in recitation;

children.text: didṛkṣavas tām ṛṣayo 'bhyupāgaman na dharmavṛddheṣu vayaḥ samīkṣyate ||
children.translated_text: among those grown great in dharma, age is not considered.

children.text: virodhisattvojjhitapūrvamatsaraṃ drumair abhīṣṭaprasavārcitātithi
children.translated_text: That penance-grove became pure: its former mutual hostility among opposed beings was abandoned, and guests were worshiped by trees with their desired blossoms;

children.text: navoṭajābhyantarasaṃbhṛtānalaṃ tapovanaṃ tac ca babhūva pāvanam ||
children.translated_text: within its new huts fire was kept stored up.

children.text: yadā phalaṃ pūrvatapaḥsamādhinā na tāvatā labhyam amaṃsta kāṅkṣitam
children.translated_text: When she judged that the desired fruit was not obtainable by that much concentration in former austerity,

children.text: tadānapekṣya svaśarīramārdavaṃ tapo mahat sā carituṃ pracakrame ||
children.translated_text: then, disregarding the softness of her own body, she began to perform great austerity.

children.text: klamaṃ yayau kandukalīlayāpi yā tayā munīnāṃ caritaṃ vyagāhyata
children.translated_text: She, who had tired even from playing with a ball, entered into the conduct of sages.

children.text: dhruvaṃ vapuḥ kāñcanapadmanirmitaṃ mṛdu prakṛtyā ca sasāram eva ca ||
children.translated_text: Surely her body was formed from a golden lotus, soft by nature and yet enduring.

children.text: śucau caturṇāṃ jvalatāṃ havirbhujāṃ śucismitā madhyagatā sumadhyamā
children.translated_text: In the hot season, standing in the middle of four blazing fire-eaters, she of pure smile and lovely waist

children.text: vijitya netrapratighātinīṃ prabhām ananyadṛṣṭiḥ savitāram aikṣata ||
children.translated_text: looked at the sun with no other gaze, overcoming its eye-repelling brilliance.

children.text: tathābhitaptaṃ savitur gabhastibhir mukhaṃ tadīyaṃ kamalaśriyaṃ dadhau
children.translated_text: Her face, thus heated by the rays of the sun, bore the beauty of a lotus;

children.text: apāṅgayoḥ kevalam asya dīrghayoḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ śyāmikayā kṛtaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: only at the edges of her long eyes did darkness slowly, slowly take its place.

children.text: ayācitopasthitam ambu kevalaṃ rasātmakasyoḍupateś ca raśmayaḥ
children.translated_text: Water that came of itself without asking, and the rays of the moon, whose essence is nectar,

children.text: babhūva tasyāḥ kila pāraṇāvidhir na vṛkṣavṛttivyatiriktasādhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: were, it is said, the means by which she broke her fast; she had no support beyond the way of trees.

children.text: nikāmataptā vividhena vahninā nabhaścareṇendhanasaṃbhṛtena ca
children.translated_text: Thoroughly heated by varied fire, by that which moves in the sky and by that gathered with fuel,

children.text: tapātyaye vāribhir ukṣitā navair bhuvā sahoṣmāṇam amuñcad ūrdhvagam ||
children.translated_text: at the end of summer, sprinkled by fresh waters, she released upward heat together with the earth.

children.text: sthitāḥ kṣaṇaṃ pakṣmasu tāḍitādharāḥ payodharotsedhanipātacūrṇitāḥ
children.translated_text: The first drops of rain, standing for a moment on her eyelashes, striking her lower lip, and crushed by falling on the swell of her breasts,

children.text: valīṣu tasyāḥ skhalitāḥ prapedire cireṇa nābhiṃ prathamodabindavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: slipped along her folds and after a long time reached her navel.

children.text: śilāśayāṃ tām aniketavāsinīṃ nirantarāsv antaravātavṛṣṭiṣu
children.translated_text: As she lay on stone and lived without a house during uninterrupted storms of wind and rain,

children.text: vyalokayann unmiṣitais taḍinmayair mahātapaḥsākṣya iva sthitāḥ kṣapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the nights watched her with eyes opened by lightning, as if standing witness to her great austerity.

children.text: nināya sātyantahimotkirānilāḥ sahasyarātrīr udavāsatatparā
children.translated_text: Intent on dwelling in water, she passed the nights of the cold season, when winds scattered extreme frost,

children.text: parasparākrandini cakravākayoḥ puro viyukte mithune kṛpāvatī ||
children.translated_text: compassionate before pairs of <s>cakravāka</s> birds separated and crying to one another.

children.text: mukhena sā padmasugandhinā niśi pravepamānādharapatraśobhinā
children.translated_text: At night, with her lotus-scented face, beautiful with lower-lip petals trembling...

children.text: tuṣāravṛṣṭikṣatapadmasaṃpadāṃ sarojasaṃdhānam ivākarod apām ||
children.translated_text: She made, as it were, a restoration of lotuses in the waters, whose wealth of lotuses had been damaged by showers of snow.

children.text: svayaṃviśīrṇadrumaparṇavṛttitā parā hi kāṣṭhā tapasas tayā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Again, by living on tree-leaves that had fallen of themselves, she reached the highest limit of austerity.

children.text: tad apy apākīrṇam ataḥ priyaṃvadāṃ vadanty aparṇeti ca tāṃ purāvidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When even that was scattered away, the ancient knowers call that sweet-spoken one <s>Aparṇā</s>, 'leafless.'

children.text: mṛṇālikāpelavam evamādibhir vrataiḥ svam aṅgaṃ glapayanty aharniśam
children.translated_text: Thus, day and night, by vows and the like, she wasted her own body, delicate as a lotus-fiber.

children.text: tapaḥ śarīraiḥ kaṭhinair upārjitaṃ tapasvināṃ dūram adhaś cakāra sā ||
children.translated_text: With her hard bodily practices she set far beneath her the austerity gained by other ascetics.

children.text: athājināṣāḍhadharaḥ pragalbhavāg jvalann iva brahmamayena tejasā
children.translated_text: Then a certain matted-haired ascetic, wearing an antelope-skin and carrying an āṣāḍha staff, bold in speech and blazing as if with brahmanic splendor,

children.text: viveśa kaścij jaṭilas tapovanaṃ śarīrabaddhaḥ prathamāśramo yathā ||
children.translated_text: entered the hermitage, like the first āśrama (student stage) bound in bodily form.

children.text: tam ātitheyī bahumānapūrvayā saparyayā pratyudiyāya pārvatī
children.translated_text: <s>Pārvatī</s> went forward to him as hostess, with service marked by deep respect.

children.text: bhavanti sāmye 'pi niviṣṭacetasāṃ vapurviśeṣeṣv atigauravāḥ kriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those whose minds are fixed on equality, actions of special honor are still shown toward distinctions of bodily form.

children.text: vidhiprayuktāṃ parigṛhya satkriyāṃ pariśramaṃ nāma vinīya ca kṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Having accepted the ritual welcome offered according to rule, and having for a moment removed what is called fatigue,

children.text: umāṃ sa paśyann ṛjunaiva cakṣuṣā pracakrame vaktum anujjhitakramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he looked at <s>Umā</s> with a straightforward eye and began to speak, without abandoning proper order.

children.text: api kriyārthaṃ sulabhaṃ samitkuśaṃ jalāny api snānavidhikṣamāṇi te
children.translated_text: Is fuel and kuśa grass easy for you to obtain for ritual action? Are the waters also suitable for the rite of bathing?

children.text: api svaśaktyā tapasi pravartase śarīram ādyaṃ khalu dharmasādhanam ||
children.translated_text: Are you undertaking austerity according to your own strength? For the body is indeed the primary means for accomplishing <s>dharma</s> (religious duty).

children.text: api tvadāvarjitavārisaṃbhṛtaṃ pravālam āsām anubandhi vīrudhām
children.translated_text: Does the sprout joined to these creepers, nourished by the water bent aside by you,

children.text: cirojjhitālaktakapāṭalena te tulāṃ yad ārohati dantavāsasā ||
children.translated_text: reach equality with your lip, which is pale-red from long abandonment of lac-dye?

children.text: api prasannaṃ hariṇeṣu te manaḥ karasthadarbhapraṇayāpahāriṣu
children.translated_text: Is your mind kindly disposed toward the deer, who steal the affection of the darbha grass held in your hand,

children.text: ya utpalākṣi pracalair vilocanais tavākṣisādṛśyam iva prayuñjate ||
children.translated_text: and who, lotus-eyed one, seem with their restless eyes to assume a resemblance to your own eyes?

children.text: yad ucyate pārvati pāpavṛttaye na rūpam ity avyabhicāri tad vacaḥ
children.translated_text: What is said, <s>Pārvatī</s>, that beauty is not for a sinful way of life, is an unfailing saying.

children.text: tathā hi te śīlam udāradarśane tapasvinām apy upadeśatāṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: For so, noble-looking one, your conduct has become fit to instruct even ascetics.

children.text: vikīrṇasaptarṣibaliprahāsibhis tathā na gāṅgaiḥ salilair divaś cyutaiḥ
children.translated_text: This mountain, together with its lineage, has not been so purified by the waters of <s>Gaṅgā</s>, fallen from heaven and laughing at the scattered offerings to the Seven Sages,

children.text: yathā tvadīyaiś caritair anāvilair mahīdharaḥ pāvita eṣa sānvayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as by your stainless deeds.

children.text: anena dharmaḥ saviśeṣam adya me trivargasāraḥ pratibhāti bhāvini
children.translated_text: By this, fair one, <s>dharma</s>, the essence of the three aims of life, appears especially clear to me today,

children.text: tvayā manonirviṣayārthakāmayā yad eka eva pratigṛhya sevyate ||
children.translated_text: since you, desiring an object beyond the range of the mind, have accepted and serve that one alone.

children.text: prayuktasatkāraviśeṣam ātmanā na māṃ paraṃ sampratipattum arhasi
children.translated_text: You should not regard me as a stranger, after I have received from you this special honor of hospitality,

children.text: yataḥ satāṃ saṃnatagātri saṃgataṃ manīṣibhiḥ sāptapadīnam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: because, slender-bodied one, among the good a meeting accompanied by seven steps is called friendship by the wise.

children.text: ato 'tra kiṃcid bhavatīṃ bahukṣamāṃ dvijātibhāvād upapannacāpalaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, here this person, made properly somewhat forward by the condition of being twice-born, wishes to ask you something, rich in austerity, you who are very patient,

children.text: ayaṃ janaḥ praṣṭumanās tapodhane na ced rahasyaṃ prativaktum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: if it is not a secret and you think it fit to answer.

children.text: kule prasūtiḥ prathamasya vedhasas trilokasaundaryam ivoditaṃ vapuḥ
children.translated_text: Your birth is in the family of the first creator; your body has arisen as if it were the beauty of the three worlds;

children.text: amṛgyam aiśvaryasukhaṃ navaṃ vayas tapaḥphalaṃ syāt kim ataḥ paraṃ vada ||
children.translated_text: unsearchable sovereignty and happiness are yours; your youth is fresh. Tell me, what fruit of austerity could there be beyond this?

children.text: bhavaty aniṣṭād api nāma duḥsahān manasvinīnāṃ pratipattir īdṛśī
children.translated_text: Such resolve among high-spirited women can indeed arise even from some unbearable misfortune,

children.text: vicāramārgaprahitena cetasā na dṛśyate tac ca kṛśodari tvayi ||
children.translated_text: but that is not seen in you, slender-waisted one, by a mind sent along the path of inquiry.

children.text: alabhyaśokābhibhaveyam ākṛtir vimānanā subhru kutaḥ pitur gṛhe
children.translated_text: This form cannot be overcome by unobtained grief. Whence could humiliation come in your father's house, beautiful-browed one?

children.text: parābhimarśo na tavāsti kaḥ karaṃ prasārayet pannagaratnasūcaye ||
children.translated_text: Nor is there any touching by another against you. Who would stretch out a hand toward a serpent's jewel?

children.text: kim ity apāsyābharaṇāni yauvane dhṛtaṃ tvayā vārddhakaśobhi valkalam
children.translated_text: Why have you put aside ornaments in youth and worn bark-garments that befit old age?

children.text: vada pradoṣe sphuṭacandratārake vibhāvarī yady aruṇāya kalpate ||
children.translated_text: Tell me, if night at evening, when moon and stars are bright, is suitable for the sun's redness.

children.text: divaṃ yadi prārthayase vṛthā śramaḥ pituḥ pradeśās tava devabhūmayaḥ
children.translated_text: If you seek heaven, your toil is useless; the regions of your father are themselves lands of the gods.

children.text: athopayantāram alaṃ samādhinā na ratnam anviṣyati mṛgyate hi tat ||
children.translated_text: But if you seek a husband, enough of concentration: a jewel does not search, it is searched for.

children.text: niveditaṃ niśvasitena soṣmaṇā manas tu me saṃśayam eva gāhate
children.translated_text: My thought has been revealed by my warm sigh; yet my mind enters only into doubt.

children.text: na dṛśyate prārthayitavya eva te bhaviṣyati prārthitadurlabhaḥ katham ||
children.translated_text: No one suitable to be sought by you is seen. How then will there be one difficult to obtain even after being sought?

children.text: aho sthiraḥ ko 'pi tavepsito yuvā cirāya karṇotpalaśūnyatāṃ gate
children.translated_text: Ah, some youth desired by you must be firm indeed, since your ears have long gone without their lotus-ornaments,

children.text: upekṣate yaḥ ślathalambinīr jaṭāḥ kapoladeśe kalamāgrapiṅgalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he disregards the slack-hanging matted locks, tawny like the tips of rice-shoots, on the region of your cheeks.

children.text: munivratais tvām atimātrakarśitāṃ divākarāpluṣṭavibhūṣaṇāspadām
children.translated_text: Seeing you excessively emaciated by the vows of sages, the place for ornaments scorched by the sun,

children.text: śaśāṅkalekhām iva paśyato divā sacetasaḥ kasya mano na dūyate ||
children.translated_text: like a crescent moon seen by day, whose conscious mind would not be pained?

children.text: avaimi saubhāgyamadena vañcitaṃ tava priyaṃ yaś caturāvalokinaḥ
children.translated_text: I know that your beloved has been deceived by the pride of good fortune,

children.text: karoti lakṣyaṃ ciram asya cakṣuṣo na vaktram ātmīyam arālapakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: since he does not for a long time make his own face, with its curved eyelashes, the target of your sidelong glances.

children.text: kiyac ciraṃ śrāmyasi gauri vidyate mamāpi pūrvāśramasaṃcitaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: How long, <s>Gaurī</s>, will you weary yourself? I too have austerity accumulated from a former stage of life.

children.text: tadardhabhāgena labhasva kāṅkṣitaṃ varaṃ tam icchāmi ca sādhu veditum ||
children.translated_text: With half of that, obtain the boon you desire; and I wish to know it properly.

children.text: iti praviśyābhihitā dvijanmanā manogataṃ sā na śaśāka śaṃsitum
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the twice-born one after he had entered, she could not declare what was in her mind.

children.text: atho vayasyāṃ paripārśvavartinīṃ vivartitānañjananetram aikṣata ||
children.translated_text: Then she looked at her friend standing nearby, turning toward her eyes free of collyrium.

children.text: sakhī tadīyā tam uvāca varṇinaṃ nibodha sādho tava cet kutūhalam
children.translated_text: Her friend said to that brahmacārin: Understand, holy sir, if you have curiosity,

children.text: yadartham ambhojam ivoṣṇavāraṇaṃ kṛtaṃ tapaḥsādhanam etayā vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: for what purpose this woman has made her body, like a lotus against heat, into an instrument of austerity.

children.text: iyaṃ mahendraprabhṛtīn adhiśriyaś caturdigīśān avamatya māninī
children.translated_text: This proud woman, scorning the lords of the four quarters, beginning with <s>Mahendra</s>, who possess sovereignty,

children.text: arūpahāryaṃ madanasya nigrahāt pinākapāṇiṃ patim āptum icchati ||
children.translated_text: wishes to obtain <s>Pinākapāṇi</s>, whom beauty cannot win, as her husband, because <s>Madana</s> has been restrained.

children.text: asahyahuṃkāranivartitaḥ purā purārim aprāptamukhaḥ śilīmukhaḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago, the flower-arrow which had been turned back by the unbearable roar of anger before reaching <s>Purāri</s>'s face

children.text: imāṃ hṛdi vyāyatapātam akṣaṇod viśīrṇamūrter api puṣpadhanvanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: struck this girl in the heart with a far-reaching fall, though the flower-bowed god's body had been shattered.

children.text: tadāprabhṛty unmadanā pitur gṛhe lalāṭikācandanadhūsarālakā
children.translated_text: From that time onward, maddened by love in her father's house, her curls grey with the sandal paste on her forehead,

children.text: na jātu bālā labhate sma nirvṛtiṃ tuṣārasaṃghātaśilātaleṣv api ||
children.translated_text: the young girl never found relief, even on slabs of stone covered with masses of snow.

children.text: upāttavarṇe carite pinākinaḥ sabāṣpakaṇṭhaskhalitaiḥ padair iyam
children.translated_text: When the deeds of the bearer of the <s>Pināka</s> were being described, with words faltering from throats choked by tears,

children.text: anekaśaḥ kinnararājakanyakā vanāntasaṃgītasakhīr arodayat ||
children.translated_text: she made the daughters of the kinnara king, her companions in forest song, weep again and again.

children.text: tribhāgaśeṣāsu niśāsu ca kṣaṇam nimīlya netre sahasā vyabudhyata
children.translated_text: And when only a third of the nights remained, she would close her eyes for a moment and suddenly wake,

children.text: kva nīlakaṇṭha vrajasīty alakṣyavāg asatyakaṇṭhārpitabāhubandhanā ||
children.translated_text: murmuring indistinctly, "Where are you going, blue-throated one?" while her arms embraced an unreal neck.

children.text: yadā budhaiḥ sarvagatas tvam ucyase na vetsi bhāvastham imaṃ janaṃ katham
children.translated_text: "When the wise say that you are all-pervading, how do you not know this person who has you in her heart?"

children.text: iti svahastollikhitaś ca mugdhayā rahasy upālabhyata candraśekharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the moon-crested god, drawn by her own hand, was reproached in secret by the innocent girl.

children.text: yadā ca tasyādhigame jagatpater apaśyad anyaṃ na vidhiṃ vicinvatī
children.translated_text: And when, searching for a way to attain him, the lord of the world, she saw no other means,

children.text: tadā sahāsmābhir anujñayā guror iyaṃ prapannā tapase tapovanam ||
children.translated_text: then, with us and with her elder's permission, she came to the ascetic grove to practice austerity.

children.text: drumeṣu sakhyā kṛtajanmasu svayaṃ phalaṃ tapaḥsākṣiṣu dṛṣṭam eṣv api
children.translated_text: Though the fruits are seen here on trees whose birth was brought about by my friend herself, and which witness her austerity,

children.text: na ca prarohābhimukho 'pi dṛśyate manoratho 'syāḥ śaśimaulisaṃśrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: still the desire she has, resting on the moon-crested god, is not seen even to be turning toward sprouting.

children.text: na vedmi sa prārthitadurlabhaḥ kadā sakhībhir asrottaram īkṣitām imām
children.translated_text: I do not know when that one, hard to obtain though prayed for, will come to this friend of mine, watched by her companions with tear-filled eyes,

children.text: tapaḥkṛśām abhyupapatsyate sakhīṃ vṛṣeva sītāṃ tadavagrahakṣatām ||
children.translated_text: thin from austerity, like a bull coming to a furrow damaged by the withholding of rain.

children.text: agūḍhasadbhāvam itīṅgitajñayā nivedito naiṣṭhikasundaras tayā
children.translated_text: When the beautiful lifelong celibate, who understood signs, had been told by her of a love that was not concealed,

children.text: ayīdam evaṃ parihāsa ity umām apṛcchad avyañjitaharṣalakṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he asked <s>Umā</s>, showing no sign of joy, "Ah, is this really so, or is it a joke?"

children.text: athāgrahaste mukulīkṛtāṅgulau samarpayantī sphaṭikākṣamālikām
children.translated_text: Then, placing in his forward hand, whose fingers were folded like a bud, a crystal rosary,

children.text: kathaṃcid adres tanayā mitākṣaraṃ ciravyavasthāpitavāg abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: the mountain's daughter somehow spoke a few words, after her speech had long been held back.

children.text: yathā śrutaṃ vedavidāṃ vara tvayā jano 'yam uccaiḥpadalaṅghanotsukaḥ
children.translated_text: "As you have heard, best of the knowers of the Veda, this person longs to cross beyond a lofty station.

children.text: tapaḥ kiledaṃ tadavāptisādhanaṃ manorathānām agatir na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: This austerity, they say, is the means of obtaining him; there is no impossibility for desires."

children.text: athāha varṇī vidito maheśvaras tadarthinī tvaṃ punar eva vartase
children.translated_text: Then the brahmacārin said, "<s>Maheśvara</s> is known. Yet you still remain intent on winning him.

children.text: amaṅgalābhyāsaratiṃ vicintya taṃ tavānuvṛttiṃ na ca kartum utsahe ||
children.translated_text: When I consider his delight in the practice of inauspicious things, I cannot bring myself to support your course.

children.text: avastunirbandhapare kathaṃ nu te karo 'yam āmuktavivāhakautukaḥ
children.translated_text: Since you persist in something unreal, how will this hand of yours, with its wedding bracelet fastened on,

children.text: kareṇa śaṃbhor valayīkṛtāhinā sahiṣyate tatprathamāvalambanam ||
children.translated_text: endure the first grasp of <s>Śaṃbhu</s>'s hand, around which a serpent has been made into a bracelet?

children.text: tvam eva tāvat paricintaya svayaṃ kadācid ete yadi yogam arhataḥ
children.translated_text: Consider for yourself first whether these two could ever deserve union:

children.text: vadhūdukūlaṃ kalahaṃsalakṣaṇaṃ gajājinaṃ śoṇitabinduvarṣi ca ||
children.translated_text: a bride's silk garment marked with graceful swans, and an elephant-hide dripping drops of blood.

children.text: catuṣkapuṣpaprakarāvikīrṇayoḥ paro 'pi ko nāma tavānumanyate
children.translated_text: Who else would approve your feet, marked with red lac,

children.text: alaktakāṅkāni padāni pādayor vikīrṇakeśāsu paretabhūmiṣu ||
children.translated_text: as they move over cremation grounds strewn with scattered hair, though they deserve to be scattered with heaps of flowers at crossroads?

children.text: ayuktarūpaṃ kim ataḥ paraṃ vada trinetravakṣaḥ sulabhaṃ tavāpi yat
children.translated_text: Tell me, what could be more unsuitable than this: that the chest of the three-eyed one, easy for you too to reach,

children.text: stanadvaye 'smin haricandanāspade padaṃ citābhasmarajaḥ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will place the dust of funeral ashes upon these two breasts, the proper seat of yellow sandal paste?

children.text: iyaṃ ca te 'nyā purato viḍambanā yad ūḍhayā vāraṇarājahāryayā
children.translated_text: And here is another mockery before you: when you, fit to be borne by a royal elephant, are married,

children.text: vilokya vṛddhokṣam adhiṣṭhitaṃ tvayā mahājanaḥ smeramukho bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: people will look at you mounted on an old bull and will become smiling-faced.

children.text: dvayaṃ gataṃ saṃprati śocanīyatāṃ samāgamaprārthanayā kapālinaḥ
children.translated_text: Two things have now fallen into a pitiable state because of the wish for union with the skull-bearer:

children.text: kalā ca sā kāntimatī kalāvatas tvam asya lokasya ca netrakaumudī ||
children.translated_text: that lovely digit of the digit-bearing moon, and you, the moonlight for the eyes of this world.

children.text: vapur virūpākṣam alakṣyajanmatā digambaratvena niveditaṃ vasu
children.translated_text: His body is deformed by odd eyes; his unknown birth is declared by his nakedness.

children.text: vareṣu yad bālamṛgākṣi mṛgyate tad asti kiṃ vyastam api trilocane ||
children.translated_text: Among suitors, fawn-eyed girl, what quality sought in a bridegroom exists in the three-eyed one, even when counted separately?

children.text: nivartayāsmād asadīpsitān manaḥ kva tadvidhas tvaṃ kva ca puṇyalakṣaṇā
children.translated_text: Turn your mind away from this improper desire. What likeness is there between such a man and you, marked with auspicious signs?

children.text: apekṣyate sādhujanena vaidikī śmaśānaśūlasya na yūpasatkriyā ||
children.translated_text: Good people expect a Vedic consecration at the sacrificial post, not at the cremation-ground stake."

children.text: iti dvijātau pratikūlavādini pravepamānādharalakṣyakopayā
children.translated_text: As the twice-born one spoke against him, her anger was visible from her trembling lower lip;

children.text: vikuñcitabhrūlatam āhite tayā vilocane tiryag upāntalohite ||
children.translated_text: she cast on him a sidelong glance, its brow-creeper bent and its corners reddened.

children.text: uvāca cainaṃ paramārthato haraṃ na vetsi nūnaṃ yata evam āttha mām
children.translated_text: And she said to him, "Surely you do not truly know <s>Hara</s>, since you speak of him to me in this way.

children.text: alokasāmānyam acintyahetukaṃ dviṣanti mandāś caritaṃ mahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: The dull hate the conduct of great souls, which is beyond ordinary people and has causes beyond thought.

children.text: vipatpratīkārapareṇa maṅgalaṃ niṣevyate bhūtisamutsukena vā
children.translated_text: Auspiciousness is sought by one intent on warding off misfortune, or by one eager for prosperity;

children.text: jagaccharaṇyasya nirāśiṣaḥ sataḥ kim ebhir āśopahatātmavṛttibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: what have such people, whose conduct is impaired by hope, to do with one who is the refuge of the world and free of wishes?

children.text: akiñcanaḥ san prabhavaḥ sa saṃpadāṃ trilokanāthaḥ pitṛsadmagocaraḥ
children.translated_text: Though possessing nothing, he is the source of wealth; though lord of the three worlds, he frequents the abode of the dead.

children.text: sa bhīmarūpaḥ śiva ity udīryate na santi yāthārthyavidaḥ pinākinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Though terrifying in form, he is called <s>Śiva</s>, the auspicious one. There are none who know the bearer of the <s>Pināka</s> as he really is.

children.text: vibhūṣaṇodbhāsi pinaddhabhogi vā gajājinālambi dukūladhāri vā
children.translated_text: Whether he shines with ornaments or is bound with serpents, whether he wears an elephant-hide or a silk garment,

children.text: kapāli vā syād atha venduśekharaṃ na viśvamūrter avadhāryate vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether he is a skull-bearer or wears the crescent moon on his head, the body of him whose form is the universe cannot be determined.

children.text: tadaṅgasaṃsargam avāpya kalpate dhruvaṃ citābhasmarajo viśuddhaye
children.translated_text: Having attained contact with his body, the dust of funeral ashes surely becomes fit for purity.

children.text: tathā hi nṛtyābhinayakriyācyutaṃ vilipyate maulibhir ambaraukasāṃ ||
children.translated_text: For it is smeared on the heads of the gods when it has fallen during the acts of dance and gesture.

children.text: asaṃpadas tasya vṛṣeṇa gacchataḥ prabhinnadigvāraṇavāhano vṛṣā
children.translated_text: The bull on which he rides is no poverty of his, though he has as his mounts the rutting elephants of the quarters.

children.text: karoti pādāv upagamya maulinā vinidramandārarajo'ruṇāṅgulī ||
children.translated_text: he approaches his feet with his crest, making his toes red with the pollen of wakeful mandāra flowers.

children.text: vivakṣatā doṣam api cyutātmanā tvayaikam īśaṃ prati sādhu bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: "Though you have fallen from yourself in wishing to speak blame, what you have said toward the one lord is good,

children.text: yam āmananty ātmabhuvo 'pi kāraṇaṃ kathaṃ sa lakṣyaprabhavo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: for how will he, whom even the self-born ones declare to be the cause, have an origin that can be marked?"

children.text: alaṃ vivādena yathā śrutas tvayā tathāvidhas tāvad aśeṣam astu saḥ
children.translated_text: "Enough of dispute. Let him indeed be entirely such as you have heard.

children.text: mamātra bhāvaikarasaṃ manaḥ sthitaṃ na kāmavṛttir vacanīyam īkṣate ||
children.translated_text: Here my mind rests with love as its only essence; a lover's inclination does not look to what is blameworthy."

children.text: nivāryatām āli kim apy ayaṃ baṭuḥ punar vivakṣuḥ sphuritottarādharaḥ
children.translated_text: "Friend, stop this boy somehow, for he wishes to speak again and his lower lip is quivering.

children.text: na kevalaṃ yo mahato 'pabhāṣate śṛṇoti tasmād api yaḥ sa pāpabhāk ||
children.translated_text: Not only the one who speaks ill of the great is sinful, but also the one who listens to him."

children.text: ito gamiṣyāmy athaveti vādinī cacāla bālā stanabhinnavalkalā
children.translated_text: Saying, "I shall go from here, or else...", the young girl, her bark garment split by her breasts, moved away;

children.text: svarūpam āsthāya ca tāṃ kṛtasmitaḥ samālalambe vṛṣarājaketanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but assuming his own form, <s>Śiva</s>, whose banner bears the lordly bull, smiling, took hold of her.

children.text: taṃ vīkṣya vepathumatī sarasāṅgayaṣṭir nikṣepaṇāya padam uddhṛtam udvahantī
children.translated_text: Seeing him, trembling, her body like a fresh, graceful stalk, lifting the foot she had raised to set down,

children.text: mārgācalavyatikarākuliteva sindhuḥ śailādhirājatanayā na yayau na tasthau ||
children.translated_text: the daughter of the mountain-king neither went nor stood, like a river confused by the obstruction of a mountain in its path.

children.text: adyaprabhṛty avanatāṅgi tavāsmi dāsaḥ krītas tapobhir iti vādini candramaulau
children.translated_text: When the moon-crested lord said, "From today, bending-limbed one, I am your servant, bought by your austerities,"

children.text: ahnāya sā niyamajaṃ klamam utsasarja kleśaḥ phalena hi punar navatāṃ vidhatte ||
children.translated_text: she at once cast off the fatigue born of observance; for hardship, when its fruit has come, indeed assumes freshness again.

children.text: Chapter 6
atha viśvātmane gaurī saṃdideśa mithaḥ sakhīm
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gaurī</s> sent a confidential message through her friend to the soul of the universe:

children.text: dātā me bhūbhṛtāṃ nāthaḥ pramāṇīkriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Let the lord of mountains, my giver, be made the authority."

children.text: tayā vyāhṛtasaṃdeśā sā babhau nibhṛtā priye
children.translated_text: When her message had been spoken by that friend, she shone, restrained in the presence of her beloved,

children.text: cūtayaṣṭir ivābhyāṣye madhau parabhṛtāmukhī ||
children.translated_text: like a mango shoot in spring close at hand, with a cuckoo for its mouth.

children.text: sa tatheti pratijñāya visṛjya kathamapyumām
children.translated_text: He promised, "So be it," and, somehow dismissing <s>Umā</s>,

children.text: ṛṣīñ jyotirmayān sapta sasmāra smaraśāsanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s>, chastiser of Love, remembered the seven light-filled seers.

children.text: te prabhāmaṇḍalair vyoma dyotayantas tapodhanāḥ
children.translated_text: Those ascetics, illuminating the sky with circles of radiance,

children.text: sārundhatīkāḥ sapadi prādurāsan puraḥ prabhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>Arundhatī</s>, immediately appeared before the lord.

children.text: āplutās tīramandārakusumotkiravīciṣu
children.translated_text: They had bathed in the streams of the heavenly <s>Gaṅgā</s>, whose waves were strewn with blossoms from the shore mandāra trees,

children.text: ākāśagaṅgāsrotassu diṅnāgamadagandhiṣu ||
children.translated_text: and which were fragrant with the ichor of the elephants of the quarters.

children.text: muktāyajñopavītāni bibhrato haimavalkalāḥ
children.translated_text: They wore pearl sacred threads and golden bark garments,

children.text: ratnākṣasūtrāḥ pravrajyāṃ kalpavṛkṣā ivāśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, with rosaries of jewels, seemed like wish-granting trees that had adopted the life of renunciation.

children.text: adhaḥpravartitāśvena samāvarjitaketunā
children.translated_text: They were constantly looked upon with due measure by the thousand-rayed sun,

children.text: sahasraraśminā śaśvat sapramāṇam udīkṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose horse was turned downward and whose banner was bent back.

children.text: āsaktabāhulatayā sārdham uddhṛtayā bhuvā
children.translated_text: At the calamity of dissolution they had rested, together with the earth lifted up and clinging like a creeper to his arm,

children.text: mahāvarāhadaṃṣṭrāyāṃ viśrāntāḥ pralayāpadi ||
children.translated_text: upon the tusk of the great boar.

children.text: sargaśeṣapraṇayanād viśvayoner anantaram
children.translated_text: Because they fashioned the remnant of creation immediately after the universal source,

children.text: purātanāḥ purāvidbhir dhātāra iti kīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the ancient knowers of old tradition call those ancient ones creators.

children.text: prāktanānāṃ viśuddhānāṃ paripākam upeyuṣām
children.translated_text: They were ascetics enjoying the fruits even of former austerities,

children.text: tapasām upabhuñjānāḥ phalāny api tapasvinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: which were pure and had reached full ripening.

children.text: teṣāṃ madhyagatā sādhvī patyuḥ pādārpitekṣaṇā
children.translated_text: In their midst the virtuous <s>Arundhatī</s>, her gaze fixed on her husband's feet,

children.text: sākṣād iva tapaḥsiddhir babhāse bahv arundhatī ||
children.translated_text: shone as if she were austerity's success made visible in person.

children.text: tām agauravabhedena munīṃś cāpaśyad īśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: The lord looked at her and at the sages without any distinction in honor.

children.text: strī pumān ity anāsthaiṣā vṛttaṃ hi mahitaṃ satām ||
children.translated_text: Such disregard for "woman" and "man" belongs to the noble; it is conduct that is honored among the good.

children.text: taddarśanād abhūcchaṃbhor bhūyān dārārtham ādaraḥ
children.translated_text: At the sight of her, <s>Śambhu</s>'s regard for taking a wife became greater,

children.text: kriyāṇāṃ khalu dharmyāṇāṃ satpatnyo mūlasādhanam ||
children.translated_text: for good wives are indeed the root instrument of righteous rites.

children.text: dharmeṇāpi padaṃ śarve kārite pārvatīṃ prati
children.translated_text: When even <s>dharma</s> had caused <s>Śarva</s> to take a step toward <s>Pārvatī</s>,

children.text: pūrvāparādhabhītasya kāmasyocchvāsitaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the mind of Love, afraid of its former offense, breathed again.

children.text: atha te munayaḥ sarve mānayitvā jagadgurum
children.translated_text: Then all those sages, having honored the teacher of the world,

children.text: idam ūcur anūcānāḥ prītikaṇṭakitatvacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: learned men with skin bristling from joy, spoke these words:

children.text: yad brahma samyag āmnātaṃ yad agnau vidhinā hutam
children.translated_text: "Whatever brahman has been rightly recited, whatever has been duly offered into the fire,

children.text: yac ca taptaṃ tapas tasya vipakvaṃ phalam adya naḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whatever austerity has been performed, today its ripened fruit is ours,

children.text: yad adhyakṣeṇa jagatāṃ vayam āropitās tvayā
children.translated_text: because by you, the overseer of the worlds, we have been raised

children.text: manorathasyāviṣayaṃ manoviṣayam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to be the object of your own thought, beyond the range of desire's imagining.

children.text: yasya cetasi vartethāḥ sa tāvat kṛtināṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: He in whose mind you abide is already the foremost among the successful;

children.text: kiṃ punar brahmayoner yas tava cetasi vartate ||
children.translated_text: how much more the mind of him, born from <s>Brahmā</s>, which abides in yours.

children.text: satyam arkāc ca somāc ca param adhyāsmahe padam
children.translated_text: It is true that we occupy a station higher than the sun and moon;

children.text: adya tūccaistaraṃ tasmāt smaraṇānugrahāt tava ||
children.translated_text: but today, through the favor of your remembrance, we stand still higher than that.

children.text: tvatsaṃbhāvitam ātmānaṃ bahu manyāmahe vayam
children.translated_text: We think highly of ourselves because we have been honored by you;

children.text: prāyaḥ pratyayam ādhatte svaguṇeṣūttamādaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: respect from the excellent generally creates confidence in one's own virtues.

children.text: yā naḥ prītir virūpākṣa tvadanudhyānasaṃbhavā
children.translated_text: The joy that is ours, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, born from meditation on you,

children.text: sā kim āvedyate tubhyam antarātmāsi dehinām ||
children.translated_text: how can it be reported to you? You are the inner self of embodied beings.

children.text: sākṣād dṛṣṭo 'si na punar vidmas tvāṃ vayam añjasā
children.translated_text: You have been seen directly, yet we do not know you plainly.

children.text: prasīda kathayātmānaṃ na dhiyāṃ pathi vartase ||
children.translated_text: Be gracious; tell us your nature, for you do not move on the path of intellects.

children.text: kiṃ yena sṛjasi vyaktam uta yena bibharṣi tat
children.translated_text: By which part do you manifestly create the world, or by which do you sustain it?

children.text: atha viśvasya saṃhartā bhāgaḥ katama eṣa te ||
children.translated_text: And which part of you is the destroyer of the universe?

children.text: athavā sumahaty eṣā prārthanā deva tiṣṭhatu
children.translated_text: Or else let this very great request stand aside, O god.

children.text: cintitopasthitāṃs tāvacchādhi naḥ karavāma kim ||
children.translated_text: For now command us, who have come as soon as thought of: what shall we do?"

children.text: atha mauligatasyendor viśadair daśanāṃśubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the supreme lord, increasing the slender radiance

children.text: upacinvan prabhāṃ tanvīṃ pratyāha parameśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: with the clear rays of his teeth and of the moon on his crest, replied:

children.text: viditaṃ vo yathā svārthā na me kāścit pravṛttayaḥ
children.translated_text: "You know that I have no activities for my own sake.

children.text: nanu mūrtibhir aṣṭābhir itthaṃbhūto 'smi sūcitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, by my eight forms I have been indicated to be of this nature.

children.text: so 'haṃ tṛṣṇāturair vṛṣṭiṃ vidyutvān iva cātakaiḥ
children.translated_text: I, such as I am, have been begged by the gods, injured by enemies,

children.text: ariviprakṛtair devaiḥ prasūtiṃ prati yācitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for offspring, as thirsty cātaka birds beg for rain from the lightning-bearing cloud.

children.text: ata āhartum icchāmi pārvatīm ātmajanmane
children.translated_text: Therefore I wish to take <s>Pārvatī</s> for the sake of a son of myself,

children.text: utpattaye havirbhoktur yajamāna ivāraṇim ||
children.translated_text: for the birth of the eater of oblations, as a sacrificer takes the araṇi fire-stick.

children.text: tām asmadarthe yuṣmābhir yācitavyo himālayaḥ
children.translated_text: For our sake, <s>Himālaya</s> is to be requested by you for her."

children.text: vikriyāyai na kalpante saṃbandhāḥ sadanuṣṭhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: rightly performed connections do not lead to alteration or failure.

children.text: unnatena sthitimatā dhuram udvahatā bhuvaḥ
children.translated_text: With him who is lofty, steadfast, and bears the burden of the earth,

children.text: tena yojitasaṃbandhaṃ vitta mām apy avañcitam ||
children.translated_text: know that I too, joined in relationship with him, am not deceived.

children.text: evaṃ vācyaḥ sa kanyārtham iti vo nopadiśyate
children.translated_text: 'He should be addressed thus for the sake of the maiden'--this is not something I need instruct you in;

children.text: bhavatpraṇītam ācāram āmananti hi sādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for good men declare as authoritative the conduct established by you.

children.text: āryāpy arundhatī tatra vyāpāraṃ kartuṃ arhati
children.translated_text: The noble <s>Arundhatī</s> too is fit to take part there;

children.text: prāyeṇaivaṃvidhe kārye puraṃdhrīṇāṃ pragalbhatā ||
children.translated_text: in affairs of this kind, women are generally bold and skillful.

children.text: tat prayātauṣadhiprasthaṃ siddhaye himavatpuram
children.translated_text: Therefore go to <s>Oṣadhiprastha</s>, the city of <s>Himavān</s>, for the accomplishment of the matter;

children.text: mahākośīprapāte 'smin saṃgamaḥ punar eva naḥ ||
children.translated_text: at this fall of the great <s>Kauśikī</s> let there be our meeting again.

children.text: tasmin saṃyaminām ādye jāte pariṇayonmukhe
children.translated_text: When that foremost of the self-restrained had become inclined toward marriage,

children.text: jahuḥ parigrahavrīḍāṃ prājāpatyās tapasvinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the ascetics, sons of <s>Prajāpati</s>, gave up their embarrassment about taking a wife.

children.text: tataḥ paramam ity uktvā pratasthe munimaṇḍalam
children.translated_text: Then, saying 'very well,' the circle of sages set out,

children.text: bhagavān api samprāptaḥ prathamoddiṣṭam āspadam ||
children.translated_text: and the blessed one also reached the place first appointed.

children.text: te cākāśam asiśyāmam utpatya paramarṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: And those great seers, rising up into the sword-dark sky,

children.text: āsedur oṣadhiprasthaṃ manasā samaraṃhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: reached <s>Oṣadhiprastha</s> with a speed equal to that of the mind.

children.text: alakām ativāhyeva vasatiṃ vasusaṃpadām
children.translated_text: It seemed almost to surpass <s>Alakā</s>, the dwelling-place of the wealth of the <s>Vasus</s>,

children.text: svargābhiṣyandavamanaṃ kṛtvevopaniveśitam ||
children.translated_text: as though it had been set down there after pouring out the overflow of heaven.

children.text: gaṅgāsrotaḥparikṣiptavaprāntarjvalitauṣadhi
children.translated_text: Its rampart-edge was encircled by the stream of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and gleamed with shining herbs;

children.text: bṛhanmaṇiśilāsālaṃ guptāv api manoharam ||
children.translated_text: it had great walls of jeweled stone, and was charming even though well guarded.

children.text: jitasiṃhabhayā nāgā yatrāśvā bilayonayaḥ
children.translated_text: There elephants, having conquered fear of lions, horses born from caves,

children.text: yakṣāḥ kiṃpuruṣāḥ paurā yoṣito vanadevatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Kiṃpuruṣas</s>, townsmen, women, and forest-deities dwelt.

children.text: śikharāsaktameghānāṃ vyajante yatra veśmanām
children.translated_text: There, in mansions whose tops were touched by clouds,

children.text: anugarjitasaṃdigdhāḥ karaṇair murajasvanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sounds of drums, through instruments, were hard to distinguish from answering thunder.

children.text: yatra kalpadrumair eva vilolaviṭapāṃśukaiḥ
children.translated_text: There, from wish-fulfilling trees themselves, with their fluttering branch-cloths,

children.text: gṛhayantrapatākāśrīr apaurādaranirmitā ||
children.translated_text: the splendor of house-machinery and banners was fashioned without regard for common civic artifice.

children.text: yatra sphaṭikaharmyeṣu naktam āpānabhūmiṣu
children.translated_text: There, in crystal palaces, in drinking halls at night,

children.text: jyotiṣāṃ pratibimbāni prāpnuvanty upahāratām ||
children.translated_text: the reflections of the stars attained the status of offerings.

children.text: yatrauṣadhiprakāśena naktaṃ darśitasaṃcarāḥ
children.translated_text: There, because their paths were shown at night by the light of herbs,

children.text: anabhijñās tamisrāṇāṃ durdineṣv abhisārikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: women going to secret trysts were unacquainted with darkness, even on stormy days.

children.text: yauvanāntaṃ vayo yasmin ātaṅkaḥ kusumāyudhaḥ
children.translated_text: In that city age lasted until the end of youth; Love with his flower-bow was the only disease;

children.text: ratikhedasamutpannā nidrā saṃjñāviparyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and sleep, arising from the weariness of love-play, was the only loss of consciousness.

children.text: bhrūbhedibhiḥ sakampoṣṭhair lalitāṅgulitarjanaiḥ
children.translated_text: There, by frowns, trembling lips, and graceful threatenings with fingers,

children.text: yatra kopaiḥ kṛtāḥ strīṇām ā prasādārthinaḥ priyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: women made their lovers beg for conciliation.

children.text: saṃtānakataruchāyāsuptavidyādharādhvagam
children.translated_text: And its outer pleasure-garden was fragrant <s>Gandhamādana</s>,

children.text: yasya copavanaṃ bāhyaṃ sugandhir gandhamādanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where traveling <s>Vidyādharas</s> slept in the shade of santānaka trees.

children.text: atha te munayo divyāḥ prekṣya haimavataṃ puram
children.translated_text: Then those divine sages, seeing the city of <s>Himavān</s>,

children.text: svargābhisaṃdhisukṛtaṃ vañcanām iva menire ||
children.translated_text: thought the merit aimed at heaven to be almost a deception.

children.text: te sadmani girer vegād unmukhadvāḥsthavīkṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: At the mansion of the mountain, watched by doorkeepers looking upward because of their speed,

children.text: avaterur jaṭābhārair likhitānalaniścalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: they descended, motionless like flames traced in the air by the masses of their matted hair.

children.text: gaganād avatīrṇā sā yathāvṛddhapurassarā
children.translated_text: That succession of sages, descended from the sky with the elders in front,

children.text: toyāntar bhāskarālīva reje muniparamparā ||
children.translated_text: shone like a row of suns reflected in water.

children.text: tān arghyān arghyam ādāya dūrāt pratyudyayau giriḥ
children.translated_text: Taking arghya-water for those worthy of arghya, the mountain went out from afar to meet them,

children.text: namayan sāragurubhiḥ pādanyāsair vasundharām ||
children.translated_text: bending the earth with footfalls heavy with substance.

children.text: dhātutāmrādharaḥ prāṃśur devadārubṛhadbhujaḥ
children.translated_text: His lips were coppery with minerals, he was tall, and his great arms were deodars;

children.text: prakṛtyaiva śiloraskaḥ suvyakto himavān iti ||
children.translated_text: by nature itself his chest was rock, clearly marking him as <s>Himavān</s>.

children.text: vidhiprayuktasatkāraiḥ svayaṃ mārgasya darśakaḥ
children.translated_text: With honors prescribed by rule, and himself showing the way,

children.text: sa tair ākramayāmāsa śuddhāntaṃ śuddhakarmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: he led those pure-acting sages into the inner apartments.

children.text: tatra vetrāsanāsīnān kṛtāsanaparigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: There, after they had taken seats and he had taken his own seat on a cane chair,

children.text: ity uvāceśvarān vācaṃ prāñjaliḥ pṛthivīdharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord of mountains, with joined palms, spoke these words to the lords.

children.text: apameghodayaṃ varṣam adṛṣṭakusumaṃ phalam
children.translated_text: Your sight appears to me like rain arising without clouds, like fruit from unseen blossom,

children.text: atarkitopapannaṃ vo darśanaṃ pratibhāti me ||
children.translated_text: come about unexpectedly.

children.text: mūḍhaṃ buddham ivātmānaṃ haimībhūtam ivāyasam
children.translated_text: By your favor I think myself like a fool made wise, like iron turned to gold,

children.text: bhūmer divam ivārūḍhaṃ manye bhavadanugrahāt ||
children.translated_text: like earth risen up to heaven.

children.text: adyaprabhṛti bhūtānām adhigamyo 'smi śuddhaye
children.translated_text: From today onward I am accessible for the purification of beings;

children.text: yad adhyāsitam arhadbhis taddhi tīrthaṃ pracakṣate ||
children.translated_text: for what has been occupied by the worthy is called a sacred ford.

children.text: avaimi pūtam ātmānaṃ dvayenaiva dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: I know myself purified by just two things, best of twice-born ones:

children.text: mūrdhni gaṅgāprapātena dhautapādāmbhasā ca vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by the fall of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> on my head, and by the water that has washed your feet.

children.text: jaṅgamaṃ praiṣyabhāve vaḥ sthāvaraṃ caraṇāṅkitam
children.translated_text: I think my twofold body, moving and unmoving, has received your favor in separate ways:

children.text: vibhaktānugrahaṃ manye dvirūpam api me vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the moving one is in the state of your servant, and the unmoving one is marked by your feet.

children.text: bhavatsaṃbhāvanotthāya paritoṣāya mūrchate
children.translated_text: For the delight born from your honoring me, swelling up on every side,

children.text: api vyāptadigantāni nāṅgāni prabhavanti me ||
children.translated_text: even my limbs, though extending to the ends of the directions, are not sufficient.

children.text: na kevalaṃ darīsaṃsthaṃ bhāsvatāṃ darśanena vaḥ
children.translated_text: By the sight of your radiant selves, not only has the darkness dwelling in caves been removed for me,

children.text: antargatam apāstaṃ me rajaso 'pi paraṃ tamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but also the deeper darkness within, beyond even passion's dust.

children.text: kartavyaṃ vo na paśyāmi syāc cet kiṃ nopapadyate
children.translated_text: I see no task of yours to be done; yet, if there is one, what could not be accomplished?

children.text: śaṅke matpāvanāyaiva prasthānaṃ bhavatām iha ||
children.translated_text: I suspect that your coming here is only for my purification.

children.text: tathāpi tāvat kasmiṃścid ājñāṃ me dātum arhatha
children.translated_text: Even so, please give me some command at least in some matter;

children.text: viniyogaprasādā hi kiṅkarāḥ prabhaviṣṇuṣu ||
children.translated_text: for servants gain favor from being employed by the powerful.

children.text: ete vayam amī dārāḥ kanyeyaṃ kulajīvitam
children.translated_text: Here we are, these are my wives, and this maiden is the life of my lineage;

children.text: brūta yenātra vaḥ kāryam anāsthā bāhyavastuṣu ||
children.translated_text: tell me what purpose of yours there is here, since I have no attachment to external possessions.

children.text: ity ūcivāṃs tam evārthaṃ darīmukhavisarpiṇā
children.translated_text: Having spoken that same meaning, <s>Himālaya</s> repeated it, as it were,

children.text: dvir iva pratiśabdena vyājahāra himālayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with an echo spreading through the mouths of his caves.

children.text: athāṅgirasam agraṇyam udāharaṇavastuṣu
children.translated_text: Then the seers urged <s>Aṅgiras</s>, foremost in matters requiring an example,

children.text: ṛṣayaś codayāmāsuḥ pratyuvāca sa bhūdharam ||
children.translated_text: and he replied to the mountain king.

children.text: upapannam idaṃ sarvam ataḥ param api tvayi
children.translated_text: All this is fitting in you, and even what goes beyond it is fitting;

children.text: manasaḥ śikharāṇāṃ ca sadṛśī te samunnatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the height of your mind is equal to the height of your peaks.

children.text: sthāne tvāṃ sthāvarātmānaṃ viṣṇum āhus tathā hi te
children.translated_text: They rightly call you <s>Viṣṇu</s> in an immovable form; for indeed your belly

children.text: carācarāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ kukṣir ādhāratāṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: has become the support of all beings, moving and unmoving.

children.text: gām adhāsyat kathaṃ nāgo mṛṇālamṛdubhiḥ phaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: How would the serpent have supported the earth with his hoods, soft as lotus-fibers,

children.text: ā rasātalamūlāt tvam avālambiṣyathā na cet ||
children.translated_text: if you had not been held down all the way to the very root of <s>Rasātala</s>?

children.text: acchinnāmalasaṃtānāḥ samudrormyanivāritāḥ
children.translated_text: Unbroken, stainless in their continuity, and not checked by the ocean's waves,

children.text: punanti lokān puṇyatvāt kīrtayaḥ saritaś ca te ||
children.translated_text: your glories, like your rivers, purify the worlds by their holiness.

children.text: yathaiva ślāghyate gaṅgā pādena parameṣṭhinaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is praised because of the foot of the supreme lord,

children.text: prabhaveṇa dvitīyena tathaivocchirasā tvayā ||
children.translated_text: so too, through a second source, is she praised because of you, who bear her on your head.

children.text: tiryag ūrdhvam adhastāc ca vyāpako mahimā hareḥ
children.translated_text: The greatness of <s>Hari</s>, when he rose as <s>Trivikrama</s>, spread sideways, upward, and downward;

children.text: trivikramodyatasyāsīt sa ca svābhāvikas tava ||
children.translated_text: and that same greatness is natural to you.

children.text: yajñabhāgabhujāṃ madhye padam ātasthuṣā tvayā
children.translated_text: When you took your place among the enjoyers of sacrificial shares,

children.text: uccair hiraṇmayaṃ śṛṅgaṃ sumeror vitathīkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the lofty golden peak of <s>Sumeru</s> was made false in its claim.

children.text: kāṭhinyaṃ sthāvare kāye bhavatā sarvam arpitam
children.translated_text: All hardness has been placed by you in your immovable body;

children.text: idaṃ tu bhaktinamraṃ te satām ārādhanaṃ vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: but this body of yours, bowed with devotion, is an honoring of the good.

children.text: tad āgamanakāryaṃ naḥ śṛṇu kāryaṃ tavaiva tat
children.translated_text: Therefore hear the purpose of our coming. That purpose is indeed your own task;

children.text: śreyasām upadeśāt tu vayam atrāṃśabhāginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but through the instruction of auspicious things we here become sharers in it.

children.text: aṇimādiguṇopetam aspṛṣṭapuruṣāntaram
children.translated_text: He who bears aloud the word "Lord," marked with the crescent moon,

children.text: śabdam īśvara ity uccaiḥ sārdhacandraṃ bibharti yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: endowed with powers beginning with minuteness and untouched by any other person,

children.text: kalpitānyonyasāmarthyaiḥ pṛthivyādibhir ātmani
children.translated_text: he by whom this universe is upheld in himself by earth and the other elements, whose powers are mutually arranged,

children.text: yenedaṃ dhriyate viśvaṃ dhuryair yānam ivādhvani ||
children.translated_text: as a vehicle is upheld on a road by its draught animals,

children.text: yogino yaṃ vicinvanti kṣetrābhyantaravartinam
children.translated_text: he whom yogins seek as dwelling within the field of the body,

children.text: anāvṛttibhayaṃ yasya padam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whose state the wise call free from the fear of return,

children.text: sa te duhitaraṃ sākṣāt sākṣī viśvasya karmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: that boon-giving <s>Śambhu</s>, the direct witness of the acts of the universe,

children.text: vṛṇute varadaḥ śaṃbhur asmatsaṃkrāmitaiḥ padaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: chooses your daughter, through words transferred by us.

children.text: tam artham iva bhāratyā sutayā yoktum arhasi
children.translated_text: You ought to join her to him, as meaning is joined with speech;

children.text: aśocyā hi pituḥ kanyā sadbhartre pratipāditā ||
children.translated_text: for a daughter given by her father to a worthy husband is not to be grieved for.

children.text: yāvad etāni bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca
children.translated_text: So long as these beings, both stationary and moving,

children.text: mātaraṃ kalpayanty enām īśo hi jagataḥ pitā ||
children.translated_text: regard her as their mother, the Lord is indeed the father of the world.

children.text: praṇamya śitikaṇṭhāya vibudhās tadanantaram
children.translated_text: After they have bowed to the blue-throated one, the gods thereafter

children.text: caraṇau rañjayanty asyāś cūḍāmaṇimarīcibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: will color her feet with the rays of the crest-jewels on their heads.

children.text: umā vadhūr bhavān dātā yācitāra ime vayam
children.translated_text: <s>Umā</s> is the bride, you are the giver, and we are these petitioners;

children.text: varaḥ śaṃbhur alaṃ hy eṣa tvatkulodbhūtaye vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the bridegroom is <s>Śambhu</s>. Surely this rite is enough for the prosperity of your family.

children.text: astotuḥ stūyamānasya vandyasyānanyavandinaḥ
children.translated_text: By the rite of kinship through your daughter, become the teacher of the teacher of the universe,

children.text: sutāsaṃbandhavidhinā bhava viśvaguror guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: of him who is praised though he praises none, who is venerated though he venerates no other.

children.text: evaṃ vādini devarṣau pārśve pitur adhomukhī
children.translated_text: As the divine sage was speaking thus, <s>Pārvatī</s>, at her father's side, with face lowered,

children.text: līlākamalapatrāṇi gaṇayāmāsa pārvatī ||
children.translated_text: counted the petals of her play-lotus.

children.text: śailaḥ sampūrṇakāmo 'pi menāmukham udaikṣata
children.translated_text: The mountain, though his wish was fully accomplished, looked toward <s>Menā</s>'s face;

children.text: prāyeṇa gṛhiṇīnetrāḥ kanyārthe hi kuṭumbinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for householders generally have their wives' eyes as guides in the matter of a daughter.

children.text: mene menāpi tat sarvaṃ patyuḥ kāryam abhīpsitam
children.translated_text: <s>Menā</s> too considered all that desired business to be her husband's;

children.text: bhavanty avyabhicāriṇyo bhartur iṣṭe pativratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: wives devoted to their husbands are unfailing in what their husband wishes.

children.text: idam atrottaraṃ nyāyyam iti buddhyā vimṛśya saḥ
children.translated_text: Reflecting with the thought, "This is the proper answer here," he,

children.text: ādade vacasām ante maṅgalālaṃkṛtāṃ sutām ||
children.translated_text: at the end of the speeches, took his daughter, adorned with auspicious ornaments.

children.text: ehi viśvātmane vatse bhikṣāsi parikalpitā
children.translated_text: "Come, child. You have been set apart as alms for the soul of the universe.

children.text: arthino munayaḥ prāptaṃ gṛhamedhiphalaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: The sages are the requesters; the fruit of household life has been attained by me."

children.text: etāvad uktvā tanayām ṛṣīn āha mahīdharaḥ
children.translated_text: Having said this much to his daughter, the mountain addressed the sages:

children.text: iyaṃ namati vaḥ sarvāṃs trilocanavadhūr iti ||
children.translated_text: "She, the bride of the three-eyed one, bows to you all."

children.text: īpsitārthakriyodāraṃ te 'bhinandya girer vacaḥ
children.translated_text: They approved the mountain's words, generous in fulfilling the desired purpose,

children.text: āśīrbhir edhayāmāsuḥ puraḥpākābhir ambikām ||
children.translated_text: and with blessings that had ripened before the event they made <s>Ambikā</s> prosper.

children.text: tāṃ praṇāmādarasrastajāmbūnadavataṃsakām
children.translated_text: <s>Arundhatī</s> placed her, bashful, on her lap,

children.text: aṅkam āropayāmāsa lajjamānām arundhatī ||
children.translated_text: as her golden earrings had slipped down through the respect of her bow.

children.text: tanmātaraṃ cāśrumukhīṃ duhitṛsnehaviklavām
children.translated_text: And by praising the matchless bridegroom's virtues she made her mother,

children.text: varasyānanyapūrvasya viśokām akarod guṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: tear-faced and distraught with love for her daughter, free from grief.

children.text: vaivāhikīṃ tithiṃ pṛṣṭās tatkṣaṇaṃ harabandhunā
children.translated_text: Asked at that very moment by <s>Hara</s>'s kinsman about the wedding date,

children.text: te tryahād ūrdhvam ākhyāya celuś cīraparigrahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they declared it to be after three days and departed, wearing bark garments.

children.text: te himālayam āmantrya punaḥ prekṣya ca śūlinam
children.translated_text: Having taken leave of <s>Himālaya</s> and looked again at the trident-bearing lord,

children.text: siddhaṃ cāsmai nivedyārthaṃ tadvisṛṣṭāḥ kham udyayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and having reported to him that the matter was accomplished, they were dismissed by him and rose into the sky.

children.text: paśupatir api tāny ahāni kṛcchrād agamayad adrisutāsamāgamotkaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Paśupati</s> too passed those days with difficulty, longing for union with the mountain's daughter;

children.text: kam aparam avaśaṃ na viprakuryur vibhum api taṃ yad amī spṛśanti bhāvāḥ ||
