children.translated_text: whom else would those emotions not disturb, when they touch even that mighty lord?

children.text: Chapter 7
athauṣadhīnām adhipasya vṛddhau tithau ca jāmitraguṇānvitāyām
children.translated_text: Then, when the lord of herbs was waxing and on a lunar day endowed with auspicious qualities for marriage,

children.text: sametabandhur himavān sutāyā vivāhadīkṣāvidhim anvatiṣṭhat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Himavān</s>, with his relatives assembled, performed the initiatory rite for his daughter's wedding.

children.text: vaivāhikaiḥ kautukasaṃvidhānair gṛhe gṛhe vyagrapuraṃdhrivargam
children.translated_text: With wedding festal arrangements, the groups of women were busy in every house;

children.text: āsīt puraṃ sānumato 'nurāgād antaḥpuraṃ caikakulopameyam ||
children.translated_text: through affection for the mountain, the city and the inner apartments seemed like one family.

children.text: saṃtānakākīrṇamahāpathaṃ tac cīnāṃśukaiḥ kalpitaketumālam
children.translated_text: That city, whose great roads were strewn with garlands and whose rows of banners were made of Chinese silk,

children.text: bhāsā jvalat kāñcanatoraṇānāṃ sthānāntarasvarga ivābabhāse ||
children.translated_text: shone, with the radiance of blazing golden gateways, like heaven transferred to another place.

children.text: ekaiva satyām api putrapaṅktau cirasya dṛṣṭeva mṛtotthiteva
children.translated_text: Although there was a whole line of sons, <s>Umā</s> alone, as if seen after a long time, as if risen from the dead,

children.text: āsannapāṇigrahaṇeti pitror umā viśeṣocchvasitaṃ babhūva ||
children.translated_text: became the special swelling joy of her parents, since the taking of her hand was near.

children.text: aṅkād yayāv aṅkam udīritāśīḥ sā maṇḍanān maṇḍanam anvabhuṅkta
children.translated_text: Blessings were uttered as she went from lap to lap, and she passed from one ornament to another;

children.text: saṃbandhibhinno 'pi gireḥ kulasya snehas tadekāyatanaṃ jagāma ||
children.translated_text: though the mountain's family was divided by relations, its affection went to her as its single abode.

children.text: maitre muhūrte śaśalāñchanena yogaṃ gatāsūttaraphalgunīṣu
children.translated_text: At the friendly muhūrta, when the moon-marked lunar mansion had joined the Uttaraphalgunīs,

children.text: tasyāḥ śarīre pratikarma cakrur bandhustriyo yāḥ patiputravatyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the married women among her relatives, whose husbands and sons were living, performed the adornment of her body.

children.text: sā gaurasiddhārthaniveśavadbhir dūrvāpravālaiḥ pratibhinnarāgam
children.translated_text: She adorned herself for the ceremonial bath and dressing, her color set off by fresh shoots of dūrvā grass

children.text: nirnābhikauśeyam upāttabāṇam abhyaṅganepathyam alaṃcakāra ||
children.translated_text: bearing pale mustard seeds, and wearing spotless silk and an assumed arrow.

children.text: babhau ca saṃparkam upetya bālā navena dīkṣāvidhisāyakena
children.translated_text: And the young girl, having come into contact with the fresh arrow of the consecration rite, shone

children.text: kareṇa bhānor bahulāvasāne saṃdhukṣyamāṇeva śaśāṅkalekhā ||
children.translated_text: like a digit of the moon being kindled by the sun's ray at the end of the dark fortnight.

children.text: tāṃ lodhrakalkena hṛtāṅgatailām āśyānakāleyakṛtāṅgarāgām
children.translated_text: Women led her out toward the four-sided court, her body oil removed with lodhra paste, her limbs colored with thickened kāleya,

children.text: vāso vasānām abhiṣekayogyaṃ nāryaś catuṣkābhimukhaṃ vyanaiṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and wearing a garment suitable for the ceremonial bath.

children.text: vinyastavaidūryaśilātale 'sminn aviddhamuktāphalabhakticitre
children.translated_text: On that floor paved with lapis-lazuli slabs and variegated with patterns of unpierced pearls,

children.text: āvarjitāṣṭāpadakumbhatoyāḥ satūryam enāṃ snapayāṃbabhūvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: they bathed her to the sound of instruments with water poured from tilted golden jars.

children.text: sā maṅgalasnānaviśuddhagātrī gṛhītapatyudgamanīyavastrā
children.translated_text: With her body purified by the auspicious bath and wearing the garment meant for going forth to her husband,

children.text: nirvṛttaparjanyajalābhiṣekā praphullakāśā vasudheva reje ||
children.translated_text: she shone like the earth with flowering kāśa grass after it has received the rain-water's sprinkling.

children.text: tasmāt pradeśāc ca vitānavantaṃ yuktaṃ maṇistambhacatuṣṭayena
children.translated_text: From that place, the devoted wives took her to the middle of the marriage altar, furnished with seats,

children.text: pativratābhiḥ parigṛhya ninye kﾱptāsanaṃ kautukavedimadhyam ||
children.translated_text: canopied and fitted with four jeweled pillars.

children.text: tāṃ prāṅmukhīṃ tatra niveśya tanvīṃ kṣaṇaṃ vyalambanta puro niṣaṇṇāḥ
children.translated_text: After seating the slender girl there facing east, the women sat before her and lingered for a moment,

children.text: bhūtārthaśobhāhriyamāṇanetrāḥ prasādhane saṃnihite 'pi nāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: their eyes carried away by the beauty of her true form, though the means of adornment were close at hand.

children.text: dhūpoṣmaṇā tyājitam ārdrabhāvaṃ keśāntam antaḥkusumaṃ tadīyam
children.translated_text: One woman arranged the end of her hair, whose dampness had been removed by the warmth of incense and which had flowers within it,

children.text: paryākṣipat kācid udārabandhaṃ dūrvāvatā pāṇḍumadhūkadāmnā ||
children.translated_text: into a noble knot, with a garland of pale madhūka blossoms mixed with dūrvā grass.

children.text: vinyastaśuklāguru cakrur asyā gorocanāpatravibhaṅgam aṅgam
children.translated_text: They made designs like gorocanā leaves on her limbs with white aguru laid on,

children.text: sā cakravākāṅkitasaikatāyās trisrotasaḥ kāntim atītya tasthau ||
children.translated_text: and she surpassed the beauty of the three-streamed river whose sandy banks are marked by cakravāka birds.

children.text: lagnadvirephaṃ paribhūya padmaṃ sameghalekhaṃ śaśinaś ca bimbam
children.translated_text: The beauty of her face, with its well-known curls, defeated the lotus clung to by bees

children.text: tadānanaśrīr alakaiḥ prasiddhaiś cicheda sādṛśyakathāprasaṅgam ||
children.translated_text: and the disk of the moon crossed by a line of cloud, cutting short any talk of resemblance.

children.text: karṇārpito lodhrakaṣāyarūkṣe gorocanākṣepanitāntagaure
children.translated_text: On her cheek, rough with the astringent of lodhra placed at the ear and extremely fair from a touch of gorocanā,

children.text: tasyāḥ kapole parabhāgalābhād babandha cakṣūṃṣi yavaprarohaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a barley shoot fixed all eyes by gaining a contrasting excellence.

children.text: rekhāvibhaktaś ca vibhaktagātryāḥ kiṃcinmadhūcchiṣṭavimṛṣṭarāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Her lower lip, on a body whose limbs were distinct and graceful, was marked by a line and its color was slightly rubbed with beeswax;

children.text: kāmapy abhikhyāṃ sphuritair apuṣyad āsannalāvaṇyaphalo 'dharoṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: quivering, it nourished an indescribable loveliness, as if the fruit of near-at-hand beauty.

children.text: patyuḥ śiraścandrakalām anena spṛśeti sakhyā parihāsapūrvam
children.translated_text: "Touch your husband's crescent moon on his head with this," said a friend jokingly;

children.text: sā rañjayitvā caraṇau kṛtāśīr mālyena tāṃ nirvacanaṃ jaghāna ||
children.translated_text: after reddening her feet, <s>Umā</s>, blessed, struck her silently with the garland.

children.text: tasyāḥ sujātotpalapatrakānte prasādhikābhir nayane nirīkṣya
children.translated_text: Looking at her eyes, beautiful like well-formed blue lotus petals, the beauticians

children.text: na cakṣuṣoḥ kāntiviśeṣabuddhyā kālāñjanaṃ maṅgalam ity upāttam ||
children.translated_text: did not apply black collyrium from any thought that the eyes lacked special beauty, but only as an auspicious mark.

children.text: sā sambhavadbhiḥ kusumair lateva jyotirbhir udyadbhir iva triyāmā
children.translated_text: She shone as ornaments were being fastened on her, like a creeper with unfolding flowers,

children.text: sarid vihaṅgair iva līyamānair āmucyamānābharaṇā cakāśe ||
children.translated_text: like night with rising stars, or like a river with birds settling down upon it.

children.text: ātmānam ālokya ca śobhamānam ādarśabimbe stimitāyatākṣī
children.translated_text: Then, seeing herself splendid in the mirror's disk, with wide motionless eyes,

children.text: haropayāne tvaritā babhūva strīṇāṃ priyālokaphalo hi veṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: she became eager for <s>Hara</s>'s arrival; for women's adornment bears its fruit in the sight of the beloved.

children.text: athāṅgulibhyāṃ haritālam ārdraṃ māṅgalyam ādāya manaḥśilāṃ ca
children.translated_text: Then her mother, taking moist haritāla and auspicious manaḥśilā with her fingers,

children.text: karṇāvasaktāmaladantapatraṃ mātā tadīyaṃ mukham unnamayya ||
children.translated_text: and lifting up her daughter's face, from which a spotless ivory leaf hung at the ear,

children.text: umāstanodbhedam anupravṛddho manoratho yaḥ prathamo babhūva
children.translated_text: made, somehow, as the marriage-consecration tilaka of her daughter, that very first desire

children.text: tam eva menā duhituḥ kathaṃcid vivāhadīkṣātilakaṃ cakāra ||
children.translated_text: which had grown along with the budding of <s>Umā</s>'s breasts.

children.text: babandha cāsrākuladṛṣṭir asyāḥ sthānāntare kalpitasaṃniveśam
children.translated_text: With eyes clouded by tears, she tied on <s>Umā</s>'s auspicious woolen wrist-thread,

children.text: dhātryaṅgulībhiḥ pratisāryamāṇam ūrṇamayaṃ kautukahastasūtram ||
children.translated_text: set in a newly chosen place and pushed along by the nurse's fingers.

children.text: kṣīrodaveleva saphenapuñjā paryāptacandreva śarattriyāmā
children.translated_text: Like the shore of the milk ocean with heaps of foam, like an autumn night filled with moonlight,

children.text: navaṃ navakṣaumanivāsinī sā bhūyo babhau darpaṇam ādadhānā ||
children.translated_text: she shone still more, wearing a new garment of fresh linen and holding the mirror.

children.text: tām arcitābhyaḥ kuladevatābhyaḥ kulapratiṣṭhāṃ praṇamayya mātā
children.translated_text: After making her daughter, the foundation of the family, bow to the honored family deities,

children.text: akārayat kārayitavyadakṣā krameṇa pādagrahaṇaṃ satīnām ||
children.translated_text: her mother, skilled in what had to be done, had her touch the feet of virtuous women in due order.

children.text: akhaṇḍitaṃ prema labhasva patyur ity ucyate tābhir umā sma namrā
children.translated_text: "May you obtain your husband's love unbroken," they said, while <s>Umā</s> bowed;

children.text: tayā tu tasyārdhaśarīrabhājā paścātkṛtāḥ snigdhajanāśiṣo 'pi ||
children.translated_text: yet even the blessings of affectionate people were left behind by her, who was to share half of his body.

children.text: icchāvibhūtyor anurūpam adris tasyāḥ kṛtī kṛtyam aśeṣayitvā
children.translated_text: The mountain, successful, having completed all that had to be done for her in keeping with both his wish and his majesty,

children.text: sabhyaḥ sabhāyāṃ suhṛdāsthitāyāṃ tasthau vṛṣāṅkāgamanapratīkṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: remained in the assembly, where his friends were gathered, awaiting the arrival of the bull-marked lord.

children.text: tāvad varasyāpi kuberaśaile tatpūrvapāṇigrahaṇānurūpam
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, on <s>Kubera</s>'s mountain, the mothers, respectfully intent, placed before the ruler of the city

children.text: prasādhanaṃ mātṛbhir ādṛtābhir nyastaṃ purastāt puraśāsanasya ||
children.translated_text: an adornment suited to the bridegroom before that taking of the bride's hand.

children.text: tadgauravān maṅgalamaṇḍanaśrīḥ sā paspṛśe kevalam īśvareṇa
children.translated_text: Out of regard for them, the lord merely touched the splendor of auspicious ornament,

children.text: sva eva veṣaḥ pariṇetur iṣṭaṃ bhāvāntaraṃ tasya vibhoḥ prapede ||
children.translated_text: and his own attire, dear to the bridegroom, assumed a different state by his power.

children.text: babhūva bhasmaiva sitāṅgarāgaḥ kapālam evāmalaśekharaśrīḥ
children.translated_text: Ash itself became his white body cosmetic; the skull itself became the bright beauty of his crest;

children.text: upāntabhāgeṣu ca rocanāṅko gajājinasyaiva dukūlabhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the marks of yellow pigment at the edges became the fine-silk condition of his elephant hide.

children.text: śaṅkhāntaradyoti vilocanaṃ yad antarniviṣṭāmalapiṅgatāram
children.translated_text: His eye, shining within its conch-like orbit, with a spotless tawny pupil set inside,

children.text: sānnidhyapakṣe haritālamayyās tad eva jātaṃ tilakakriyāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: itself became the act of applying a haritāla tilaka, once brought into proximity with it.

children.text: yathāpradeśaṃ bhujageśvarāṇāṃ kariṣyatām ābharaṇāntaratvam
children.translated_text: When the lordly serpents were about to become other ornaments, each in its proper place,

children.text: śarīramātraṃ vikṛtiṃ prapede tathaiva tasthuḥ phaṇaratnaśobhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: only his body changed; the splendors of the jewels on their hoods remained just as they were.

children.text: divāpi niṣṭhyūtamarīcibhāsā bālyād anāviṣkṛtalāñchanena
children.translated_text: Since the moon, even by day casting forth the brightness of its rays and from youth showing no mark,

children.text: candreṇa nityaṃ pratibhinnamauleś cūḍāmaṇeḥ kiṃ grahaṇaṃ harasya ||
children.translated_text: constantly divided <s>Hara</s>'s matted crest, what need had he of a crest-jewel?

children.text: ity adbhutaikaprabhavaḥ prabhāvāt prasiddhanepathyavidher vidhātā
children.translated_text: Thus, through his power, he who was the single source of wonders and the creator of the famed procedure of costume...

children.text: ātmānam āsannagaṇopanīte khaḍge niṣaktapratimaṃ dadarśa ||
children.translated_text: He saw himself reflected, attached to the sword brought near by an attendant.

children.text: sa gopatiṃ nandibhujāvalambī śārdūlacarmāntaritorupṛṣṭham
children.translated_text: Supported by <s>Nandin</s>'s arm, he mounted the bull, whose broad back was covered with a tiger-skin,

children.text: tadbhaktisaṃkṣiptabṛhatpramāṇam āruhya kailāsam iva pratasthe ||
children.translated_text: and, its great bulk contracted by devotion to him, he set out as if ascending <s>Kailāsa</s> itself.

children.text: taṃ mātaro devam anuvrajantyaḥ svavāhanakṣobhacalāvataṃsāḥ
children.translated_text: The Mothers followed that god, their head-ornaments shaking from the agitation of their own vehicles,

children.text: mukhaiḥ prabhāmaṇḍalareṇugauraiḥ padmākaraṃ cakrur ivāntarīkṣam ||
children.translated_text: and with faces pale from the dust of their halos they made the sky like a lotus-pond.

children.text: tāsāṃ ca paścāt kanakaprabhāṇāṃ kālī kapālābharaṇā cakāśe
children.translated_text: Behind them, who had the radiance of gold, shone <s>Kālī</s>, adorned with skulls,

children.text: balākinī nīlapayodarājī dūraṃ puraḥkṣiptaśatahradeva ||
children.translated_text: like a line of blue rain-clouds with a row of cranes, after lightning has been cast far ahead.

children.text: tato gaṇaiḥ śūlabhṛtaḥ purogair udīrito maṅgalatūryaghoṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the auspicious sound of ceremonial drums, raised by the gaṇas who went before the trident-bearer,

children.text: vimānaśṛṅgāṇy avagāhamānaḥ śaśaṃsa sevāvasaraṃ surebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: penetrating the peaks of the aerial palaces, announced to the gods that the time for service had come.

children.text: upādade tasya sahasraraśmis tvaṣṭrā navaṃ nirmitam ātapatram
children.translated_text: The thousand-rayed Sun took up for him a new parasol made by <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>.

children.text: sa taddukūlād avidūramaulir babhau patadgaṅga ivottamāṅge ||
children.translated_text: With its pole not far from his garment, it shone on his head like the falling <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: mūrte ca gaṅgāyamune tadānīṃ sacāmare devam aseviṣātām
children.translated_text: And then <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>, embodied, served the god with chowries,

children.text: samudragārūpaviparyaye 'pi sahaṃsapāte iva lakṣyamāṇe ||
children.translated_text: appearing, despite the reversal of their ocean-going form, like two rivers with flights of swans.

children.text: tam anvagacchat prathamo vidhātā śrīvatsalakṣmā puruṣaś ca sākṣāt
children.translated_text: First <s>Vidhātṛ</s> followed him, and the person marked with <s>Śrīvatsa</s> himself,

children.text: jayeti vācā mahimānam asya saṃvardhayantyā haviṣeva vahnim ||
children.translated_text: increasing his greatness with the cry, "Victory!" as an oblation increases fire.

children.text: ekaiva mūrtir bibhide tridhā sā sāmānyam eṣāṃ prathamāvaratvam
children.translated_text: That single form divided itself threefold; priority and posteriority are common among them:

children.text: viṣṇor haras tasya hariḥ kadācid vedhās tayos tāv api dhātur ādyau ||
children.translated_text: sometimes <s>Hara</s> is first for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, sometimes <s>Hari</s> for him; <s>Vedhas</s> is first for those two, and they also for the creator.

children.text: taṃ lokapālāḥ puruhūtamukhyāḥ śrīlakṣaṇotsargavinītaveṣāḥ
children.translated_text: The guardians of the worlds, headed by <s>Puruhūta</s>, with garments modestly simple through the abandonment of marks of majesty,

children.text: dṛṣṭipradāne kṛtanandisaṃjñās taddarśitāḥ prāñjalayaḥ praṇemuḥ ||
children.translated_text: being shown by <s>Nandin</s> at the giving of his glance, bowed with folded hands.

children.text: kampena mūrdhnaḥ śatapatrayoniṃ vācā hariṃ vṛtrahaṇaṃ smitena
children.translated_text: He honored the lotus-born one with a nod of his head, <s>Hari</s> with speech, <s>Vṛtrahan</s> with a smile,

children.text: ālokamātreṇa surān aśeṣān saṃbhāvayāmāsa yathāpradhānam ||
children.translated_text: and all the remaining gods with a mere glance, each according to his rank.

children.text: tasmai jayāśīḥ sasṛje purastāt saptarṣibhis tān smitapūrvam āha
children.translated_text: To him the Seven Sages first uttered blessings of victory; smiling, he said to them,

children.text: vivāhayajñe vitate 'tra yūyam adhvaryavaḥ pūrvavṛtā mayeti ||
children.translated_text: "In this extended wedding-sacrifice, you have already been chosen by me as the officiating priests."

children.text: viśvāvasuprāgraharaiḥ pravīṇaiḥ saṃgīyamānatripurāvadānaḥ
children.translated_text: With skilled <s>gandharvas</s>, led by <s>Viśvāvasu</s>, singing the exploit of the destruction of <s>Tripura</s>,

children.text: adhvānam adhvāntavikāralaṅghyas tatāra tārādhipakhaṇḍadhārī ||
children.translated_text: the bearer of the fragment of the lord of stars traversed the road, across which darkness could make no change.

children.text: khe khelagāmī tam uvāha vāhaḥ saśabdacāmīkarakiṅkiṇīkaḥ
children.translated_text: His vehicle, moving playfully in the sky, bore him, with golden bells that rang aloud,

children.text: taṭābhighātād iva lagnapaṅke dhunvan muhuḥ protaghane viṣāṇe ||
children.translated_text: shaking again and again its horns on which clouds were strung, as if mud had stuck to them from striking a riverbank.

children.text: sa prāpad aprāptaparābhiyogaṃ nagendraguptaṃ nagaraṃ muhūrtāt
children.translated_text: In a moment he reached the city, free from any assault of enemies and protected by the king of mountains,

children.text: puro vilagnair haradṛṣṭipātaiḥ suvarṇasūtrair iva kṛṣyamāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as if drawn forward by golden threads, the glances of <s>Hara</s> fastened before him.

children.text: tasyopakaṇṭhe ghananīlakaṇṭhaḥ kutūhalād unmukhapauradṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Near that city, the dark-blue-throated god, looked upon by the citizens whose faces were raised in curiosity,

children.text: svabāṇacihnād avatīrya mārgād āsannabhūpṛṣṭham iyāya devaḥ ||
children.translated_text: descended from the path marked by his own arrows and went to the nearby ground.

children.text: tam ṛddhimadbandhujanādhirūḍhair vṛndair gajānāṃ giricakravartī
children.translated_text: The emperor of mountains, with troops of elephants mounted by prosperous kinsmen,

children.text: pratyujjagāmāgamanapratītaḥ praphullavṛkṣaiḥ kaṭakair iva svaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: went out to meet him, delighted at his arrival, as if with his own slopes covered with blossoming trees.

children.text: vargāv ubhau devamahīdharāṇāṃ dvāre purasyodghaṭitāpidhāne
children.translated_text: The two groups, of gods and of mountains, came together at the city gate, whose door had been opened,

children.text: samīyatur dūravisarpighoṣau bhinnaikasetū payasām ivaughau ||
children.translated_text: with sounds spreading far, like two floods of waters when a single embankment has broken.

children.text: hrīmān abhūd bhūmidharo hareṇa trailokyavandyena kṛtapraṇāmaḥ
children.translated_text: The mountain lord became bashful when <s>Hara</s>, worshiped by the three worlds, bowed to him;

children.text: pūrvaṃ mahimnā sa hi tasya dūram āvarjitaṃ nātmaśiro viveda ||
children.translated_text: for earlier, because of the great distance of his majesty, he had not known his own head to have been bent by him.

children.text: sa prītiyogād vikasanmukhaśrīr jāmātur agresaratām upetya
children.translated_text: With the beauty of his face opening from affection, he went before his son-in-law

children.text: prāveśayan mandiram ṛddham enam ā gulphakīrṇāpaṇamārgapuṣpam ||
children.translated_text: and led him into his splendid palace, while flowers from the market-streets were scattered up to the ankles.

children.text: tasmin muhūrte purasundarīṇām īśānasaṃdarśanalālasānām
children.translated_text: At that moment, among the beautiful women of the city, eager for a sight of <s>Īśāna</s>,

children.text: prāsādamālāsu babhūvur itthaṃ tyaktānyakāryāṇi viceṣṭitāni ||
children.translated_text: such gestures occurred on the rows of palaces, all other duties abandoned.

children.text: ālokamārgaṃ sahasā vrajantyā kayācid udveṣṭanavāntamālyaḥ
children.translated_text: As one woman suddenly went to the path of sight, her garland fell out as she unwound her hair;

children.text: bandhuṃ na saṃbhāvita eva tāvat kareṇa ruddho 'pi na keśapāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: she did not even finish attending to her hair-knot, though she had held it back with her hand.

children.text: prasādhikālambitam agrapādam ākṣipya kācid dravarāgam eva
children.translated_text: Another, snatching away the forepart of her foot held by her cosmetic attendant, with the lac still wet,

children.text: utsṛṣṭalīlāgatir ā gavākṣād alaktakāṅkāṃ padavīṃ tatāna ||
children.translated_text: abandoning her graceful gait, spread a trail marked with red lac all the way to the window.

children.text: vilocanaṃ dakṣiṇam añjanena saṃbhāvya tadvañcitavāmanetrā
children.translated_text: Another, having honored only her right eye with collyrium, while the left eye was cheated of it,

children.text: tathaiva vātāyanasaṃnikarṣaṃ yayau śalākām aparā vahantī ||
children.translated_text: went just so toward the window, carrying the applicator-stick.

children.text: jālāntarapreṣitadṛṣṭir anyā prasthānabhinnāṃ na babandha nīvīm
children.translated_text: Another, her gaze sent through the lattice, did not tie her lower garment, loosened by her start;

children.text: nābhipraviṣṭābharaṇaprabheṇa hastena tasthāv avalambya vāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: she stood holding the cloth with a hand bright from the ornaments sunk into her navel.

children.text: ardhācitā satvaram utthitāyāḥ pade pade durnimite galantī
children.translated_text: For one woman, who had risen hastily with her girdle half put on, it kept slipping badly at every step,

children.text: kasyāścid āsīd raśanā tadānīm aṅguṣṭhamūlārpitasūtraśeṣā ||
children.translated_text: so that then only the remaining cord rested at the base of her big toe.

children.text: tāsāṃ mukhair āsavagandhagarbhair vyāptāntarāḥ sāndrakutūhalānām
children.translated_text: The windows, their interiors filled with the wine-scented faces of those women dense with curiosity,

children.text: vilolanetrabhramarair gavākṣāḥ sahasrapatrābharaṇā ivāsan ||
children.translated_text: with their restless eyes like bees, seemed adorned with thousand-petaled lotuses.

children.text: tāvat patākākulam indumaulir uttoraṇaṃ rājapathaṃ prapede
children.translated_text: Meanwhile the moon-crested god reached the royal road, crowded with banners and provided with high gateways,

children.text: prāsādaśṛṅgāṇi divāpi kurvañ jyotsnābhiṣekadviguṇadyutīni ||
children.translated_text: making the palace-spires, even by day, doubly bright as if bathed in moonlight.

children.text: tam ekadṛśyaṃ nayanaiḥ pibantyo nāryo na jagmur viṣayāntarāṇi
children.translated_text: The women, drinking with their eyes the one sight of him, did not go to any other objects,

children.text: tathā hi śeṣendriyavṛttir āsāṃ sarvātmanā cakṣur iva praviṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: for the activity of all their remaining senses seemed to have entered wholly into sight.

children.text: sthāne tapo duścaram etadartham aparṇayā pelavayāpi taptam
children.translated_text: Rightly did delicate <s>Aparṇā</s> perform this hard-to-practice austerity for this very end.

children.text: yā dāsyam apy asya labheta nārī sā syāt kṛtārthā kimutāṅkaśayyām ||
children.translated_text: The woman who could obtain even servitude to him would be fulfilled; how much more one who obtained a place on his lap as his bed.

children.text: paraspareṇa spṛhaṇīyaśobhaṃ na ced idaṃ dvandvam ayojayiṣyat
children.translated_text: If the creator had not joined this pair, whose beauty was mutually desirable,

children.text: asmin dvaye rūpavidhānayatnaḥ patyuḥ prajānāṃ viphalo 'bhaviṣyat ||
children.translated_text: then his effort in fashioning beauty in these two, the lord of creatures' work, would have been fruitless.

children.text: na nūnam ārūḍharuṣā śarīram anena dagdhaṃ kusumāyudhasya
children.translated_text: Surely the body of the flower-weaponed <s>Kāma</s> was not burned by him in anger that had mounted high;

children.text: vrīḍād amuṃ devam udīkṣya manye saṃnyastadehaḥ svayam eva kāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I think that, from shame on seeing this god, <s>Kāma</s> himself abandoned his body.

children.text: anena saṃbandham upetya diṣṭyā manorathaprārthitam īśvareṇa
children.translated_text: O friend, through good fortune, by entering into kinship with this lord whom his wishes had sought,

children.text: mūrdhānam āli kṣitidhāraṇoccam uccaistarāṃ vakṣyati śailarājaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the mountain-king, whose head is lofty from bearing the earth, will speak with his head still higher.

children.text: ity oṣadhiprasthavilāsinīnāṃ śṛṇvan kathāḥ śrotrasukhās trinetraḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing such stories, pleasant to the ear, from the women of <s>Oṣadhiprastha</s>, the three-eyed lord

children.text: keyūracūrṇīkṛtalājamuṣṭiṃ himālayasyālayam āsasāda ||
children.translated_text: reached <s>Himālaya</s>'s palace, with handfuls of parched grain crushed to powder by his armlets.

children.text: tatrāvatīryācyutadattahastaḥ śaradghanād dīdhitimān ivokṣṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having dismounted there, with a hand given by <s>Acyuta</s>, like the radiant sun descending from an autumn cloud on a bull,

children.text: krāntāni pūrvaṃ kamalāsanena kakṣyāntarāṇy adripater viveśa ||
children.translated_text: he entered the inner courts of the mountain-lord, previously traversed by the lotus-seated <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: tam anvag indrapramukhāś ca devāḥ saptarṣipūrvāḥ paramarṣayaś ca
children.translated_text: After him came the gods headed by <s>Indra</s>, and the great seers preceded by the seven sages,

children.text: gaṇāś ca giryālayam abhyagacchan praśastam ārambham ivottamārthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the gaṇas went to the mountain's palace, like excellent purposes coming to a praiseworthy undertaking.

children.text: tatreśvaro viṣṭarabhāg yathāvat saratnam arghyaṃ madhumac ca gavyam
children.translated_text: There the Lord, seated properly on a couch, accepted the jeweled arghya and the honeyed cow-product offering,

children.text: nave dukūle ca nagopanītaṃ pratyagrahīt sarvam amantravarjam ||
children.translated_text: and the new silk garments brought by the mountain, everything except the mantras.

children.text: dukūlavāsāḥ sa vadhūsamīpaṃ ninye vinītair avarodharakṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: Clothed in silk, he was led near the bride by modest guards of the inner apartments,

children.text: velāsamīpaṃ sphuṭaphenarājir navair udanvān iva candrapādaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: like the young ocean, its rows of foam clearly shining, led near the shore by fresh moonbeams.

children.text: tayā pravṛddhānanacandrakāntyā praphullacakṣuḥkumudaḥ kumāryā
children.translated_text: By that maiden, whose face had grown bright like the moon, his eyes bloomed like kumuda lotuses,

children.text: prasannacetaḥsalilaḥ śivo 'bhūt saṃsṛjyamānaḥ śaradeva lokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Śiva</s>, his mind's water made clear, became like the world when joined with autumn.

children.text: tayoḥ samāpattiṣu kātarāṇi kiṃcidvyavasthāpitasaṃhṛtāni
children.translated_text: At their meeting, their eyes became timid, partly steadied and partly withdrawn,

children.text: hrīyantraṇāṃ tatkṣaṇam anvabhūvann anyonyalolāni vilocanāni ||
children.translated_text: and, wavering toward one another, at that moment they experienced the restraint of bashfulness.

children.text: tasyāḥ karaṃ śailagurūpanītaṃ jagrāha tāmrāṅgulim aṣṭamūrtiḥ
children.translated_text: The eight-formed lord took her hand, brought forward by the venerable mountain, its fingers copper-red,

children.text: umātanau gūḍhatanoḥ smarasya tacchaṅkinaḥ pūrvam iva praroham ||
children.translated_text: as if it were the first sprout of bodiless <s>Smara</s>, hidden in <s>Umā</s>'s body and fearing him.

children.text: romodgamaḥ prādurabhūd umāyāḥ svinnāṅguliḥ puṅgavaketur āsīt
children.translated_text: Horripilation appeared on <s>Umā</s>, and the bull-bannered lord's fingers grew moist with sweat;

children.text: vṛttis tayoḥ pāṇisamāgamena samaṃ vibhakteva manobhavasya ||
children.translated_text: through the meeting of their hands, the operation of love seemed divided equally between the two.

children.text: prayuktapāṇigrahaṇaṃ yad anyad vadhūvaraṃ puṣyati kāntim agryām
children.translated_text: If the hand-taking rite lends supreme beauty to any other bride and bridegroom,

children.text: sānnidhyayogād anayos tadānīṃ kiṃ kathyate śrīr ubhayasya tasya ||
children.translated_text: what can be said of the splendor then possessed by both of these two, through their union in nearness?

children.text: pradakṣiṇaprakramaṇāt kṛśānor udarciṣas tan mithunaṃ cakāśe
children.translated_text: As that pair began to move clockwise around the fire of upward flames, it shone

children.text: meror upānteṣv iva vartamānam anyonyasaṃsaktam ahastriyāmam ||
children.translated_text: like day and night, mutually joined, existing on the slopes of <s>Meru</s>.

children.text: tau dampatī triḥ pariṇīya vahnim karāgrasaṃsparśanimīlitākṣīm
children.translated_text: When the couple had gone three times around the fire, the priest made the bride, whose eyes were closed by the touch of his fingertips,

children.text: tāṃ kārayāmāsa vadhūṃ purodhās tasmin samiddhārciṣi lājamokṣam ||
children.translated_text: release the parched grain into that fire with its kindled flames.

children.text: sā lājadhūmāñjalim iṣṭagandhaṃ gurūpadeśād vadanaṃ nināya
children.translated_text: Following her elder's instruction, she brought to her face the handful of parched-grain smoke, fragrant from the offering;

children.text: kapolasaṃsarpiśikhaḥ sa tasyā muhūrtakarṇotpalatāṃ prapede ||
children.translated_text: as its flame crept along her cheek, it for a moment became like a blue lotus at her ear.

children.text: tad īṣadārdrāruṇagaṇḍalekham ucchvāsikālāñjanarāgam akṣṇoḥ
children.translated_text: Her bridal face, with cheek-lines slightly moist and red, with the collyrium-color of her eyes stirred by her breath,

children.text: vadhūmukhaṃ klāntayavāvataṃsam ācāradhūmagrahaṇād babhūva ||
children.translated_text: and with its barley-ornament wearied, became so through taking in the ritual smoke.

children.text: vadhūṃ dvijaḥ prāha tavaiṣa vatse vahnir vivāhaṃ prati pūrvasākṣī
children.translated_text: The brahmin said to the bride, 'Child, this fire is the first witness with regard to your marriage;

children.text: śivena bhartrā saha dharmacaryā kāryā tvayā muktavicārayeti ||
children.translated_text: you must perform <s>dharma</s>-conduct together with <s>Śiva</s> as your husband, free from hesitation.'

children.text: ālocanāntaṃ śravaṇe vitatya pītaṃ guros tadvacanaṃ bhavānyā
children.translated_text: <s>Bhavānī</s> drank in that word of the teacher, stretching her attention to the very edge of hearing,

children.text: nidāghakālolbaṇatāpayeva māhendram ambhaḥ prathamaṃ pṛthivyā ||
children.translated_text: as the earth first drinks <s>Indra</s>'s rainwater when scorched by the fierce heat of summer.

children.text: dhruveṇa bhartrā dhruvadarśanāya prayujyamānā priyadarśanena
children.translated_text: Being directed by her firm husband, lovely to behold, to look at the fixed star <s>Dhruva</s>,

children.text: sā dṛṣṭa ity ānanam unnamayya hrīsannakaṇṭhī kathamapy uvāca ||
children.translated_text: she lifted her face and, her throat sunk with bashfulness, somehow said, 'It has been seen.'

children.text: itthaṃ vidhijñena purohitena prayuktapāṇigrahaṇopacārau
children.translated_text: Thus, when the hand-taking ceremonies had been performed by the priest who knew the rite,

children.text: praṇematus tau pitarau prajānāṃ padmāsanasthāya pitāmahāya ||
children.translated_text: the two parents of creatures bowed to the grandsire seated on the lotus-seat.

children.text: vadhūr vidhātrā pratinandyate sma kalyāṇi vīraprasavā bhaveti
children.translated_text: The bride was congratulated by the creator with the words, 'Blessed lady, become the mother of a hero';

children.text: vācaspatiḥ sann api so 'ṣṭamūrttāv āśāsya cintāstimito babhūva ||
children.translated_text: though he was <s>Vācaspati</s>, he became motionless in thought when he had to pronounce a blessing upon the eight-formed lord.

children.text: kﾱptopacārāṃ caturasravedīṃ tāv etya paścāt kanakāsanasthau
children.translated_text: Afterwards the husband and wife approached the square altar with its rites arranged, and, seated on golden seats,

children.text: jāyāpatī laukikam eṣitavyam ārdrākṣatāropaṇam anvabhūtām ||
children.translated_text: they underwent the worldly rite to be performed, the sprinkling of moist unbroken rice.

children.text: patrāntalagnair jalabindujālair ākṛṣṭamuktāphalajālaśobham
children.translated_text: With networks of water-drops clinging to the tips of its leaves, lovely like a drawn net of pearls,

children.text: tayor upary āyatanāladaṇḍam ādhatta lakṣmīḥ kamalātapatram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> held above them a lotus parasol whose stalk served as a long handle.

children.text: dvidhā prayuktena ca vāṅmayena sarasvatī tan mithunaṃ nunāva
children.translated_text: And <s>Sarasvatī</s> praised that pair with speech employed in two forms:

children.text: saṃskārapūtena varaṃ vareṇyaṃ vadhūṃ sukhagrāhyanibandhanena ||
children.translated_text: the excellent bridegroom with language purified by refinement, and the bride with composition easy to understand.

children.text: tau sandhiṣu vyañjitavṛttibhedaṃ rasāntareṣu pratibaddharāgam
children.translated_text: For a while they watched the apsarases' first performance, showing changes of meter at the transitions,

children.text: apaśyatām apsarasāṃ muhūrtaṃ prayogam ādyaṃ lalitāṅgahāram ||
children.translated_text: fixed to passion in the changes of rasa, and marked by graceful movements of the limbs.

children.text: devās tadante haram ūḍhabhāryaṃ kirīṭabaddhāñjalayo nipatya
children.translated_text: At its end the gods, their joined hands bound to their crowns, fell down before <s>Hara</s>, who had taken a wife,

children.text: śāpāvasāne pratipannamūrter yayācire pañcaśarasya sevām ||
children.translated_text: and begged for the service of the five-arrowed <s>Kāma</s>, whose body would be restored at the end of the curse.

children.text: tasyānumene bhagavān vimanyur vyāpāram ātmany api sāyakānām
children.translated_text: The blessed lord, free from anger, consented to the operation of the arrows even upon himself;

children.text: kāle prayuktā khalu kāryavidbhir vijñāpanā bhartṛṣu siddhim eti ||
children.translated_text: for a petition made at the proper time by those who know their business attains success with masters.

children.text: atha vibudhagaṇāṃs tān indumaulir visṛjya kṣitidharapatikanyām ādadānaḥ kareṇa
children.translated_text: Then the moon-crested lord, having dismissed those hosts of gods and taking the daughter of the lord of mountains by the hand,

children.text: kanakakalaśarakṣābhaktiśobhāsanāthaṃ kṣitiviracitaśayyaṃ kautukāgāram āgāt ||
children.translated_text: entered the bridal chamber, furnished with a bed made on the ground and made splendid by the beauty of golden pitchers set there for protection.

children.text: navapariṇayalajjābhūṣaṇāṃ tatra gaurīṃ vadanam apaharantīṃ tatkṛtotkṣepam īśaḥ
children.translated_text: There <s>Isa</s> saw <s>Gauri</s>, adorned with the bashfulness of a newly married woman, turning her face away when he lifted it up.

children.text: api śayanasakhībhyo dattavācaṃ kathaṃcit pramathamukhavikārair hāsayāmāsa gūḍham ||
children.translated_text: Though she could scarcely speak even to her companions on the bed, he secretly made her laugh by the grimaces of the <s>pramatha</s> attendants.

children.text: Chapter 8
pāṇipīḍanavidher anantaraṃ śailarājaduhitur haraṃ prati
children.translated_text: Immediately after the rite of hand-clasping, toward <s>Hara</s>, the daughter of the mountain king

children.text: bhāvasādhvasaparigrahād abhūt kāmadohadamanoharaṃ vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: had a body charming with the longing of love because she was possessed by the trembling of emotion.

children.text: vyāhṛtā prativaco na saṃdadhe gantum aicchad avalambitāṃśukā
children.translated_text: When spoken to, she gave no answer; held by the edge of her garment, she wished to go away.

children.text: sevate sma śayanaṃ parāṅmukhī sā tathāpi rataye pinākinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even so, though she turned her face away, she served the bed for the pleasure of the wielder of <s>Pinaka</s>.

children.text: kaitavena śayite kutūhalāt pārvatī pratimukhaṃ nipātitam
children.translated_text: When he had lain down in feigned sleep, <s>Parvati</s>, from curiosity, cast her eyes upon his face.

children.text: cakṣur unmiṣati sasmitaṃ priye vidyudāhatam iva nyamīlayat ||
children.translated_text: But when her beloved opened his eyes with a smile, she shut them, as if struck by lightning.

children.text: nābhideśanihitaḥ sakampayā śaṅkarasya rurudhe tayā karaḥ
children.translated_text: With trembling, she checked <s>Sankara</s>'s hand when it was placed near her navel.

children.text: taddukūlam atha cābhavat svayaṃ dūram ucchvasitanīvibandhanam ||
children.translated_text: Then her silk garment of itself became loosened far away, its girdle-knot having breathed open.

children.text: evam āli nigṛhītasādhvasaṃ śaṅkaro rahasi sevyatām iti
children.translated_text: "In this way, friend, after mastering your fear, <s>Sankara</s> is to be served in private";

children.text: sā sakhībhir upadiṣṭam ākulā nāsmarat pramukhavartini priye ||
children.translated_text: but, bewildered with her beloved before her, she did not remember what her friends had taught her.

children.text: apy avastuni kathāpravṛttaye praśnatatparam anaṅgaśāsanam
children.translated_text: Even when the chastiser of <s>Ananga</s> was intent on questioning her, to begin conversation on some trivial matter,

children.text: vīkṣitena parigṛhya pārvatī mūrdhakampamayam uttaraṃ dadau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Parvati</s>, receiving him with a glance, gave an answer consisting only of a movement of her head.

children.text: śūlinaḥ karataladvayena sā saṃnirudhya nayane hṛtāṃśukā
children.translated_text: She covered the two eyes of the trident-bearer with both her palms after her garment had been taken away.

children.text: tasya paśyati lalāṭalocane moghayatnavidhurā rahasy abhūt ||
children.translated_text: But, while his forehead eye was looking on, she became helpless in private, her effort made vain.

children.text: cumbaneṣv adharadānavarjitaṃ sannahastam adayopagūhane
children.translated_text: In kisses she withheld the gift of her lower lip; in merciless embraces she kept her hands drawn together.

children.text: kliṣṭamanmatham api priyaṃ prabhor durlabhapratikṛtaṃ vadhūratam ||
children.translated_text: Yet, though love was tormented, the bride's love-play with her lord, hard for him to answer in kind, was dear.

children.text: yan mukhagrahaṇam akṣatādharaṃ dattam avraṇapadaṃ nakhaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: The taking of her face that left her lips uninjured, the nail mark that made no wounded place,

children.text: yad rataṃ ca sadayaṃ priyasya tat pārvatī viṣahate sma netarat ||
children.translated_text: and the love-play of her beloved that was gentle: these <s>Parvati</s> could bear, but not anything else.

children.text: rātrivṛttam anuyoktum udyataṃ sā vibhātasamaye sakhījanam
children.translated_text: At daybreak, when her friends set out to ask about the events of the night,

children.text: nākarod apakutūhalaṃ hriyā śaṃsituṃ ca hṛdayena tatvare ||
children.translated_text: she did not satisfy their curiosity because of shame, yet in her heart she hurried to tell it.

children.text: darpaṇe ca paribhogadarśinī pṛṣṭhataḥ praṇayino niṣeduṣaḥ
children.translated_text: In a mirror showing the signs of enjoyment, when she saw behind her the reflection of her lover sitting down

children.text: prekṣya bimbam anu bimbam ātmanaḥ kāni kāni na cakāra lajjayā ||
children.translated_text: and then her own reflection after his, what various things did she not do out of bashfulness?

children.text: nīlakaṇṭhaparibhuktayauvanāṃ tāṃ vilokya jananī samāśvasat
children.translated_text: Seeing her youth enjoyed by the blue-throated one, her mother took comfort.

children.text: bhartṛvallabhatayā hi mānasīṃ mātur asyati śucaṃ vadhūjanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a young bride, by being dear to her husband, throws off the mental grief of her mother.

children.text: vāsarāṇi katicit kathañcana sthāṇunā ratam akāri cānayā
children.translated_text: For a few days, somehow, love was made by this woman with <s>Sthanu</s>.

children.text: jñātamanmatharasā śanaiḥ śanaiḥ sā mumoca ratiduḥkhaśīlatām ||
children.translated_text: Having learned the flavor of love, little by little she gave up the habit of suffering in love-play.

children.text: sasvaje priyam uronipīḍitā prārthitaṃ mukham anena nāharat
children.translated_text: Pressed against his chest, she embraced her beloved; when he asked for her face, she did not draw it away.

children.text: mekhalāpaṇayalolatāṃ gataṃ hastam asya śithilaṃ rurodha sā ||
children.translated_text: And when his hand moved restlessly to loosen her girdle, she checked it only gently.

children.text: bhāvasūcitam adṛṣṭavipriyaṃ cāṭumat kṣaṇaviyogakātaram
children.translated_text: Signaled by feeling, seeing no offence in the beloved, full of coaxing, anxious at a moment's separation,

children.text: kaiścid eva divasais tadā tayoḥ prema rūḍham itaretarāśrayam ||
children.translated_text: within only a few days their love grew firm, each depending on the other.

children.text: taṃ yathātmasadṛśaṃ varaṃ vadhūr anvarajyata varas tathaiva tām
children.translated_text: As the bride became attached to the bridegroom suited to herself, so the bridegroom became attached to her.

children.text: sāgarād anapagā hi jāhnavī so 'pi tanmukharasaikanirvṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Jahnavi</s> is not separated from the ocean, and he too found his sole delight in the flavor of her face.

children.text: śiṣyatāṃ nidhuvanopadeśinaḥ śaṅkarasya rahasi prapannayā
children.translated_text: She had entered in private into discipleship under <s>Sankara</s>, the teacher of love-sport.

children.text: śikṣitaṃ yuvatinaipuṇaṃ tayā yat tad eva gurudakṣiṇīkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: The very skill in womanhood that she learned from him she made into the teacher's fee.

children.text: daṣṭamuktam adharoṣṭham āmbikā vedanāvidhutahastapallavā
children.translated_text: <s>Ambika</s>, her hand-sprouts shaken away by pain, for a moment cooled her lower lip when it had been bitten and released

children.text: śītalena niravāpayat kṣaṇaṃ maulicandraśakalena śūlinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with the cool fragment of the moon on the trident-bearer's crest.

children.text: cumbanādalakacūrṇadūṣitaṃ śaṅkaro 'pi nayanaṃ lalāṭajam
children.translated_text: And <s>Sankara</s> too offered his forehead eye, soiled with powder from her curls during kissing,

children.text: ucchvasatkamalagandhaye dadau pārvatīvadanagandhavāhine ||
children.translated_text: to the breath from <s>Parvati</s>'s mouth, which carried the fragrance of an opening lotus.

children.text: evam indriyasukhasya vartmanaḥ sevanād anugṛhītamanmathaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, by following the path of sensual pleasure, having come under the favor of <s>Manmatha</s>,

children.text: śailarājabhavane sahomayā māsamātram avasad vṛṣadhvajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the bull-bannered lord lived for about a month with <s>Uma</s> in the palace of the mountain king.

children.text: so 'numānya himavantam ātmabhūr ātmajāvirahaduḥkhakheditam
children.translated_text: Then the self-born lord, after taking leave of <s>Himavat</s>, who was pained by grief at separation from his daughter,

children.text: tatra tatra vijahāra saṃpatann aprameyagatinā kakudmatā ||
children.translated_text: wandered here and there, alighting with the bull whose movement is immeasurable.

children.text: merum etya marudāśugokṣakaḥ pārvatīstanapuraskṛtān kṛtī
children.translated_text: Having reached <s>Meru</s>, the accomplished lord, whose windows were the wind-swift clouds, with <s>Parvati</s>'s breasts before him,

children.text: hemapallavavibhaṅgasaṃstarān anvabhūt suratamardanakṣamān ||
children.translated_text: enjoyed couches made from broken golden shoots, capable of enduring the pressure of love-play.

children.text: padmanābhacaraṇāṅkitāśmasu prāptavatsv amṛtavipruṣo navāḥ
children.translated_text: On the slopes of <s>Mandara</s>, among stones marked by the feet of <s>Padmanabha</s> and newly touched by drops of nectar,

children.text: mandarasya kaṭakeṣu cāvasat pārvatīvadanapadmaṣaṭpadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he dwelt as a bee at the lotus of <s>Parvati</s>'s face.

children.text: vāraṇadhvanitabhītayā tayā kaṇṭhasaktaghanabāhubandhanaḥ
children.translated_text: When she was frightened by the trumpeting of elephants, and his neck was fastened by the tight bond of her arms,

children.text: ekapiṅgalagirau jagadgurur nirviveśa viśadāḥ śaśiprabhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the teacher of the world enjoyed the clear moonbeams on <s>Ekapingala</s> mountain.

children.text: tasya jātu malayasthalīrate dhūtacandanalataḥ priyāklamam
children.translated_text: Once, as he delighted on the slopes of <s>Malaya</s>, the southern wind, shaking sandal creepers,

children.text: ācacāma salavaṅgakesaraś cāṭukāra iva dakṣiṇānilaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with clove filaments, sipped away his beloved's fatigue like a flatterer.

children.text: hematāmarasatāḍitapriyā tatkarāmbuvinimīlitekṣaṇā
children.translated_text: When golden lotuses struck his beloved and her eyes were closed by the water from his hands,

children.text: khe vyagāhata taraṅgiṇīm umā mīnapaṅktipunaruktamekhalā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Uma</s> plunged in the sky into the river, her girdle echoed by rows of fish.

children.text: tāṃ pulomatanayālakocitaiḥ pārijātakusumaiḥ prasādhayan
children.translated_text: Adorning her with <s>parijata</s> flowers loosened from the hair of the daughter of <s>Puloman</s>,

children.text: nandane ciram ayugmalocanaḥ saspṛhaṃ suravadhūbhir īkṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the uneven-eyed lord remained long in <s>Nandana</s>, gazed at with longing by the wives of the gods.

children.text: ity abhaumam anubhūya śaṅkaraḥ pārthivaṃ ca dayitāsakhaḥ sukham
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Shankara</s>, with his beloved as companion, having experienced superhuman joy and earthly joy too,

children.text: lohitāyati kadācid ātape gandhamādanagiriṃ vyagāhata ||
children.translated_text: once, when the sunlight was growing red, entered <s>Gandhamadana</s> mountain.

children.text: tatra kāñcanaśilātalāśrayo netragamyam avalokya bhāskaram
children.translated_text: There, resting on a slab of gold, after looking at the sun that was within range of sight,

children.text: dakṣiṇetarabhujavyapāśrayāṃ vyājahāra sahadharmacāriṇīm ||
children.translated_text: he addressed his wife in <s>dharma</s>, who was leaning upon his left arm.

children.text: padmakāntim aruṇatribhāgayoḥ saṃkramayya tava netrayor iva
children.translated_text: "Transferring, as it were, the lotus-luster into the reddish thirds of your eyes,

children.text: saṃkṣaye jagad iva prajeśvaraḥ saṃharaty ahar asāv aharpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: this lord of the day, at the day's end, gathers in the day, as <s>Prajeshvara</s> gathers in the world at dissolution.

children.text: sīkaravyatikaraṃ marīcibhir dūrayaty avanate vivasvati
children.translated_text: When the sun has bent downward, these waterfalls of your father, with his rays, drive away their spray-mingling

children.text: indracāpapariveṣaśūnyatāṃ nirjharās tava pitur vrajanty amī ||
children.translated_text: and come to be without the encircling rainbow.

children.text: daṣṭatāmarasakesarasrajoḥ krandator viparivṛttakaṇṭhayoḥ
children.translated_text: For the pair of <s>cakravaka</s> birds in the lake, whose lotus-fiber garlands have been bitten, crying with necks turned around,

children.text: nighnayoḥ sarasi cakravākayor alpam antaram analpatāṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: and striking at each other, a little interval has become no little thing.

children.text: sthānam āhnikam apāsya dantinaḥ sallakīviṭapabhaṅgavāsitam
children.translated_text: The elephants, leaving their daytime station scented by the breaking of <s>sallaki</s> branches,

children.text: ā vibhātacaraṇāya gṛhṇāte vāri vāriruhabaddhaṣaṭpadam ||
children.translated_text: take water, with bees fastened in the lotuses, until the morning wandering begins.

children.text: paśya paścimadigantalambinā nirmitaṃ mitakathe vivasvatā
children.translated_text: Look, O sparing speaker: by the sun hanging on the edge of the western quarter,

children.text: dīrghayā pratimayā saro 'mbhasāṃ tāpanīyam iva setubandhanam ||
children.translated_text: with his long reflection in the waters of the lake, there has been made, as it were, a golden causeway.

children.text: uttaranti vinikīrya palvalaṃ gāḍhapaṅktam ativāhitātapāḥ
children.translated_text: The tusked leaders of herds of forest boars, having passed the heat of the day, are crossing a pond, scattering its thick mud,

children.text: daṃṣṭriṇo vanavarāhayūthapā daṣṭabhaṅgurabisāṅkurā iva ||
children.translated_text: as if they were lotus-root sprouts made brittle by being bitten.

children.text: eṣa vṛkṣaśikhare kṛtāspado jātarūparasagauramaṇḍalaḥ
children.translated_text: This peacock, having made its perch on the top of a tree, its circular body pale like the juice of gold,

children.text: hīyamānam ahar atyayātapaṃ pīvaroru pibatīva barhiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seems, O full-thighed one, to drink the declining heat of the day, the late sunlight.

children.text: pūrvabhāgatimirapravṛttibhir vyaktapaṅkam iva jātam ekataḥ
children.translated_text: With the onset of darkness in the eastern part, the sky has become, on one side, like a lake whose mud is visible,

children.text: khaṃ hṛtātapajalaṃ vivasvatā bhāti kiṃcid iva śeṣavat saraḥ ||
children.translated_text: its water of sunlight drawn away by the sun, shining as though with something remaining.

children.text: āviśadbhir uṭajāṅgaṇaṃ mṛgair mūlasekasarasaiś ca vṛkṣakaiḥ
children.translated_text: With deer entering the hut courtyards, with small trees wet from watering at their roots,

children.text: āśramāḥ praviśadagnidhenavo bibhrati śriyam udīritāgnayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with their sacred fires kindled as the fire-cows enter, the hermitages bear a new beauty.

children.text: baddhakośam api tiṣṭhati kṣaṇaṃ sāvaśeṣavivaraṃ kuśeśayam
children.translated_text: Even when the lotus stands with its cup closed, for a moment it leaves an opening still remaining,

children.text: ṣaṭpadāya vasatiṃ grahīṣyate prītipūrvam iva dātum antaram ||
children.translated_text: as if, out of affection, to give a space to the bee that will take it as a dwelling.

children.text: dūramagraparimeyaraśminā vāruṇī dig aruṇena bhānunā
children.translated_text: The western quarter, colored red by the sun whose rays can be measured only at their tips in the distance,

children.text: bhāti kesaravateva maṇḍitā bandhujīvatilakena kanyakā ||
children.translated_text: shines like a maiden adorned with a <s>bandhujiva</s> tilaka rich in filaments.

children.text: sāmabhiḥ sahacarāḥ sahasraśaḥ syandanāśvahṛdayaṅgamasvaraiḥ
children.translated_text: His thousands of companions, with <s>saman</s> chants whose tones delight the hearts of the chariot-horses,

children.text: bhānum agniparikīrṇatejasaṃ saṃstuvanti kiraṇoṣmapāyinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: praise the sun, whose splendor is spread around by fire, while they drink the heat of his rays.

children.text: so 'yam ānataśirodharair hayaiḥ karṇacāmaravighaṭṭitekṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: This sun, with horses whose necks are bowed and whose eyes are brushed by ear-chowries,

children.text: astam eti yugabhugnakesaraiḥ saṃnidhāya divasaṃ mahodadhau ||
children.translated_text: sets, after depositing the day in the great ocean, their manes bent by the yoke.

children.text: khaṃ prasuptam iva saṃsthite ravau tejaso mahata īdṛśī gatiḥ
children.translated_text: When the sun has come to rest, the sky seems asleep. Such is the course of great brilliance:

children.text: tat prakāśayati yāvad udgataṃ mīlanāya khalu tāvataś cyutam ||
children.translated_text: only so long as it has risen does it illumine; for when it has fallen, it is only for closing.

children.text: saṃdhyayāpy anugataṃ raver vapur vandyam astaśikhare samarpitam
children.translated_text: The body of the sun, followed even by twilight and placed in worship upon the peak of setting,

children.text: yena pūrvam udaye puraskṛtā nānuyāsyati kathaṃ tam āpadi ||
children.translated_text: was honored by her before at his rising; how would she not follow him in distress?

children.text: raktapītakapiśāḥ payomucāṃ koṭayaḥ kuṭilakeśi bhānty amūḥ
children.translated_text: O curly-haired one, those edges of the clouds, red, yellow, and tawny, are shining,

children.text: drakṣyasi tvam iti saṃdhyayānayā vartikābhir iva sādhumaṇḍitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as if well adorned by this twilight with paintbrushes, saying, 'You shall see them.'

children.text: siṃhakesarasaṭāsu bhūbhṛtāṃ pallavaprasaviṣu drumeṣu ca
children.translated_text: On the lion-mane fringes of the mountains, on trees producing new shoots,

children.text: paśya dhātuśikhareṣu bhānunā saṃvibhaktam iva sāṃdhyam ātapam ||
children.translated_text: and on mineral peaks, see how the evening sunlight has been distributed by the sun.

children.text: adrirājatanaye tapasvinaḥ pāvanāmbuvihitāñjalikriyāḥ
children.translated_text: O daughter of the mountain king, these ascetics, their joined-hand rite performed with purifying water,

children.text: brahma gūḍham abhisaṃdhyam ādṛtāḥ śuddhaye vidhivido gṛṇanty amī ||
children.translated_text: knowing the proper rule and intent on purification, respectfully recite the hidden <s>brahman</s> at twilight.

children.text: tan muhūrttam anumantum arhasi prastutāya niyamāya mām api
children.translated_text: Therefore you should allow me, too, for a moment, to observe the rule that has begun.

children.text: tvāṃ vinodanipuṇaḥ sakhījano valguvādini vinodayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Your circle of friends, skilled in diversion, O sweet-speaking one, will entertain you."

children.text: nirvibhujya daśanacchadaṃ tato vāci bhartur avadhīraṇāparā
children.translated_text: Then, pressing her lip-cover with her teeth and intent on slighting her husband's speech,

children.text: śailarājatanayā samīpagām ālalāpa vijayām ahetukam ||
children.translated_text: the daughter of the mountain king spoke, without cause, to <s>Vijaya</s>, who was standing nearby.

children.text: īśvaro 'pi divasātyayocitaṃ mantrapūrvam anutasthivān vidhim
children.translated_text: The lord too performed, with mantras, the rite proper to the passing of the day;

children.text: pārvatīm avacanām asūyayā pratyupetya punar āha sasmitam ||
children.translated_text: then, approaching <s>Parvati</s>, who was silent from jealousy, he spoke again with a smile.

children.text: muñca kopam animittakopane saṃdhyayā praṇamito 'smi nānyayā
children.translated_text: "Give up your anger, you who are angry without cause. I have bowed to <s>Sandhya</s>, not to another woman.

children.text: kiṃ na vetsi sahadharmacāriṇaṃ cakravākasamavṛttim ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Do you not know that I, your husband in <s>dharma</s>, have the same way of life as the <s>cakravaka</s> bird?

children.text: nirmiteṣu pitṛṣu svayaṃbhuvā yā tanuḥ sutanu pūrvam ujjhitā
children.translated_text: O slender one, that body which was first abandoned by <s>Svayambhu</s> when the Fathers were created,

children.text: seyam astam udayaṃ ca sevate tena mānini mamātra gauravam ||
children.translated_text: this same one attends upon setting and rising; therefore, proud lady, my reverence here is for that.

children.text: tām imāṃ timiravṛddhipīḍitāṃ śailarājatanaye 'dhunā sthitām
children.translated_text: O daughter of the mountain king, now look at this twilight standing oppressed by the growth of darkness,

children.text: ekatas taṭatamālamālinīṃ paśya dhāturasanimnagām iva ||
children.translated_text: bordered on one side by a row of <s>tamala</s> trees along the bank, like a river whose current is full of minerals.

children.text: sāndhyam astamitaśeṣam ātapaṃ raktalekham aparā bibharti dik
children.translated_text: The western quarter bears the evening sunlight remaining after sunset as a red streak,

children.text: sāṃparāyavasudhā saśoṇitaṃ maṇḍalāgram iva tiryagujjhitam ||
children.translated_text: like the blood-stained edge of a disk hurled sideways upon the battlefield earth of the next world.

children.text: yāminīdivasasandhisambhave tejasi vyavahite sumeruṇā
children.translated_text: When the light born at the junction of night and day has been blocked by <s>Sumeru</s>,

children.text: etad andhatamasaṃ niraṅkuśaṃ dikṣu dīrghanayane vijṛmbhate ||
children.translated_text: this unchecked mass of deepest darkness, O long-eyed one, expands through the quarters.

children.text: nordhvam īkṣaṇagatir na cāpy adho nābhito na purato na pṛṣṭhataḥ
children.translated_text: The range of sight goes neither upward nor downward, neither to the side nor before nor behind.

children.text: loka eṣa timiraughaveṣṭito garbhavāsa iva vartate niśi ||
children.translated_text: This world, wrapped in a flood of darkness, exists at night as if in the womb.

children.text: śuddham āvilam avasthitaṃ calaṃ vakram ārjavaguṇānvitaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Whatever is pure, turbid, fixed, moving, crooked, and endowed with the quality of straightness...

children.text: sarvam eva tamasā samīkṛtaṃ dhiṅ mahattvam asatāṃ hṛtāntaram ||
children.translated_text: Everything has indeed been made equal by darkness; shame on the greatness of the wicked, whose inner nature is hidden.

children.text: nūnam unnamati yajvanāṃ patiḥ śārvarasya tamaso niṣiddhaye
children.translated_text: Surely the lord of sacrificers is rising high to ward off the darkness of night,

children.text: puṇḍarīkamukhi pūrvadiṅmukhaṃ kaitakair iva rajobhir āvṛtam ||
children.translated_text: O lotus-faced one, while the face of the eastern quarter is covered with rays like ketaka pollen.

children.text: mandarāntaritamūrtinā niśā lakṣyate śaśabhṛtā satārakā
children.translated_text: Night, with her stars, is seen with the moon-bearer's form partly hidden by <s>Mandara</s> mountain,

children.text: tvaṃ mayā priyasakhīsamāgatā śroṣyateva vacanāni pṛṣṭhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: as if she were your dear friend who has come with me and will hear your words from behind.

children.text: ruddhanirgamanam ā dinakṣayāt pūrvadṛṣṭatanucandrikāsmitam
children.translated_text: This moon-disc, whose emergence has been held back until the end of day and whose slender smile of moonlight was seen before,

children.text: etad udgirati candramaṇḍalaṃ digrahasyam iva rātricoditam ||
children.translated_text: now pours forth, as if urged on by night, the secret of the quarters.

children.text: paśya pakvaphalinīphalatviṣā bimbalāñchitaviyatsaro'mbhasā
children.translated_text: Look: with the water of the sky-lake marked by the bimba-fruit color of ripe-fruited fruit trees,

children.text: viprakṛṣṭavivaraṃ himāṃśunā cakravākamithunaṃ viḍambyate ||
children.translated_text: a pair of cakravakas, their separation drawn far apart, is being mocked by the moon.

children.text: śakyam oṣadhipater navodayāḥ karṇapūraracanākṛte tava
children.translated_text: From the fresh rising of the lord of herbs, O you whose hands are fit to make ear-ornaments,

children.text: apragalbhayavasūcikomalāś chettum agranakhasaṃpuṭaiḥ karāḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is possible to cut off, with the cases of your front nails, rays soft as timid blades of young grass.

children.text: aṅgulībhir iva keśasaṃcayaṃ saṃnigṛhya timiraṃ marīcibhiḥ
children.translated_text: As if grasping the mass of hair that is darkness with fingers that are his rays,

children.text: kuḍmalīkṛtasarojalocanaṃ cumbatīva rajanīmukhaṃ śaśī ||
children.translated_text: the moon seems to kiss the face of night, whose lotus-eyes have been made into buds.

children.text: paśya pārvati navenduraśmibhiḥ sāmibhinnatimiraṃ nabhastalam
children.translated_text: Look, <s>Parvati</s>: with the rays of the new moon, the expanse of sky, its darkness half split,

children.text: lakṣyate dviradabhogadūṣitaṃ samprasīdad iva mānasaṃ saraḥ ||
children.translated_text: appears as if it were <s>Manasa</s> lake, clearing after being muddied by the play of elephants.

children.text: raktabhāvam apahāya candramā jāta eṣa pariśuddhamaṇḍalaḥ
children.translated_text: Having abandoned its reddish condition, the moon has now become a disc entirely pure.

children.text: vikriyā na khalu kāladoṣajā nirmalaprakṛtiṣu sthirodayā ||
children.translated_text: A change born from the fault of time is not lasting in those whose nature is stainless.

children.text: unnateṣu śaśinaḥ prabhā sthitā nimnasaṃśrayaparaṃ niśātamaḥ
children.translated_text: The moon's radiance rests upon high places, while the darkness of night is devoted to low refuges.

children.text: nūnam ātmasadṛśī prakalpitā vedhaseha guṇadoṣayor gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely here the creator has fashioned the course of virtues and faults according to their own likeness.

children.text: candrapādajanitapravṛttibhiś candrakāntajalabindubhir giriḥ
children.translated_text: With drops of water from moonstones, set in motion by the moon's rays, the mountain

children.text: mekhalātaruṣu nidritān amūn bodhayaty asamaye śikhaṇḍinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is waking these peacocks sleeping in the girdle-trees at an untimely hour.

children.text: kalpavṛkṣaśikhareṣu saṃprati prasphuradbhir iva paśya sundari
children.translated_text: Look, beautiful one: now, with rays flashing on the tops of the wish-granting trees,

children.text: hārayaṣṭigaṇanām ivāṃśubhiḥ kartum āgatakutūhalaḥ śaśī ||
children.translated_text: the moon seems to have come, eager to count the strings of pearls.

children.text: unnatāvanatabhāvavattayā candrikā satimirā girer iyam
children.translated_text: Because it has both raised and lowered forms, this moonlight of the mountain, mixed with darkness,

children.text: bhaktibhir bahuvidhābhir arpitā bhāti bhūtir iva mattadantinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: shines like ash applied in many different streaks upon a rutting elephant.

children.text: etad ucchvasitapītam aindavaṃ voḍhum akṣamam iva prabhārasam
children.translated_text: This water-lily, as if unable to bear the heavy draught of moonlight that it has breathed in and drunk,

children.text: muktaṣaṭpadavirāvam añjasā bhidyate kumudam ā nibandhanāt ||
children.translated_text: bursts at once from its fastening, with the humming of bees released.

children.text: paśya kalpatarulambi śuddhayā jyotsnayā janitarūpasaṃśayam
children.translated_text: Look, fierce lady: by the pure moonlight, the garment hanging from the wish-tree is made doubtful in form,

children.text: mārute calati caṇḍi kevalaṃ vyajyate viparivṛttam aṃśukam ||
children.translated_text: and only when the wind moves is it revealed as a turned-over cloth.

children.text: śakyam aṅgulibhir uddhṛtair adhaḥ śākhināṃ patitapuṣpapeśalaiḥ
children.translated_text: With your raised fingers, using these fragments of moonlight fallen down from the trees, tender as fallen flowers,

children.text: patrajarjaraśaśiprabhālavair ebhir utkacayituṃ tavālakān ||
children.translated_text: it would be possible to dress your curls, as if with leaf-worn pieces of lunar radiance.

children.text: eṣa cārumukhi yogatārayā yujyate taralabimbayā śaśī
children.translated_text: This moon, O lovely-faced one, is joined with the unsteady image of the conjunction-star,

children.text: sādhvasād upagataprakampayā kanyayeva navadīkṣayā varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like a bridegroom with a newly consecrated maiden who trembles because of timidity.

children.text: pākabhinnaśarakāṇḍagaurayor ullasatpratikṛtiprasannayoḥ
children.translated_text: On your two cheek-lines, pale like split, ripe reed-stalks and bright with clear, shining reflections,

children.text: rohatīva tava gaṇḍalekhayoś candrabimbanihitākṣṇi candrikā ||
children.translated_text: the moonlight seems to rise, while your eye is fixed on the moon's disc.

children.text: lohitārkamaṇibhājanārpitaṃ kalpavṛkṣamadhu bibhratī svayam
children.translated_text: Bearing in her own hands the honey of the wish-tree, placed in a vessel of red sun-stone,

children.text: tvām iyaṃ sthitimatīm upasthitā gandhamādanavanādhidevatā ||
children.translated_text: this presiding goddess of the <s>Gandhamadana</s> forest has come before you, who are steadfast.

children.text: ārdrakesarasugandhi te mukhaṃ mattaraktanayanaṃ svabhāvataḥ
children.translated_text: Your face is fragrant with moist filaments, and your eyes are naturally intoxicated and red.

children.text: atra labdhavasatir guṇāntaraṃ kiṃ vilāsini madaḥ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Since intoxication has found its dwelling here, O playful one, what further quality will it produce?

children.text: mānyabhaktir athavā sakhījanaḥ sevyatām idam anaṅgadīpanam
children.translated_text: Or else, let this friend, respectfully devoted, be served; this drink kindles <s>Ananga</s>.

children.text: ity udāram abhidhāya śaṅkaras tām apāyayata pānam ambikām ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus nobly, <s>Sankara</s> made <s>Ambika</s> drink the liquor.

children.text: pārvatī tadupayogasambhavāṃ vikriyām api satāṃ manoharām
children.translated_text: <s>Parvati</s>, with even the change produced by its use charming among good people,

children.text: apratarkyavidhiyoganirmitām āmrateva sahakāratāṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: attained a condition like that of a mango tree brought to fruition by an inscrutable conjunction of fate.

children.text: tatkṣaṇaṃ viparivartitahriyor neṣyatoḥ śayanam iddharāgayoḥ
children.translated_text: At that moment, when shame had turned away and the two, kindled with passion, wished to go to the bed,

children.text: sā babhūva vaśavartinī dvayoḥ śūlinaḥ suvadanā madasya ca ||
children.translated_text: the lovely-faced woman came under the control of both the trident-bearer and intoxication.

children.text: ghūrṇamānanayanaṃ skhalatkathaṃ svedibindumad akāraṇasmitam
children.translated_text: With eyes rolling, speech faltering, drops of sweat appearing, and a causeless smile,

children.text: ānanena na tu tāvad īśvaraś cakṣuṣā ciram umāmukhaṃ papau ||
children.translated_text: the lord drank in <s>Uma</s>'s face for a long time with his eye, but not yet with his mouth.

children.text: tāṃ vilambitapanīyamekhalām udvahañ jaghanabhāradurvahām
children.translated_text: Carrying her, whose girdle was loosened and hanging and who was hard to carry because of the weight of her hips,

children.text: dhyānasaṃbhṛtavibhūtir īśvaraḥ prāviśan maṇiśilāgṛhaṃ rahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord, whose power had been gathered through meditation, entered a jeweled rock chamber in private.

children.text: tatra haṃsadhavalottaracchadaṃ jāhnavīpulinacārudarśanam
children.translated_text: There, on a bed with coverlets white as swans, lovely to see as a sandbank of <s>Jahnavi</s>,

children.text: adhyaśeta śayanaṃ priyāsakhaḥ śāradābhram iva rohiṇīpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the friend of his beloved lay down, like the lord of <s>Rohini</s> upon an autumn cloud.

children.text: kliṣṭakeśam avaluptacandanaṃ vyatyayārpitanakhaṃ samatsaram
children.translated_text: Her hair was disheveled, her sandal paste rubbed away, nail-marks placed irregularly, and her jealousy aroused;

children.text: tasya tacchiduramekhalāguṇaṃ pārvatīratam abhūn na tṛptaye ||
children.translated_text: that love-play of <s>Parvati</s> with him, with its girdle-string broken, was not enough for satisfaction.

children.text: kevalaṃ priyatamādayālunā jyotiṣām avanatāsu paṅktiṣu
children.translated_text: Only, when the rows of stars had bent downward, he, compassionate toward his beloved,

children.text: tena tatparigṛhītavakṣasā netramīlanakutūhalaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: with her breast held in his embrace, created merely a curiosity for closing the eyes.

children.text: sa vyabudhyata budhastavocitaḥ śatakumbhakamalākaraiḥ samam
children.translated_text: That wise one, fit to be praised by the learned, awoke at dawn along with the golden lotuses,

children.text: mūrcchanāparigṛhītakaiśikaiḥ kinnarair uṣasi gītamaṅgalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while kinnaras, whose <s>kaisiki</s> mode was seized by a swoon-like softness, sang auspicious songs.

children.text: tau kṣaṇaṃ śithilitopagūhanau dampatī calitamānasormayaḥ
children.translated_text: For a moment, when their embrace had slackened, the minds of the two spouses stirred like waves,

children.text: padmabhedapiśunāḥ siṣevire gandhamādanavanāntamārutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the breezes from the forest-edge of <s>Gandhamadana</s>, betraying the opening of lotuses, attended them.

children.text: ūrumūlanakhamārgarājibhis tatkṣaṇaṃ hṛtavilocano haraḥ
children.translated_text: At that moment <s>Hara</s>, his eyes stolen by the rows of nail-tracks at the roots of her thighs,

children.text: vāsasaḥ praśithilasya saṃyamaṃ kurvatīṃ priyatamām avārayat ||
children.translated_text: stopped his beloved as she was fastening the restraint of her loosened garment.

children.text: sa prajāgarakaṣāyalocanaṃ gāḍhadantapadatāḍitādharam
children.translated_text: Passionately, he delighted in seeing his beloved's face: its eyes reddened by wakefulness, its lower lip struck hard by tooth-marks,

children.text: ākulālakam araṃsta rāgavān prekṣya bhinnatilakaṃ priyāmukham ||
children.translated_text: its curls disordered, and its tilaka broken.

children.text: tena bhaṅgiviṣamottaracchadaṃ madhyapiṇḍitavisūtramekhalam
children.translated_text: Because of him, though spotless, the bed was not abandoned at the end of night: its upper cover was uneven with folds, its girdle-strings were gathered and broken at the middle,

children.text: nirmale 'pi śayanaṃ niśātyaye nojjhitaṃ caraṇarāgalāñchitam ||
children.translated_text: and it was marked with the red lac of her feet.

children.text: sa priyāmukharasaṃ divāniśaṃ harṣavṛddhijananaṃ siṣeviṣuḥ
children.translated_text: Wishing to enjoy day and night the nectar of his beloved's face, which brought about the increase of his joy,

children.text: darśanapraṇayinām adṛśyatām ājagāma vijayānivedanāt ||
children.translated_text: he became invisible to those who desired an audience, on the pretext of announcing victory.

children.text: samadivasaniśīthaṃ saṅginas tatra śambhoḥ śatam agamad ṛtūnāṃ sāgram ekā niśeva
children.translated_text: There, for <s>Sambhu</s> joined with her, a hundred seasons, with more besides, passed with day and midnight equal, like a single night.

children.text: na tu suratasukheṣu chinnatṛṣṇo babhūva jvalana iva samudrāntargatas tajjaleṣu ||
children.translated_text: Yet he did not become one whose thirst was cut off in the pleasures of love, like fire submerged in the ocean toward those waters.
